Optimal quantum discrimination at Liouvillian exceptional points

Central to non-Hermitian sensing is the question of whether exceptional points (EPs) can make weak perturbations easier to detect. We show that despite enhanced spectral response, in finite-dimensional Lindblad systems with a unique stationary state and a nonzero relaxation gap, EPs offer no fundamental advantage in how the observation time required for reliable detection of a weak perturbation scales with the perturbation strength. We nevertheless demonstrate that by selectively choosing perturbations that enhance the quantum Fisher information rate, EPs can shorten the observation time needed to reach a predefined detection accuracy relative to a comparable non-EP reference at the same decay rate. As an illustration, we show using an optomechanical model at an EP that we can detect a weak force through the cavity output at the same reliability in less time than a non-EP reference. Our results establish fundamental limits on perturbation detection at EPs and can guide the design of faster non-Hermitian sensors based on optomechanical resonators, superconducting qubits, and trapped ions.
Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities

We prove a new functional inequality for uniformly log-concave measures, stronger than the Poincaré inequality. This new inequality bounds the variance of differences of convex functions and is motivated by the stability theory of optimal transport: for a fixed uniformly log-concave source measure, it provides a sharp stability bound for Brenier potentials with respect to variations of the target measure. Applying this inequality to Gaussian measures, we recover the fact that the Bures-Wasserstein distance between two positive semidefinite matrices is equivalent to the Frobenius distance between their square roots. Our proofs hinge upon linearization arguments for the Monge-Ampère equation governing the quadratic optimal transport problem.
Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity

We construct two distinct solutions of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation with the same initial vorticity in $\bigcap_{1\le p<\infty}L^p(\mathbb R^2)$. The vorticities are compactly supported in space and have mean zero, so the corresponding velocities have finite energy. The nonuniqueness mechanism is a cascade of transitions in quadrupole dynamics across infinitely many scales.

We introduce the $(m,p,q)$-Lefschetz property for $(1,1)$-type endomorphisms of Hodge--Lefschetz modules, providing a framework for studying nef $(1,1)$-classes and characteristic classes of nef vector bundles on compact Kähler manifolds. Under a Hall--Rado type condition on nef twisted vector bundles, we prove Hodge--Riemann relations for products of top Chern classes and, in suitable bidegrees, for products of derived Schur classes. For products of nef $(1,1)$-classes, we show furthermore that the Hall--Rado type condition is equivalent to simultaneous Hodge--Riemann relations. Our proofs build on the purity theorem and descent lemma of Cattani, Kaplan, and Schmid. We extend the descent lemma to Schur classes of nef vector bundles. We also establish formal analogs for projective bundle modules over Hodge--Lefschetz modules, with applications to tautological classes and descent on matroid Chow rings.
MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
Athanasios Glentis; Dawei Li; Mingyi Hong

Weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in language model pretraining, yet a unified understanding of why such control helps and how much is needed remains incomplete. We analyze norm control in Muon over the entire training trajectory using the \emph{accumulated effective learning rate}, $C_T=\sum_{t<T}η_t/\|W_t\|_F$, where $η_t$ is the nominal learning rate and $η_t/\|W_t\|_F$ is the effective learning rate relative to the weight norm. For bounded update directions, accumulation over any training interval bounds relative weight displacement. We show that vanilla Muon can accumulate only logarithmically, potentially limiting exploration and helping explain its slower empirical progress, whereas MuonW and MuonH guarantee at least linear accumulation under the stated conditions. Going beyond bounded-norm control, we show that sufficiently slow norm growth guarantees faster accumulation than the logarithmic worst case, opening up less restrictive optimizer designs.
 Based on this insight, we propose MuonGS, which uses Gram--Schmidt (GS) projection to remove the radial component of each Muon update without fixing the weight norm. With bounded update directions and a constant nominal learning rate, we prove that the weight norm grows at most proportionally to $\sqrt{t}$ after $t$ steps. Consequently, MuonGS guarantees $C_T=Ω(\sqrt{T})$, with accumulation sustained even in later training. Further, for smooth scale-invariant objectives we establish its $O(T^{-1/2})$ stationarity guarantee. In pretraining experiments with 160M- and 400M-parameter dense models as well as a 135M active- and 1B total- parameter MoE model, MuonGS achieves lower validation perplexity than MuonH at long training horizons. In particular, for the dense model it achieves an estimated token-equivalent speedup up to about $15\%$ at matched validation loss to MuonH.
Applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles: ODEs, PDEs, integer and difference equations
E. Petrov; R. Salimov; R. Taranets

Mappings contracting perimeters of triangles are Banach contractions whenever every point of the underlying metric space is an accumulation point. Consequently, applying the perimeter-contraction theorem on a complete metric space without isolated points yields an existence result already covered by Banach's fixed point theorem. This observation applies, in particular, to operators associated with differential and integral equations acting on standard nontrivial function spaces, such as spaces of continuous functions $C[a,b]$, Lebesgue spaces $L_p$, and Sobolev spaces $W^{k,p}$, equipped with their usual norm metrics. Thus, applications extending beyond Banach's theorem for the same operator and metric require a complete invariant domain containing some number of isolated points. Such a domain may be a closed subset of a standard function space, despite the absence of isolated points in the ambient space. The main goal of this paper is to illustrate applications of the fixed point theorem for mappings contracting perimeters of triangles in settings where the associated operators are not Banach contractions. The differential-equation examples admit interpretations as stylized models combining continuous evolution, nonlocal measurement, and quantized feedback. The integer and difference-equation examples illustrate the effects of rounding on equilibria and periodic responses.
Algebraic fiberings of right-angled Coxeter groups on bipartite cone graphs

We study systems of moves and states in the sense of [JNW21] on certain bipartite graphs, and the associated homomorphisms from the commutator subgroups of right-angled Coxeter groups to $\mathbb Z$. We give examples of right-angled Coxeter groups whose graphs do not satisfy the legal system criterion, but contain finite index right-angled Coxeter subgroups whose graphs admit legal systems. We also provide a family of examples of graphs without legal systems, where no sequence of the considered graph operations yields a graph with a legal system. Moreover, we show that for a bipartite graph and an orbit of non-empty states under the bipartite system of moves, the associated homomorphism from the commutator subgroup of the right-angled Coxeter group to $\mathbb Z$ has finitely generated kernel if and only if the system is legal.
Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP I: The shock region

We investigate the role of asymmetry in the stationary measures of integrable probabilistic models with boundary interactions. This paper is the first in a series of three focusing on the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The stationary measure of open ASEP admits a two-layer Gibbs representation in which a correction term, which we call the Bryc polynomial, encodes the dependence on the asymmetry parameter. We give a probabilistic interpretation of the Bryc polynomial in terms of a birth-death-type Markov chain. As an application, we obtain sharp total variation approximations of the stationary measure by Bernoulli product measures in the high- and low-density phases of the shock region. These approximations yield further applications, including moderate deviation estimates for the stationary measure of open ASEP, as well as asymptotic results for the related model of open ASEP with light particles.
Continuum thermodynamics of chemically reacting multi-temperature fluid mixtures

We develop a continuum-thermodynamic model for chemically reacting, multi-velocity and multi-temperature fluid mixtures. Partial balances of mass, momentum and total energy are closed using a single entropy density depending jointly on the constituent mass and nonkinetic internal-energy densities. Its partial derivatives determine the constituent temperatures and chemical potentials. For the chosen entropy flux and separately treated volume deformation, the strengthened entropy principle yields a weighted Euler relation constraining the partial thermodynamic pressures. We construct thermodynamically consistent constitutive relations for viscosity, heat conduction, Maxwell--Stefan momentum exchange, thermal relaxation and nonlinear reaction kinetics. The baseline model includes thermo-diffusion and its reciprocal coupling; a fully coupled reciprocal completion is given within the stated isotropic co-factor class. An alternative formulation couples chemical conversion and energy redistribution through specified elementary processes. We identify the material functions required for closure and admissible shifts of constituent energy zeros. An ionization network with resolved electronic levels yields Saha-type ionization relations and Boltzmann excitation ratios under the stated detailed-balance assumptions, recovering the Saha--Eggert relation at common temperature. Competing electron- and heavy-particle processes can maintain stationary populations while transferring energy between groups at different prescribed temperatures.
Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP II: The coexistence line

We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) on the coexistence line. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation, together with the probabilistic interpretation, established in the first paper in this series, of the associated Bryc polynomial in terms of an inhomogeneous birth--death chain. Our main result gives a sharp approximation of the stationary measure. Specifically, we identify the shock location as an explicit observable of the particle configuration and obtain optimal bounds on the total variation distance between its law and the uniform measure on the lattice. Conditional on the shock location, we approximate, in total variation distance, the joint law of the occupation variables away from the shock by Bernoulli product measures with different densities to its left and right. These approximations lead to further applications, including fluctuation limits, moderate deviation bounds for the particle density, and limits for correlation functions under the stationary measure.
Approximate Counting for Mixed $p$-Spin Glasses in Weak External Fields via Cluster Expansion

We give algorithms for approximating the partition function $Z_N$ of the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) model and finite mixed Ising $p$-spin models with $p\ge 3$. The algorithms apply at a fixed margin below the second-moment threshold $β_{\mathrm f}$ with homogeneous weak external fields $|h|\leqρ_0N^{-1/4}$, for fixed $ρ_0>0$. For any accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and failure parameter $δ\in(0,1)$, they approximate $\log Z_N$ to additive error $\varepsilon$. The number of exact operations is polynomial jointly in $N$, $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and $δ^{-1}$. The disorder variables have i.i.d symmetric distribution with unit variance. The failure probability is at most $δ$ plus an explicit disorder tail bound. This tail bound tends to zero under a finite fourth moment condition. Our approach builds on the cluster expansions of Aizenman--Lebowitz--Ruelle~\cite{ALR87} and Dey--Wu~\cites{DW23,DW26}. For higher-order mixtures, we retain hypergraphs using few vertices and evaluate their total weight deterministically through local spin averages and inclusion--exclusion. For SK, we impose cutoffs on the number of vertices of degree at least three and on the total number of edges. We estimate the retained sum using randomized color coding~\cite{AYZ95}. A lower tail control based on reverse hypercontractivity~\cite{MOS13} converts the mean-square approximation of the normalized partition function into logarithmic accuracy.
Lower- and upper-$C^2$ integrands: a structured class of functions for stochastic nonconvex optimization
Felipe Atenas; Alejandro Jofré; Pedro Pérez-Aros; David Torregrosa-Belén

We study nonconvex stochastic functions that admit a structured second-order representation, a generalization of lower- and upper-$C^2$ functions to normal integrands. Similarly to the deterministic case, lower-$C^2$ normal integrands are defined as the pointwise maxima over a compact random index set of functions that are twice-continuously differentiable in the decision variable with an integrable bounded Hessian. Our main result is a local value function characterization of this class of functions, namely, that they satisfy a local sufficient ascent property almost surely. Equivalently, they differ from a convex normal integrand by a random quadratic. The upper-$C^2$ theory follows by a change of sign, and delivers the corresponding lower envelopes, the form in which these integrands appear as second-stage value functions of stochastic programs with compact recourse. We also show that for this class integrability of the function values, of the local Lipschitz moduli, and of the minimum-norm Clarke subgradients are equivalent. We then study smooth integrands, finite lower envelopes, difference-of-convex integrands, Moreau and forward--backward envelopes, compositions with a smooth map, monotone convex compositions, and compact-recourse stochastic programs within these classes of nonconvex stochastic functions. As an application, we show that the optimistic loss of partial-label regression and the variational formulation of the conditional value-at-risk fit within this framework.

We use the method of equivariant localization to obtain a recursion for the cobordism-valued one-point psi-class intersections on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$, and hence the cobordism classes $[\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}]$. Restricting to the hyperbolic formal group law, we recover the Poincaré polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ as a special case, and obtain new formulas for Hirzebruch $χ_y$-genera of $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ twisted by tautological line bundles.

For diffusion-limited aggregation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \geq 2$, we rule out convergence in volume to bounded regions with boundary measure zero. Moreover, the number of boundary edges grows linearly. For Euclidean DLA in dimensions $2$, $3$, $8$, and $24$, we prove an analogous shape exclusion.
Diffusive-dispersive traveling waves and kinetic relations. Generic flux with multiple inflection points

We consider the broad class of scalar hyperbolic conservation laws with generic non-convex fluxes, which may thus have an arbitrary finite number of inflection points. We investigate the properties of classical and nonclassical shock waves realized as traveling-wave limits of a linear diffusive-dispersive regularization and provide a phase-plane classification beyond the case of a single inflection point. Within the speed range of the generalized Maxwell construction, our main result classifies the left outgoing profiles by their limiting equilibria. In an elementary bowtie configuration, we prove the existence of nonclassical shock profiles with arbitrarily many oscillations. For nested configurations, we order the saddle connections on each entry interval, taking account of inaccessible saddles. We show that the number of oscillations present in the non-classical shock depends on the diffusion-dispersion ratio, and tends to infinity along the elementary families of saddle connections as this ratio tends to zero. Our construction is based on a generalization of Maxwell's equal area rule, which provides us with an invariant region in the phase space for the study of diffusive-dispersive traveling waves.
Linear-quadratic mean field games with Volterra dynamics
Niccolò Fontana; Mattia Martini; Huyên Pham

We study a class of linear-quadratic mean field games in which the state of each agent follows a stochastic Volterra equation of convolution type. The resulting dynamics are non-Markovian and account for memory effects through a completely monotone kernel, while the mean field interaction enters both the drift and diffusion coefficients. Exploiting a Markovian lifting of the Volterra dynamics, which restores the Markov property at the price of moving to an infinite-dimensional state space, we characterize the optimal response of a representative agent for a given population mean through a system of Riccati equations in Banach spaces, thereby obtaining a feedback representation of the optimal control. We then study the consistency condition defining the mean field equilibrium, which reduces to a forward-backward fixed point equation for the equilibrium mean: we prove existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium on short horizons and, when the control does not act on the diffusion coefficient, on arbitrary horizons under a monotonicity condition on the interaction. Finally, we consider the corresponding finite-player game and establish a quantitative propagation of chaos result. As a consequence, the feedback control of any mean field equilibrium, when implemented by each agent on its own state, yields an $\varepsilon_N$-Nash equilibrium for the $N$-player game, with an explicit rate as the number of agents tends to infinity.
Sharp approximations for the stationary measures of the open ASEP III: The fan region

We study the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) in the fan region with general boundary rates. The stationary height fluctuations in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region are known to have limits involving Brownian excursions or meanders. We establish discrete counterparts of these limits: on intervals away from the boundaries, the joint law of the occupation variables is approximated in total variation distance by particle configurations constructed from lazy simple random walk excursions and meanders. In the high- and low-density phases of the fan region, we establish Bernoulli product approximations with errors that decay exponentially in the distance from the relevant boundary. Our methods combine refined combinatorial estimates for Motzkin paths and the matrix product ansatz in the totally asymmetric case with a Fourier-type decomposition (based on Askey--Wilson polynomials) of the change of measure for general asymmetry. In addition, in the maximal current phase and on its boundaries within the fan region, we prove moderate deviation estimates for particle counts on arbitrary sets of sites. These estimates rely on a covariance identity for an auxiliary path measure, through which total nonnegativity (of order two) of the matrices yields negative correlations.
Stationary measures of the open KPZ equation: A short proof

In this note, we give a short probabilistic proof of the two-layer Brownian representation of the stationary measure of the open Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on a finite interval with arbitrary Neumann boundary parameters, conjectured by Barraquand and Le Doussal and recently established in full generality by Dunlap, Gu and Rosati. Our starting point is Bryc's two-layer Gibbs representation of the stationary measure of the open asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) under Liggett's condition, together with our previously established probabilistic interpretation of the associated Bryc polynomials in terms of inhomogeneous birth--death Markov chains. Martingale estimates yield uniform asymptotics for these polynomials under weakly asymmetric scaling. Combined with known convergence results from open ASEP to open KPZ, these estimates recover the stationary height profile of the open KPZ equation as the first marginal of a reweighted pair of Brownian motions.
Generic tensor products are not maximal

We construct tensor products of uniform matroids which are strictly freer than their generic linear tensor products. In particular, the generic tensor product of two copies of $U_{7,9}$ is not maximal. More generally, for every $a,b\ge2$, this holds for $U_{7,a+7}$ and $U_{7,b+7}$. The construction disproves the uniform tensor-product formulation of Mason's conjecture. Its dual is a relaxation of an explicit circuit-hyperplane of a generic birigidity matroid. By the author's representability theorem, the resulting matroids are non-representable over every field. We also obtain full-rank counterexamples to the Jackson--Tanigawa hyperconnectivity conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$.
Iwahori Whittaker functions for unramified quasi-split groups
Solomon Friedberg; Claire Frechette; Henrik P. A. Gustafsson

Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected unramified quasi-split reductive group defined over a nonarchimedean local field $F$. This paper concerns the Iwahori Whittaker functions attached to the unramified principal series of $\mathbf{G}(F)$. We introduce Demazure-Whittaker operators and show that in the non-split case they generate a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters that are determined by $\mathbf{G}$. We then connect these operators to the Whittaker functions, establishing formulas for calculating all values for a basis of Iwahori Whittaker functions and giving a new proof of the Casselman-Shalika formula for the spherical Whittaker function. In doing so we build on the work for split groups of Brubaker, Bump and Licata; the new feature here is the appearance of a Hecke algebra with unequal parameters.
On $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundles on $\mathbb{P}^3$ that are small modifications of a Fano fourfold

We find necessary conditions for the projectivization of a rank two vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ to be related to a smooth Fano 4-fold by a small $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial modification (SQM). Furthermore, we fully describe the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$ when $\mathcal{E}$ is stable, with $c_1=-1$, $c_2=2$. In this case, we prove that there exists a flip from $X^+$ to $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{P}^3}(\mathcal{E})$, where $X^+$ is smooth and Fano. We also determine the birational geometry and numerical invariants of $X^+$.
Polynomial automorphisms of C^2 with the same equilibrium measure

We review the following question: when do two polynomial automorphisms of C^2 have the same maximal entropy measure? While the answer has been known for some time when both automorphisms are compositions of Hénon maps, the general case is more delicate. In this (mostly expository) note we explain how recent results in random dynamics give an almost complete solution to the question, and point out a number of related open problems.

Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Schütz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. Lewark independently gave a related local equivalence group and concordance invariant, using only the Bar-Natan deformation. In this paper, we construct $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\infty$ subgroups of Lewark's local equivalence group and the kernel of the map from our local equivalence group to Lewark's, as well as $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ direct summands of Lewark's group and this kernel, invisible to the $s$-invariants. The construction gives at least six $\mathbb{Z}$-valued concordance homomorphisms linearly independent from $s$, $τ$, and Dai--Hom--Stoffregen--Truong's invariants.
GNBG-C: A Unified and Configurable Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization
Ali Ghasemzadeh; Erfan Babakhani; Armin Khosravi; Pariya Ghasemzadeh; Yong-Hong Kuo; Seyedali Mirjalili; Amir H. Gandomi

Many real-world optimization tasks are governed not only by what should be optimized, but also by what is allowed: a solution must first satisfy physical, operational, safety, budgetary, or structural requirements before its objective value becomes meaningful. Yet benchmark design for constrained continuous optimization often treats these restrictions as fixed properties of predefined test instances. Existing generators and benchmark suites provide essential foundations for reproducible comparison, but they either focus primarily on configurable objective landscapes or expose constraint properties within limited, predefined regimes, making it difficult to ask targeted questions about constraint-induced difficulty: whether an optimizer struggles because feasible regions are small, boundaries are restrictive, variables are tightly coupled, or constraint information is poorly scaled. We introduce GNBG-C, a Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator for Constrained Continuous Optimization. The central idea is to treat the feasible region itself as a configurable object rather than as an inseparable attachment to a fixed test function. By generating controlled constraint regimes around the known GNBG global minimizer, the generator enables systematic studies in which feasibility pressure can be varied while preserving that point as a global minimizer of the constrained problem. This allows researchers to examine how optimizers discover feasibility, handle constraint pressure, and improve objective quality under diverse and controllable feasibility conditions. GNBG-C therefore provides a flexible and auditable framework for probing the strengths and weaknesses of constrained continuous optimizers under targeted forms of feasibility-side difficulty.
Every route counts, but some count more: a max-plus view of the C. elegans brain
Emma Reyner-Fuentes; Sebastian Rudolph; Carmen Peláez-Moreno; Francisco J. Valverde-Albacete

Brains do not simply add up every signal they receive: they select which routes dominate. Yet connectomes are usually analyzed with tools that sum over all paths and place neural states in Euclidean spaces, blurring the feedback circuits that may sustain internal states. Here we treat neural signaling as routing instead of diffusion and describe it with max-plus algebra, in which signals accumulate along a path and the strongest route prevails. We propose a model in which the functional connectome of Caenorhabditis elegans emerges from the time-varying combination of electrical, synaptic, monoaminergic, neuropeptidergic and hormonal layers, and analyze five networks within this framework. Each collapses onto a handful of dominant feedback loops, which recover well-characterized circuits and point to new candidates for experimental study. Unlike linear spectra, these structures keep the biological meaning of the data, and their order-based description suggests that brain states live in lattices rather than Euclidean spaces.
A cubic chromatic bound for capped graphs

An ordered graph is capped if, for any four vertices $a<b<c<d$, the edges $ac$ and $bd$ imply the edge $ad$. We prove that every nonempty capped graph $G$ satisfies $χ(G)\leq\min\{3^{ω(G)-1},18ω(G)^3\}$, where $χ(G)$ and $ω(G)$ are its chromatic number and clique number. This proves a conjecture of Davies, Krawczyk, McCarty and Walczak.
Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
Alex Cohen; Zhenhao Li; Zhongkai Tao

Let $M$ be a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface. We give a lower bound for the $L^2$ norm of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series in a compact part of the surface. This extends a result of Soundararajan [arXiv:0901.4060] to the nonarithmetic setting. The crucial components of the proof are a long-time Egorov's theorem designed for this setting, a nonlinear uncertainty principle of Cohen--Dyatlov [arXiv:2609.30261], and an application of Weyl's method for exponential sums.
Vanishing theorems for $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles

In this note, using J.-P. Demailly's $L^2$ existence theorem for possibly incomplete Kähler metrics, we establish $L^2$ estimates and vanishing theorems for a class of domains in $\mathbb P^n$ without any boundary regularity assumptions. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to M.-C. Shaw's question concerning the vanishing of the $L^2$ Dolbeault cohomology groups of projective Hartogs triangles.
No closed-form formula for Stiefel geodesics

We use differential Galois theory to prove that given two arbitrary points $X$ and $Y$ on the Stiefel manifold, there is no closed-form analytic expression for the Riemannian logarithm $\log_X Y$, the geodesic between $X$ and $Y$, or the geodesic distance between $X$ and $Y$. In other words, these cannot be expressed in terms of elementary functions of the coordinates of $X$ and $Y$; in fact, our result goes further --- even if we allow for repeated integrals of elementary functions, there is still no such expression.
Stability of attractive 3D Bose gases with repulsive three-body interactions
Arnaud Triay; François L. A. Visconti

We consider three-dimensional Bose gases with attractive two-body interactions and repulsive three-body interactions. We prove the stability of the second kind of the system for a large class of interaction potentials and scaling regimes, which includes the Gross--Pitaevskii regime for the three-body potential. In addition, we even prove the classical stability of the system for a more restrictive class of interactions and scaling regimes. The main ingredient of the proof is a bound that was derived recently in a study by the authors on the dynamics of Bose gases with three-body interactions in the Gross--Pitaevskii regime (2026).

Given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we classify $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$. The main idea of this paper is due to an LLM, and the paper was written by an LLM, under the guidance of the authors.

We give a complete list of the possible local shapes of soap films where they wet the whole wire. In rigorous terms, given a straight line $\ell \subset \mathbb R^3$, we study $2$-dimensional cones in $\mathbb R^3$ which contain $\ell$ and are Almgren minimizing with respect to $\ell$.
Weak tracial approximation and a weak Rokhlin property for C*-dynamical systems
George A. Elliott; Chun Guang Li; Zhuang Niu; Qingyun Wang

We extend results on tracial approximability of crossed products from the setting of topological dynamical systems to C*-dynamical systems. For actions of discrete amenable groups on unital C*-algebras, we introduce a weak Rokhlin property which leads to a weak tracial approximation of the crossed products by means of finite direct sums of matrix algebras over hereditary subalgebras of the original algebra. Examples are given.

Quantum field theory unifies special relativity and quantum mechanics, yet relies on externally imposed prescriptions for quantization, renormalization, and probabilistic interpretation that lack a common algebraic foundation. This work derives these features from a single principle: the finite-resolution realization of the additive group (R, +) under four consistency constraints: finite operational resolution (FR1), multiplicative linearity (FR2), phase coherence (FR3), and statistical typicality (FR4).
 The Hilbert-space formalism of quantum theory, the Born probability rule, and the Kolmogorov structure of statistical mechanics emerge as limiting projections of a common additive algebra, without additional postulates. Extending this framework to spacetime translations and their automorphisms, we recover the kinematic and dynamical structure of quantum field theory and address ultraviolet divergences through intrinsic finiteness rather than external renormalization.
 Quantization and unitarity emerge from additive symmetry, while the gravitational field is interpreted as the algebraic kernel transporting boundary information into bulk observables, without requiring an independent quantization of the metric. This framework aims to provide a unified, finite, and algebraic foundation for physical law.nite, and algebraic foundation for physical law.
Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
Tarik Aougab; Jonah Gaster; Nicholas Miller

We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. We also construct super-exponentially many (in $g$) pants decompositions with exponential volume growth for which our techniques still imply stronger upper bounds for kissing numbers. The proofs use the technology of ``stem systems'' and ``tulips'' developed by the first and second author to study $1$-systems of curves.

We prove an uncertainty principle for subsets of $\mathbb R$ under weak branching assumptions. We impose a nonlinearity condition on the phase; without it our uncertainty principle fails e.g. for arithmetic progressions. The key ingredient in the proof is Shmerkin's nonlinear projection theorem. This paper is a part of a work in progress, but it is released earlier than the rest of that paper since it is also used in a paper of Cohen-Li-Tao. It also has an overlap with our recent paper [arXiv:2609.30261]; see the end of the introduction for more details.
Essential norms of fractional Volterra-type operators

Given a radial doubling weight $μ$ on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ and $f(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \hat{f}(n)z^n\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, the fractional derivative of $f$ induced by $μ$ is
 $$
 D^μ(f)(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{\hat{f}(n)}{μ_{2n+1}}z^n,
 $$ where $μ_{2n+1}=\int_0^1 r^{2n+1}μ(r)\,dr$ are the odd moments of $μ$. The fractional integral of $f$ induced by $μ$ is $I^μ(f)(z)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty μ_{2n+1}\hat{f}(n)z^n$. We study the fractional Volterra-type operator
 $$
 V_{μ,g}(f)(z)=I^μ(f\cdot D^μ(g))(z),\quad f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}),
 $$ with symbol $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, introduced by Bellavita, Moreno, Nikolaidis and Peláez. First, we estimate the essential norm of $V_{μ,g}$ acting on $H^p$ and $A^p_α$. Later, we study the same questions for $V_{μ,g}:H^p\to H^q$ and $V_{μ,g}:A^p_α\to A^q_α$, characterizing their boundedness and compactness and estimating their essential norms for all $0<p,q<\infty$.
Reflected constraint algebras of open Carroll--Weyl null strings

We construct a classical reflected phase space for open Carroll--Weyl null strings with Dirichlet conditions at the target origin or linear mixed target gluings. The reflection-compatible constraints are differentiable, their Hamiltonian flows preserve the boundary domain, and the constraint system is weakly first class on its regular part. The induced boundary algebra extends the boundary Carrollian conformal algebra by an even weight-one Carroll--Weyl current, with normalization fixed by the reflected symplectic form. The regular local embedding count agrees with that of the closed theory. We exhibit a four-dimensional mixed sector with one canonical field pair and a separate solution family carrying a nonzero conserved target-space boost charge and a nondegenerate symplectic pullback. Smooth fixed-point reflection selects characteristic endpoints. For timelike defects with natural tangential variations and no additional boundary interactions, non-characteristic endpoints have vanishing Carroll flow. For displaced Dirichlet data, we derive the canonical affine lift and its required shift of the edge momentum by integrated bulk momentum.
The packing and covering number of trees are local
Caelan Atamanchuk; Simon Briend; Serte Donderwinkel; Elaine Herrera

For a graph, its $r$-packing number is the size of the largest $r$-separated set and its $r$-covering number is the size of the smallest $r$-net. We show that the $r$-covering number and $r$-packing number are continuous in the fringe topology on locally finite trees. This recovers convergence results by Meir and Moon for e.g. uniform binary trees, uniform plane trees, uniform Polyá trees and random recursive trees, and proves new results for many other tree models, such as size-conditioned Bienaymé trees, simply generated trees, $m$-ary search trees, the minimum spanning tree of the complete graph and preferential attachment trees. Moreover, our formulation provides an intuitive interpretation of the limiting constant, that also provides an easy route for explicit computations in the case of size-conditioned Bienaymé trees. Our method relies on the definition of a canonical minimum $r$-net, and a relation between covering numbers and packing numbers due to Meir and Moon.
Local regularity for solutions to singular and degenerate quasilinear parabolic equations

The main purpose of this paper is to prove local Hölder continuity for weak solutions to quasilinear parabolic equations of $p$-Laplace type under finite integrability assumptions on the forcing, covering the supercritical singular range and the entire degenerate regime. The key ingredient is an $L^\infty$-valued temporal Hölder estimate of the solution after any fixed positive waiting time, which is achieved by coupling a time-rescaling argument with De Giorgi iteration. We also provide counterexamples involving forcing terms with weaker spatial integrability to show that even bounded continuous solutions with compatible data may possess no positive temporal Hölder exponent. In particular, these examples establish the sharpness of the spatial integrability threshold in the degenerate case. Finally, a separate counterexample is constructed to demonstrate that the temporal Lipschitz endpoint can fail for bounded continuous forcing when it depends on time.
Constructing Data-Driven Budgeted Uncertainty Sets for Robust Optimization
Jamie Fairbrother; Marc Goerigk; Qiongyan Zeng

In robust optimization, budgeted uncertainty sets offer a popular trade-off between modeling flexibility and computational tractability. Data that is observed in practice is often discrete in nature, which creates the need for tools to construct budgeted uncertainty sets based on observed data. This paper presents a principled approach for this purpose, which ensures that any solution found through the robust problem with respect to the constructed budgeted uncertainty set offers an approximation guarantee with respect to the optimal value of the problem with discrete data. Our approach is purely based on the geometry of data and can be applied to any nominal optimization problem. We discuss the problem of evaluating budgeted uncertainty sets, and how to construct them using exact and heuristic methods. In computational experiments, we show that it is possible to construct sets with little computation time that offer guarantees that are close to optimality.
Relative distality and incidence bounds in positive characteristic

We prove Szemerédi-Trotter-type incidence bounds for algebraic relations in any field $F$ admitting a valuation with finite residue field. This includes $\mathbb F_q(t)$, $\mathbb F_q((t))$, and all finitely generated extensions of finite fields. Bays and Martin show that any algebraic $K_{d,s}$-free relation $E\subseteq F^k\times F^\ell$ admits a power-saving in the classical Zarankiewicz bound of Kővári, Sós, and Turán. Answering a question of the authors, we show that this power-saving is uniform in $F$: There is some $ε>0$ depending only on $d$ and the complexity of $E$ (and not on $F$) such that for $A\subseteq F^k$ and $B\subseteq F^\ell$, the number of edges $|E(A,B)|$ is at most $O(|A|^{1-ε}|B|^{1-\frac{1-ε}{d}}+|A|+|B|)$. For the case where $A$ is a set of points and $B$ is a set of lines in $F^2$ and $E$ is the incidence relation, we prove the explicit bound $O(|P|^{\frac{8}{9}}|L|^{\frac{5}{9}}+|P|+|L|)$. As the central ingredient of the proof, we introduce the model-theoretic notion of distality relative to a definable set. We begin developing this notion and prove that the theory of algebraically closed valued fields is distal relative to the residue field. An application of a result of Chernikov, Peterzil, and Starchenko, based on work of Chernikov, Galvin, and Starchenko, yields our incidence bounds.
Global Hölder solvability for parabolic equations with interior Morrey data

We prove global Hölder solvability for uniformly parabolic divergence-form equations with locally finite measure data under an interior Morrey growth condition and a capacity density condition on the spatial domain. The parabolic distance to the initial and lateral boundary is assumed bounded on the source support. For nonnegative data, we establish necessity results that demonstrate the sharpness of the growth and domain assumptions. We also derive estimates for divergence forcing, prove solvability for equations with lower-order terms, and obtain convergence rates in periodic homogenization.
Fisher Completions and Statistical Regularization of Wrapped Gaussian Families

We determine the intrinsic Fisher completion of the full-covariance wrapped Gaussian family on a fixed torus and relate its geometry to uniform estimation. The completion is homeomorphic to the total-variation closure. Every added law is, in suitable integer torus coordinates, a product of a uniform law and a lower-dimensional wrapped Gaussian. All these densities are positive and real analytic, but in dimension at least two no added point has a compact neighborhood. Small balls remain contractible, and explicit minimizing geodesics pass through added points. In dimension at least two, every fixed Fisher neighborhood of an added point has a positive minimax risk at every sample size. For subfamilies with a common positive lower bound on the variance in every nonzero integer direction, we prove that compactness of the completed closure is equivalent to uniform consistency in either $L^1$ or completed-Fisher loss. Equivalently, the Fourier moments must decay uniformly over the subfamily. A fixed covariance floor guarantees this condition without an upper covariance bound and gives $L^1$ risk at most $C_{\varepsilon,d}n^{-1/2}\{\log(n+1)\}^{d/4}$. A common-phase example illustrates how partially uniform limits can retain relative-phase information while remaining uniformly estimable.
The Minimum Subpacketization of Reed-Solomon Codes with Linear Repair Achieving the Cut-Set Bound
Weijun Fang; Jing Qiu; Shu-Tao Xia; Fang-Wei Fu

In this paper, we study the minimum subpacketization of $(n,k)$ Reed-Solomon (RS) codes over $\mathbb{F}_{q^\ell}$ admitting cut-set-optimal exact $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear repair of every coordinate from any $d$ helpers. For $3\le k<d\le n-1$, write $s=d+1-k$ and denote this minimum by $\ell_{min}(n,k,d;q)$. Using divisibility and relative-degree constraints on cross-ratio fields of evaluation sets, we establish $\ell_{min}(n,k,d;q)\ge sG_s(d+1)$, where $G_s(m)$ is the minimum product of $m$ pairwise coprime integers, each at least $s$. Let $Δ_s(n,d)$ be the minimum of $lcm(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ over positive integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfying $lcm(a_j:j\in J\cup\{i\})\ge s~lcm(a_j:j\in J)$ for every $d$-subset $J\subseteq[n]$ and every $i\in[n]\setminus J$. We construct RS codes with subpacketization $sΔ_s(n,d)$ and further prove that $\ell_{min}(n,k,d;q)=sΔ_s(n,d)=sG_s(n)$ whenever $d(d+2)\geq 4(n+1)$, for every prime power $q$. In particular, this determines the minimum subpacketization in the full-helper case $d=n-1$, resolving the corresponding exact linear-repair case of Open Problem 20 posed by Ramkumar et al. in their survey on codes for distributed storage. We further give a finite formula for $G_s(n)$ and determine the exact threshold for its closed-form expression in terms of the first $n$ primes. For fixed $k$ and $d$, we prove $\log\ell_{min}(n,k,d;q)= Θ_{k,d}(\log n\log\log n)$ as $n\to\infty$, using divisor-function estimates and cover-free families. An affine-plane construction shows that $Δ_s(n,d)<G_s(n)$ for some parameters, so $sG_s(n)$ is not a universal formula. We conjecture that $\ell_{min}(n,k,d;q)=sΔ_s(n,d)$ for every prime power $q$ and all $3\le k<d\le n-1$.
Approaching Optimal Scaling of Queue Size for an Input-Queued Switch

We study the scaling of the expected total queue length in an $n\times n$ input-queued switch. It has been conjectured that the optimal scaling is $O(n/(1-ρ))$, up to logarithmic factors, where $ρ$ is the system load. This conjecture has been established in the traditional heavy-traffic regime and in certain sub-regimes of the large-system regime. But it remains unresolved over a wide range of load scalings in the large-system regime. In this paper, we develop a family of scheduling policies parameterized by a positive integer $k\ge 2$. We show that under uniform traffic, our policy achieves an expected total queue length of $O\bigl({n\log\max\{n,1/(1-ρ)\}}\big/{(1-ρ)^{2^k/(2^k-1)}}\bigr)$, as long as $ρ\to 1$ in the large-system regime. As $k$ increases, the exponent $2^k/(2^k-1)$ approaches $1$, bringing our bound arbitrarily close to the conjectured scaling. The expected amortized scheduling cost of the policy is $O(n^3 k)$ per time slot. Our policy is of a batching type, with a novel recursive design that allows an arbitrary number of batching levels. This design principle may also be useful for other scheduling problems in which combinatorial constraints restrict which jobs can be served simultaneously.
Statistical Uniformization of Surfaces by Heat-Kernel Fisher Information

A Brownian particle observed at time $t$ carries information about where it started. On a closed surface this makes the surface itself a statistical model, whose Fisher information pulls back to a heat-smoothed metric $h_t=2tJ_t$; its volume $V_t$ is a normalized Jeffreys volume, and $\log(V_t/2t)$ is the model-dependent constant in Rissanen's minimum-description-length complexity. We ask whether maximizing this statistical size among metrics of fixed area in a conformal class recovers the uniformizing metric. First, $9(A-2πχt-V_t)/t^2$ converges to the curvature energy $\int K^2\,dA$ (the Calabi energy up to a topological constant), uniformly on classes of bounded geometry; hence, within a fixed-area conformal class of bounded geometry containing the uniformizer, approximate maximizers of $V_t$ converge to the constant-curvature metric (on the sphere, to the round metrics). Second, near every flat torus we prove a sharp finite-scale version: for small perturbations whose oscillations are resolved by the diffusion, $t|k|^2\leθ<τ_*$, the flat-subtracted defect is comparable to $\|Δf\|_2^2$, uniformly in the frequency cutoff and over noncollapsing lattices. The explicit threshold $τ_*=4.408\ldots$ is optimal, and it is exactly the observation time at which the information about one curvature mode is maximal. Third, the flat structure is seen only at an exponential scale: the volume loss of a flat torus measures the ambiguity of winding and is comparable to $t^{-1/2}e^{-\operatorname{sys}^2/(16t)}$, which selects the hexagonal lattice as $t\to0$ but not at all times.
Model-based clustering of diffusion processes with constant volatility coefficients using high-frequency data

This paper considers model-based clustering of diffusion processes using high-frequency data. We formulate a finite mixture model for diffusion processes and develop a clustering method based on their constant diffusion coefficients. Using a quasi-likelihood, we propose estimators of the number of clusters, the diffusion coefficients and the cluster labels, and establish their consistency and the asymptotic normality of the diffusion coefficient estimators under high-frequency asymptotics with the number of observed processes fixed. Simulation studies are conducted to investigate the finite-sample performance of the proposed method.

For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=τ(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $ν_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p\nmid n$ for every prime $p$. We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. We call $n$ \emph{matchable} if $D(n)$ admits a coprime matching with the primitive arithmetic progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$. The general criterion implies that $n$ is matchable if and only if $\lfloor N/p\rfloor\le N/(ν_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We explicitly classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. A Vandermonde determinant gives the required matchings under bounds on the prime exponents, while a partition into shorter progressions handles the remaining cases.
Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification

For each time $t$, the regression function $m_t(x)=E[Y_t\mid X_t=x]$ of an outcome on contemporaneous covariates can be regarded as a field on covariate space. We study how this field evolves when the covariates of individual units move as a diffusion and the outcome attached to each unit changes according to its own dynamics. Under mild regularity we show that $m_t$ satisfies a second-order evolution equation whose diffusion term is $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(Σ\nabla^2 m_t)$, the trace of the Hessian of the regression function weighted by the instantaneous covariance $Σ$ of the covariate increments, whose transport term is the drift of the time-reversed covariate process, and whose source term is the conditional mean rate of change of the outcome. The equation is a regression-theoretic reading of a classical transport law, and it yields a Feynman-Kac representation of $m_t$ along reversed covariate paths. We connect the Hessian appearing in the equation to the Hessian estimated by quadratic regression (under Gaussian design the best quadratic approximation has Hessian $E[\nabla^2 m(X)]$ exactly) and to the leading bias of kernel smoothers. For binary outcomes governed by bistable replicator dynamics with imitation among units with similar covariates, the closed equation is of Nagumo type, its planar travelling fronts are exactly logistic in $(x,t)$, and a single logistic regression of the outcome on covariates and time identifies the ratio of diffusion to reaction and the direction of invasion. We discuss identification under panel versus repeated cross-sectional designs and a two-stage estimation strategy, and we illustrate the results with simulations.
Lojasiewicz Estimates for a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model

We investigate the structure of degree $1$ minimisers of a Baby-Skyrme energy of maps $u:Σ\to S^2$ regularised by a Sacks-Uhlenbeck perturbation, and we establish quantitative convergence rates to a simple bubble tree consisting of a single degree $1$ bubble and a constant base map.
Bounds for B-coloring planar and outerplanar graphs
Ryan R. Martin; Miklós Ruszinkó; Gábor N. Sárközy

A proper coloring of the edges of a graph is one in which every $K_{1,2}$ is totally multicolored. A B-coloring is a coloring of the edges of $G$ in which every $K_{1,2}$ and every $K_{2,2}$ is totally multicolored.
 In this paper, we improve two results by the authors and Gyárfás. The first shows that an outerplanar graph with maximum degree $Δ$ can be B-colored with $\max\{Δ,9\}$ colors, improving a bound of $Δ+1$ and this is best possible up to the constant 9.
 The second shows that a planar graph with maximum degree $Δ$ can be B-colored with $\max\{2Δ+4,22\}$, improving a bound of $2Δ+8$.
Global minimax rates for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation

Recent work established minimax rates for pointwise estimation of the conditional average treatment effect (CATE), but the fundamental limits under global losses remained unresolved. We derive matching minimax lower and upper bounds under the $L_2$ and $L_\infty$ risks on certain covariate-density and support classes. For the lower bounds, we develop a many-fuzzy-hypotheses method that replaces each fixed alternative in a multiple-hypothesis construction with a mixture over nuisance functions that leaves its CATE unchanged. A localized product-mixture $χ^2$ bound is used to control the divergence of each resulting mixture from a common baseline, enabling multiple well-separated CATE hypotheses to be handled simultaneously. For the upper bounds, we analyze a modified local polynomial R-learner. The $L_2$ argument extends the pointwise bias--variance analysis, while the $L_\infty$ argument combines concentration inequalities for U-statistics with a continuity argument enabled by the use of a continuous kernel and additional regularity of the second-order basis. The resulting rates show that the pointwise elbow phenomenon persists globally: the $L_2$ transition threshold is unchanged, while the $L_\infty$ rate has an additional logarithmic factor and a transition threshold adjusted by $1-\log\log n/\log n$.
Recovering classical gauge geometry from quantum master constraints

Exact normalizable solutions of quantum constraints form a symplectic submanifold of the space of rays, whereas classical first-class constraints define a surface on which the symplectic form is degenerate. We ask how the degenerate directions can be recovered when quantum theory is regarded as fundamental and the constraints are imposed through a single positive master operator. For a nonnegative master function whose zero set is a Morse--Bott critical manifold, the image of the linearized Hamiltonian vector field is the symplectic orthogonal of the zero set, and coisotropy is equivalent to this linearization having square zero. The image is fixed by the zero set, but the theorem identifies it with the response of the master dynamics, which makes it accessible to quantum states. Three realizations follow. The exact quantum physical space is the opposite, rotational case of the same dichotomy. For quadratic masters, the bottom of the spectrum is $(\hbar/2)\Tr_+L$, so first-class zero sets carry no offset of order $\hbar$; within the harmonic approximation this explains the $\hbar$ versus $\hbar^2$ offsets observed in tests of the master-constraint programme. Finally, the second time derivative of the limiting covariance of a semiclassical packet, which can be determined by bounded probes, has the gauge distribution as its image. Two oscillators at fixed total energy give exact master evolution, an exact realization of this covariance shear, and the reduced symplectic limit. For the non-Abelian SL(2,$\R$) model we compute the coherent and Weyl master symbols, prove essential self-adjointness and a finite-time propagation estimate, and derive the spectral bottom $\hbar^2/2$.

If $F$ is a number field and $F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2\subset \cdots$ is a tower of Galois extensions with $\mathrm{Gal}(F_n/F)$ cyclic of order $p^n$, K. Iwasawa gave a closed formula for the growth of the $p$-part of the class number of $F_n$ whenever $n$ is large enough. We present a new proof of this formula, obtained by reinterpreting its summands in terms of Sylvester matrix rank functions on the Iwasawa algebra $Λ$ without resorting to the classification of finitely-generated $Λ$-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism.
AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
David Voderholzer; Leonard Vetter; Thomas O'Leary-Roseberry

Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as $m^3$ with the number of spectral modes $m$. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative $L^2$ error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by $31\%$ (airfoil) and $42\%$ (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.
Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles

In his global theory of one-frequency Schrödinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, this provides a nonzero-degree counterpart to Avila's characterization of uniform hyperbolicity by vanishing acceleration.
 In nonzero degree, we also characterize minimal acceleration through signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures. In the positive-degree, positive Lyapunov exponent case, the proof constructs an analytic positive connection using invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer--scattering representation. A complex-analytic construction then produces a periodic gauge. As a further consequence, for each fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected: every cocycle in this locus can be joined to the linear rotation of the same degree by a path preserving premonotonicity.
The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
Binyan Yu; Bilel Selmi; Jia Liu; Yongshun Liang

This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a Hölder and count-Hölder continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-Hölder condition is at least
 \(
 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\}
 \)
 where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$. As a consequence, non-trivial lower bounds are obtained for the Assouad dimension of the graphs of classical functions such as the Weierstrass and Takagi functions. We have also employed a unified projection solely in the direction of the $y$-axis to establish lower and upper bounds for the Assouad dimension. On this basis, we have shown that the lower bound is sharp in terms of level sets, namely the upper box dimension cannot be replaced by the Assouad dimension. This provides a partial positive answer to Question 17.11.1 posed by Fraser in~\cite{Fraser2021}, and to Question 2.2 posed by Yu in~\cite{Yu2020}.
 Building on this result, the analysis has been further extended to a broader class of Weierstrass-type functions and some self-affine functions like fractal interpolation functions. Moreover, we have discussed certain circumstances under which the Assouad dimension can reach 2 with several examples constructed. A supplementary explanation of why Brownian motion has the full Assouad dimension has also been provided based on the preceding work of Howroyd and Yu \cite{Howroyd2019}.
No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces

Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.
Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials
Dzmitry Dudko; Yusheng Luo; Runze Zhang

We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog. Combined with~\cite{BCR26}, this implies the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials, resolving a conjecture by Douady from the 1980s.
Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts

We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.
On a problem of A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov concerning $S_n$-closed subformations of a one-generated formation

Throughout this paper, all groups are finite. Let $\mathrm{form}(G)$ denote the formation generated by a group $G$. A formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is said to be $S_n$-closed if every subnormal subgroup of every group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$. A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov posed the problem of proving that $\mathrm{form}(G)$ has only finitely many $S_n$-closed subformations for every group $G$ (Problem 14.81 of the Kourovka Notebook). In this paper we propose a negative answer to this problem. We prove that for the group $G_0=(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)\times\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ of order 28800, where $C_2$ acts on $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ by an outer automorphism, the formation $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ has an infinite strictly descending chain of $S_n$-closed subformations. The main tool is a family of central-valued multilinear maps, defined for every group in $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ by its outer actions on its components; their vanishing is preserved under taking epimorphic images, subdirect products and subnormal subgroups. The members of the chain are separated by central quotients of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)^{2^d-1}\rtimes C_2^d$, $d\geq 2$. Using Burichenko's description of the lattice of subformations of $\mathrm{form}(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)$, we also prove that every non-empty $S_n$-closed subformation of $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ is generated, as an ordinary formation, by a single group, and that the set of such subformations is countably infinite. Finally, we determine the intersection of the chain and give an explicit generator of it.

This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.
Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model

We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (Σ,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^α(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_Σ (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{α+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $α\to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^α$.
A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities

Let $σ(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=σ(x_1)σ(x_3)-σ(x_2)σ(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. We show that $\mathscr{M}$ is a complete embedded minimal hypersurface with infinitely many isolated singularities, which are exactly the vertices of the regular honeycomb of $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ by $24$-cells. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $π/2$ at each singularity. The isometry group of $\mathscr{M}$ is generated by the translations of the root lattice $D_4$ and a hyperoctahedral group of order $384$ fixing the centre of a $24$-cell; it has index three in the symmetry group of the honeycomb, acts transitively on the singular points, and contains a symmetry which is not visible from the defining equation. Seen from the centre of a $24$-cell, $\mathscr{M}$ is the zero set of a theta series of a translate of the Hurwitz quaternions, which makes the whole symmetry group manifest; the sections of $\mathscr{M}$ by a family of parallel hyperplanes are triply periodic surfaces with cubic symmetry which change topology through conical points. Finally, $\mathscr{M}$ is obtained from a union of $2$-planes by attaching cones over $2$-tori, and its quotient by the lattice of periods is a compact minimal hypersurface in a flat $4$-torus with exactly three singular points and infinite Morse index; we show that its regular part is one-sided and compute its Euler characteristic and integral homology.
Mert Gürbüzbalaban; M. Hamza Rafi; Necdet Serhat Aybat; Waheed U. Bajwa

With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.
Sharp Planar Anisotropic Capillarity Outside Convex Obstacles and Two-Point Rigidity of Transported Boundary Images
Lisbeth Carrero; Alexander Quaas; Andres Zuniga

For a convex surface tension $\varphi$ and the wall-energy density $σ(n)=-λ\,\varphi(-n)$, we prove sharp capillary inequalities outside arbitrary convex planar obstacles for $-1<λ\leq0$ and every finite-perimeter competitor of finite positive volume, including non-even and crystalline tensions. Equality holds precisely for translated dilates of Wulff caps in minimum-volume directions, with the entire truncating facet resting on a flat supporting face. A uniform quantitative estimate controls component concentration, shape up to translation, and directional cap-volume excess. The proof combines exact filling, planar completion, and quantitative Wulff stability. For the transport $DΦ$, $Φ=\varphi^2/2$, the zero-adhesion boundary-image estimate characterizes centered ellipsoids among even anisotropies with $Φ\in C^3$ away from the origin and positive definite Hessian. Two-point slab tests with arbitrary boundary data suffice: their projection balances yield a cubic identity forcing $Φ$ to be quadratic. Facets and smooth perturbations provide counterexamples to the transported estimate, including failures at prescribed adhesion levels in $(-1,1)$. Strict finite deficits persist under Hausdorff perturbations of the Wulff body. The classification concerns an unrestricted boundary-data property, stronger than the image estimate needed only for traces of auxiliary Neumann solutions.
Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature

We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure.
 The proof combines conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set with an HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set, overcoming both non-compactness and the loss of uniform hyperbolicity due to zero curvature. We also obtain mixing under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the existence of a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and the non-arithmeticity of the axial length spectrum are automatic.

The first eigenvalue of the $p$-bilaplacian over a domain $Ω$ is the inverse of the Poincaré constant for $W_0^{2,p}(Ω)$. In dimension two, we prove that it is minimised by disks under area constraint, thereby obtaining a sharp uniform Poincaré inequality.
Phase-type representations for Strong Stability Preserving Runge--Kutta methods
Haijun Yu; Quanfan Zhu; Zhanyang Weng

We develop a phase-type (PH) representation of strong stability preserving (SSP) Runge--Kutta (RK) methods. This representation provides a probabilistic interpretation of the RK coefficients and translates the chain order conditions into absorption-time moment identities. Using moment ratio bounds for PH distributions, we prove the conjectured optimal SSP coefficients for general implicit RK methods of orders two and three. The equality characterizations also establish uniqueness of the optimal RK tableaux.
Privacy-Preserving Over-the-Air Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with User-Centric Clustering

This paper investigates cross-layer design for differentially private federated learning over cell-free massive MIMO networks with over-the-air (OTA) aggregation. Distributed access points (APs) collaboratively serve user equipments (UEs) through user-centric clustering, where clipped local model updates are perturbed with Gaussian noise and simultaneously transmitted over a shared uplink for OTA averaging at a central processing unit. Exploiting channel hardening, we show that thermal noise inherent in wireless reception can act as a privacy-masking resource, reducing or even eliminating the need for artificial noise. Based on this observation, we formulate a joint optimization problem over AP-UE associations, UE transmit powers, and artificial noise variances to minimize aggregation variance subject to per-UE zero-concentrated differential privacy constraints derived from an ergodic privacy accounting framework. Analysis reveals a regime-dependent structure: stringent privacy requirements favor low transmit powers and sparse AP associations to exploit thermal noise for privacy, whereas relaxed requirements favor larger clusters to improve aggregation quality. The resulting mixed-integer nonconvex problem is solved via alternating optimization combining difference-of-convex power allocation and greedy coordinate-descent clustering. Numerical results show up to 89% lower aggregation variance than conventional baselines and enable 97% test accuracy on MNIST with consistent gains on CIFAR-10. Under strict privacy budgets, competing schemes remain near random-chance performance, while under relaxed budgets they continue to lag significantly behind the proposed design.
Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles

For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Codimension-Two Reduction, and Transverse Products

Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, and product constructions. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument replace the linear-independence step in Höfer's three-dimensional method. An explicit cylindrical decomposition estimate yields $\mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}$. For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two equidistant configuration splits off a common linear factor, giving $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. We also determine the sharp bound $2(n-k)$ when all directions lie in a fixed $(k+1)$-dimensional subspace. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities and makes $S(c)=\mathcal{N}(c-1,2c-1)$ supermultiplicative. In particular, $S(c)\geqslant 2^{c\bmod 2}7^{\lfloor c/2\rfloor}$. The structural results and constructions do not depend on the exact value of $\mathcal{N}(1,3)$.
Spectral $L^2$-bounds on Eisenstein series and Diophantine properties of quadratic forms

We give $L^2$-bounds with respect to the height of the spectral parameter for Epstein zeta functions $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E_{\mathfrak{c}}(s,z)$ attached to the Hecke congruence subgroup $Γ_0 (p)$ of prime level $p$. Our bounds are completely explicit in the level and, additionally, constitute an almost sure logarithmic improvement over previously established bounds for the level-one Eisenstein series. Following the approach of Kelmer--Kontorovich--Lutsko, we combine the approximate functional equation for $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ with estimates for the number of pairs of lattice vectors at which $Q$ takes nearly equal values. Under a Diophantine hypothesis on $Q$, we sharpen these counting estimates using results of Eskin--Margulis--Mozes on the distribution of values of quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$.
Typical Kakeya-type sets and their typical code sets
Josef Bell; Ezekiel Fleissner-Kates; Tamás Keleti

We study properties of compact Besicovitch sets and other Kakeya-type sets which are typical in the sense that the exceptions form a meager set in the Baire category sense in a suitable metric space. The main motivation comes from the known fact that typical compact Besicovitch sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ have minimal Hausdorff dimension among all Besicovitch sets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Thus, in order to estimate the smallest possible Hausdorff dimension of an arbitrary Besicovitch set, it is enough to estimate the Hausdorff dimension of a typical (compact) Besicovitch set, or analogously of a Besicovitch set satisfying our list of typical properties.
