We characterize the Green's functions of all strictly positive real self-adjoint realizations of this operator. The kernels are in one-to-one correspondence with positive-semidefinite $2\times2$ endpoint covariance matrices. We call the associated centered Gaussian processes Brownian processes. Each is a standard Brownian bridge plus the affine interpolation of an independent Gaussian endpoint vector. Singular endpoint covariance matrices give hard endpoint constraints, such as the pinned start $X(0)=0$ of Brownian motion. This parametrization gives explicit operator domains and energy spaces. On every mesh it gives an exact sparse precision matrix, so the likelihood of $n$ observations can be evaluated in $O(n)$ operations. Nonnegative realizations with a null space are treated separately through orthogonally normalized pseudoinverses, which are proper Gaussian covariances.
Frequency-Uniform Log-Regret Reinforcement Learning for Diffusions
Jose Blanchet; Lutong Hao; Renyuan Xu

High-frequency control problems are often studied through time discretization, but refining the timestep $δ$ increases the discrete horizon $H=T/δ$ and can make standard finite-horizon regret guarantees deteriorate even when the physical horizon $T$ is fixed. We study episodic value-based reinforcement learning for Euler discretizations of controlled diffusions. The performance is measured as the cumulative regret over $K$ episodes relative to the optimal policy of the corresponding Euler model. Under stability and regularity conditions on value function gradients, Bellman residual derivatives, and fitted critics, we prove an $\mathcal{O}(\log K)$ regret bound with constants uniform in $δ$. For dynamics with drift linear in unknown parameters and unknown constant diffusion covariance, we verify localized versions of these conditions for a constrained, model-based controlled-diffusion fitted-$Q$ algorithm (CD-FQ) and obtain high-probability $\mathcal{O}(\log K\log\log K)$ regret for fixed and finite $T$, again with constants uniform in $δ$.
A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
Wei Jiang; Chunmei Su; Ganghui Zhang

We propose a minimizing-movement framework for constructing parametric finite element methods (PFEMs) for anisotropic curve shortening flows. The cornerstone is an admissible modified energy: a smooth, convex, and iteration-dependent surrogate that majorizes the original anisotropic energy and agrees with it at the current iterate. For any fixed finite element degree $n\geq1$ and any positive surface energy density $γ\in C^2(\mathbb{S}^1)$, the unconstrained one-step problem has a unique solution for any time-step size whenever the parametric derivative of the current discrete curve does not vanish on any mesh element. It also satisfies a one-step discrete energy dissipation inequality. It therefore preserves the variational structure of the underlying $L^2$-gradient flow. The framework recovers a variational interpretation of Dziuk's isotropic scheme and applies directly to the weak anisotropies. For strong anisotropies, a convex splitting removes the weak-anisotropy restriction on the original density. A scalar constraint further extends the framework to area-preserving flows. Numerical experiments exhibit approximately the expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic examples. They also confirm energy dissipation and area preservation. In the strongly anisotropic regime, the computations produce sharp facet-like profiles but reveal mesh-scale oscillations under the grid refinement.
Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
Pu Ren; Michael W. Mahoney; N. Benjamin Erichson

Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. Our model, interpolative FLow EXpert (iFLEX), first estimates the missing field by taking a weighted average of the two observations at each grid point, giving more weight to the observation closer to the requested time. During training, subtracting this estimate from an observed intermediate field gives the residual that a conditional diffusion model learns to generate. Both observations condition the model, together with the target time, the interval between observations, and available physical parameters. To reconstruct an unobserved intermediate field, the generated residual is added to the weighted average. We evaluate iFLEX on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature. Across these datasets, iFLEX achieves lower reconstruction error than the evaluated baselines, including optical-flow and diffusion models developed for video frame interpolation in computer vision. In a controlled turbulence comparison at a Reynolds number of 36,000, learning the residual reduces relative Frobenius norm error from about 13.7 for direct field generation to 10.5, with the diffusion backbone and training setup held fixed. Code is available at https://github.com/paulpuren/iflex.
Negative edge correlation in complete bipartite graphs

We prove strict pairwise negative correlation under both the uniform forest measure and the uniform connected-subgraph measure on the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$ for all $m,n\geq2$. Under the connected-subgraph measure, any two distinct edges of a fixed copy of $K_{2,2}$ remain strictly negatively correlated after conditioning on the subgraph induced by the remaining vertices.
ODAT-SE: A modular and parallel framework for simulation-based inverse problems
Tatsumi Aoyama; Kazuyoshi Yoshimi; Yuichi Motoyama; Akito Nakano; Hengyu Li; Yusuke Konishi; Takeo Hoshi

Open Data Analysis Tool for Science and Engineering (ODAT-SE) is an open-source Python framework for inverse problems that are solved by repeated forward simulations. It succeeds 2DMAT, which was developed for surface-structure analysis with quantum-beam diffraction and has since been applied to other fields. In version 3, the search algorithms were separated from the application-specific solvers, which became independent packages, and the software was renamed; this paper describes the current version 4.0. The framework connects optimization and sampling algorithms to solvers through a common interface for parameter mapping, constraints, and objective evaluation, so that an existing simulation code can be used with any of the algorithms. Relative to the previously published 2DMAT, it provides two-level MPI parallelism, which distributes candidate evaluations over processes and each evaluation over a parallel solver, checkpoint and continuation facilities, random search, global optimizers from SciPy, tensor-train optimization, and a Bayesian workflow that estimates partition-function ratios, model evidence, effective noise levels, and marginal posterior distributions. We validate the Bayesian workflow against closed-form results for a linear regression, benchmark tensor-train optimization on continuous, binary, and mixed-integer problems, and verify the two-level parallelization by the same optimum for all process decompositions. Taking up the positron-diffraction example of the 2DMAT paper, the workflow identifies the correlated structural solutions and an effective noise scale close to the imposed perturbation, while exposing incomplete convergence of symmetry-related mode weights. Solver packages, templates, and a gallery of examples support the use of the framework as a general platform for inverse-problem analysis.
When do token systems stabilize? Compatibility constraints and community structure
Flore Sentenac; Mingwei Yang; Sophie H. Yu

Token systems support repeated service exchange without monetary transfers, but their viability depends on the stability of token balances. We study token systems with compatibility constraints among agents. A requester is randomly sampled in each period, and only a few randomly sampled agents are available to provide service. We establish a necessary and sufficient condition for stability and show that the minimum-token rule, which selects the available provider with the lowest token balance, achieves the optimal stability region. We then apply this stability criterion to a random token system generated from stochastic block models with uniformly sampled requesters. We tightly characterize the stability regime by identifying two obstructions to stability: insufficient service opportunities for a group of communities or for an individual agent.
The Costa surface with a free-boundary hole: an embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with three ends

An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface outside the unit ball whose compact boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. By Mazet and Mendes, in $\mathbb{R}^3$ every such surface with one regular end is a catenoidal piece, and every stable one with parallel embedded regular ends is catenoidal. We construct connected embedded examples with three ends from the Costa surface $M$, placed so that its central saddle point is at the origin. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ we perturb $\varepsilon^{-1}(M\setminus B_\varepsilon)$ into a properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface of genus one with one boundary circle and three ends, two catenoidal and one planar. The construction is a small-hole perturbation. The only error of the initial surface is in the boundary condition. The symmetry group of the Costa surface removes all obstructions: at the hole it forbids the logarithmic and the tilting modes, and globally it kills the bounded Jacobi fields of the Costa surface, which is nondegenerate by Nayatani. In the conformal compactification the Jacobi operator is smooth also at the ends, so the linear analysis takes place on a compact torus with one small hole. The same construction applied to the Costa-Hoffman-Meeks surfaces gives such examples of every genus $k\geq1$, of index at least $2k+3$. We also report numerical experiments with two independent implementations of the Costa surface. They confirm the period condition, the symmetries, the boundary error, the index and nullity of the Jacobi operator and the absence of an equivariant kernel. They also compute the free-boundary correction near the hole, which gives pictures of the surfaces.
Different approach to certain problems in univalent function theory

Using different approach we consider some problems for the class $\mathcal{S}_{ex}^{\star}$ defined by the condition $\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\prec e^{αz}$, $0<α\leq1.$ Our method is more simple than that used by Das and Sarkar in their work: \textit{Sharp coefficient estimates for the exponential starlike class $S^\star_{ex}$} (\cite{DS26}).
The Legendre potential and the gradient case of the differential Galois criterion for the Jacobian Conjecture

Let $h\in\C[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ have constant nonzero Hessian determinant, let $h^{*}$ be its formal Legendre transform and $g=\vv{X,\grad h}-h$. The Nambu derivations of $\grad h$ satisfy $δ_i(g)=X_i$ and $δ^α(g)=(\partial^αh^{*})\circ\grad h$. Consequently, in the gradient case the differential Galois criterion of \cite{ACH19}, consisting of $n$ membership conditions, reduces to a single membership condition. Equivalently, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $g\in\C[\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh]$. Moreover, $\grad h$ is a polynomial automorphism if and only if $δ^α(g)=0$ for $|α|=(°h-1)^{n-1}+2$, and then the coefficients $δ^α(g)(x_0)/α!$ of $h^{*}$ at $\grad h(x_0)$ determine the inverse. If the Hessian determinant of $h$ is merely a nonzero polynomial, then $g$ is still a primitive element of $\C(X)$ over $\C(\partial_1h,\dots,\partial_nh)$. For the Nambu-tower criterion, doubling a Keller map yields no independent conditions. After an affine change of coordinates putting $\grad h$ in the normal form $X+H$, the formal Legendre transform is the sum of the formal Pascal difference series of $g$, and the termination of this series implies polynomial invertibility. In at most three variables the normal form of every gradient Keller map has strongly nilpotent Jacobian part and is therefore Pascal finite, by a theorem of de Bondt, and an explicit gradient automorphism in four variables has a normal form which is not Pascal finite. The five-variable counterexample of Meng and Yang shows that the properties used here do not imply the Hessian conjecture. The results do not settle the open cases $\JC_2$ and $\HC_4$.
Finite Fields: Root Sets, Frobenius, and Algebraic Structure

This monograph develops finite field theory through root sets, Frobenius orbits, trace duality, and cyclic modules, with applications to polynomial constructions and algebraic coding theory. Root-set descent and base extension are expressed through finite reduced algebras, while linearized polynomials connect normal bases, invariant subspaces, and linear recurrences. Coefficient pairings and derivative formulas recover information lost by trace pairings in quotient algebras with repeated factors. Cyclotomic cosets are studied through additive stabilizers, power substitution, and compatible factor lifting, including extensions to Galois rings. A central theme connects low-degree representations of subfields with conjugate root blocks, polynomial composition, and recovery from relative trace data. Return maps on root fibers determine factor degrees and organize constructions of irreducible polynomials, affine symmetries, and permutation polynomials. Applications include cyclic and constacyclic codes, BCH and Goppa distance bounds, rank-metric codes, trace codes, and Fourier support. Character orthogonality and Gauss and Jacobi sums yield counting formulas, a proof of the primitive normal basis theorem, and recurrences for extension-field character sums. Gaussian periods connect these methods with short linear relations in multiplicative subgroups. Proofs of Weil bounds for polynomial character sums combine auxiliary polynomials with generating polynomials and estimates for their reciprocal roots. The emphasis throughout is on explicit arguments connecting field structure, orbit structure, and linear dependence.
Grassmannian Realizations of Classical Pseudo-Riemannian Symmetric Spaces

We establish a unified fixed-point Grassmannian framework for the classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces from Berger's classification. For a classical group $G=\mathop{\mathrm{Aut}}(V,b)$, we identify $G$ with the open graph-like locus inside an ordinary or maximal-isotropic Grassmannian $\overline{G}$. Natural involutions of $\overline{G}$ are constructed via classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations. We explicitly describe the full fixed loci of these involutions in terms of classical Grassmannians. The corresponding graph-like fixed loci (or their signature strata) are identified, respectively, with the moduli spaces of classical forms, compatible scalar structures, and subspace configurations; these moduli spaces coincide with classical pseudo-Riemannian symmetric spaces. In summary, the 54 classical series are organized into four families: 10 group-type models, 7 classical-form Grassmannians, 20 scalar-structure Grassmannians, and 17 subspace-configuration Grassmannians.
Robust Log-Contrast Regression for High-Dimensional Compositional Microbiome Data with Outliers
Xuke Hua; Yunhai Xiao; Xin Xin

It is well known that microbiome sequencing data are naturally compositional and often have a complex subcomposition structure, as well as a lot of noise and some outliers. These characteristics make classical log-contrast regression difficult to apply, because it is sensitive to extreme values and cannot fully meet the linear constraints of compositional predictors. To tackle these issues, in this paper, we propose a robust log-contrast regression framework that incorporates the Huber loss function along with a Lasso penalty, which not only boosts resistance to outliers but also facilitates sparse variable selection. It is important to note that the general linear constraints, which are explicitly imposed, serve to preserve the algebraic coherence of compositional and subcompositional covariates. Under some mild assumptions, we theoretically prove that the proposed method achieves non-asymptotic guarantees in finite samples, comparable to those of Huber loss estimators, ensuring robustness. To implement the method efficiently, we develop a symmetric Gauss--Seidel-based alternating direction method of multipliers based on its dual formulation with a convergence guarantee, and it is also easy to implement in the sense that each subproblem admits a closed-form solution. To evaluate the statistical performance of the proposed method, we conduct a series of numerical experiments using simulated data and gut microbiome data, which show that the proposed method achieves better estimation accuracy, competitive prediction performance, and more reliable outlier identification than the benchmark method RobRegCC.
Ancestor Lifting of Quasi-Cyclic Additive Codes and Certified Quantum Codes
Liangdong Lu; Ran Xu; Ruipan Yang; Qiang Fu

Additive codes over $\Ffour$ that are self-orthogonal under the trace inner product correspond to binary quantum stabilizer codes. We study 1-generator $(1,2)$-quasi-cyclic (QC) additive codes and their exact quantum distances. For composite lengths $n=\ell m$, an ancestor-lifting theorem transports dual words of the folded ancestor to the length-$n$ code. A two-layer decomposition for $\ell=2$ and a CRT splitting for odd $\ell$ yield dimension laws and explain equality, escape, and mixed-branch behavior in the certified examples. A palindromic criterion ensures symplectic self-orthogonality, while reversal pairing and a symplectic Gram rank formula describe broader construction families. Exact distances are established by information-set decoding screening, Brouwer--Zimmermann computation on the additive dual, and independent witness verification. We certify twenty-one record-breaking binary quantum codes across twenty entries of Grassl's code table, with twenty-eight certified members in total. Propagation improves thirty-four further entries, and explicit constructions are supplied for three table-tying GV entries marked Code Missing Construction. Six additional candidates are reported only with rigorous upper bounds and heuristic screening evidence. The results connect divisor-lattice structure in additive quasi-cyclic codes with reproducible certification of exact quantum distances.
Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator

Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

For conjugate shapes $λ$ and $λ'$, Stanley's duality relates the Jack symmetric functions $J_λ(x;α)$ and $J_{λ'}(x;1/α)$. Through Stanley's combinatorial formula, it is an identity between the sums of the weights of the semi-standard Young tableaux giving the same monomial. We introduce the Jack multiple zeta functions, which keep these weights separate, and prove that Stanley's duality lifts to them, including the case of skew shapes. Thus the duality holds before the weights are summed up, and in fact step by step along chains of partitions. Since the duality is an identity among formal symbols, the same duality holds when the multiple zeta functions are replaced by other functions, and replacing them with the monomial quasi-symmetric functions recovers Stanley's duality. Hence our duality is a refinement of Stanley's duality which contains it as a special case. In particular, we obtain a duality for the Schur multiple zeta functions and the classical relation between the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions. We next show that any expansion of a Jack symmetric function in terms of Schur functions can be lifted to Jack multiple zeta functions, yielding an analog of a formula conjectured by Stanley and proved by Koike. We also show that the Jack multiple zeta functions of one-row shape give a one-parameter family interpolating the multiple zeta and zeta-star functions, and we discuss their values at $\{2\}^r$ and at $\{2\}^a,3,\{2\}^b$.
The Exact Weight Spectrum of $\RM(m-7,m$): A Counterexample to the Carlet-Solé Conjecture

Boolean functions are widely used in cryptography and coding theory. A key challenge lies in finding the weight spectrum for all $n$-variable Boolean functions of degree at most $r$, also known as the Reed--Muller code $\RM(r,n)$. In 2023, Carlet and Solé determined the weight spectra of $\RM(n-c,n)$ for $c=3,4$, and conjectured the weight spectrum of $\RM(n-c, n$) for $n\ge2c$. The weight spectra of $\RM(n-5, n)$ and $\RM(n-6,n)$ were determined by Carlet in 2024 and by Lou and Wang in 2025, respectively, confirming the Carlet-Solé conjecture for the cases $c=5,6$. Very recently, Leuenberger et al. and Wei et al. investigated the weight spectrum of $\RM(7,14)$ independently, and there are eight potential weights which have not been determined. Up until now, the weight spectra of the Reed--Muller codes $RM(r,n)$ are still unknown for $r=3,...,n-7$. In this paper, we determine the exact weight spectrum of $\RM(m-7, m)$ for every $m\ge 14$. By combining affine geometry and Fourier analysis, we exclude the conjectured eight weights for $\RM(7,14)$. We then extend the exclusions to all higher dimensions using a geometric transfer. Consequently, we provide a counterexample to the Carlet-Solé conjecture.
An $L^p$ Version of Raeburn's Symmetric Imprimitivity Theorem

Let $1\leq p<\infty$. We prove an $L^p$-operator analogue of Raeburn's symmetric imprimitivity theorem for countable discrete groups. Let $A$ be an $L^p$-operator algebra with a contractive two-sided approximate identity, admitting a nondegenerate isometric representation on a $σ$-finite $L^p$-space. Given commuting free and proper actions of groups $G$ and $H$ on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space $Z$, together with commuting isometric actions on $A$, we show that the two corresponding full crossed products, and likewise the two reduced crossed products, are Morita equivalent as Banach algebras. The proof is organized through the linking groupoid. Its main analytic ingredient is a coefficient-valued spatial matrix dilation; in the reduced case we prove that this dilation preserves regularity after a Borel reindexing of the opposite corner. A pairing-valued approximate identity yields fullness and nondegeneracy.
Sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation in $H^{1/2}_\bullet$

We prove sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the half-wave maps equation on the real line $\R$ in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\). This regularity threshold for global well-posedness is optimal, as we show by constructing examples of ill-posedness in \(H^s_\bullet\) for any \(s<1/2\). Moreover, with the spectral assumption satisfied by a dense set of initial data in the energy space, we prove that solutions in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\) asymptotically decouple as an infinite superposition of solitons. Our results extend the known global well-posedness and finite soliton resolution for rational data in \(H^\infty_\bullet\) to sharp global well-posedness and soliton resolution for general data in \(H^{1/2}_\bullet\).
 Different from rational solutions, general data can also involve an infinite discrete spectrum, which makes the reduction analysis framework on the finite rank no longer applicable. For sharp well-posedness, we present a new isometry criterion and stability results for resolvent transform in the explicit formula. For soliton resolution, we develop a spectral method for this equation based on direct resolvent analysis and a novel trace norm estimate that upgrades energy convergence to uniform convergence. Our argument also yields sharp well-posedness and soliton resolution for the generalized half-wave maps equation with targets in the complex Grassmannians, extending the classical sphere-valued case.
New upper bounds for average kissing numbers

A packing of balls in Euclidean space is a set of balls with non-overlapping interiors. For a finite packing of balls, its average contact number is the average number of balls tangent to a ball in this packing, that is, twice the total number of tangencies divided by the number of balls. The average kissing number of the space is defined as the supremum of average contact numbers over all finite ball packings. In this paper, we present a new semidefinite programming approach to average kissing numbers and improve upon known upper bounds in all dimensions \(3\) through \(30\). In particular, we provide the first improvements to the upper bounds in dimensions \(10\) through \(30\) obtained from kissing numbers. We also fully solve the average kissing number problem in dimensions \(8\) and \(24\) by showing that the average kissing numbers coincide with the kissing numbers, 240 and 196560, respectively. These values are limits of average contact numbers of finite subpackings from the \(E_8\) and Leech lattices.
Design of DoF-Robust MIMO via Generalized Pinching Antennas
Zhiguo Ding; Robert Schober; H. Vincent Poor

Spatial degrees of freedom (DoF) are fundamental to the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. However, the use of conventional fixed-location antennas introduces disparities in the users' distances to a common base station, which makes the multi-user channel matrix more susceptible to rank deficiency and, consequently, a loss of spatial DoF. This paper shows that generalized pinching antennas can be used to design a new form of MIMO robust to the loss of spatial DoF. In particular, by deploying pinching antennas in close proximity to the users, the resulting multi-user channel Gram matrix can have a well-conditioned, almost diagonal structure, which reduces its sensitivity to the users' spatial deployment as well as the risk of rank deficiency. Two performance metrics, namely the rank-deficiency probability and the outage probability, are used to evaluate the performance of pinching-antenna-assisted MIMO transmission. The presented analytical and simulation results demonstrate the capability of pinching antennas to preserve spatial DoF and provide ubiquitous connectivity by effectively supporting users at spatially separated locations.
PDE-Based Bounds on Optimal Exponents in Active Simple Hypothesis Testing

We present general upper and lower bounds on the optimal error exponent for the Active Simple Hypothesis Testing (ASHT) problem. ASHT has been extensively studied across diverse fields including Information Theory, Bandits, and Operations Research, a precise characterization of this optimal exponent has remained elusive. This work combines a recent Partial Differential Equation (PDE) characterization of the optimal exponent by Vijayan (2025) with the comparison principle of viscosity solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi PDEs. This leads to bounds that are parametrized by convex functions, sets and lower Hamiltonian relaxations, a flexibility that generalizes many known results in the literature.
Eduardo Alves da Silva; Fernando Figueroa; José Ignacio Yáñez; Joaquín Moraga

We prove that most rational smooth Fano threefolds are compactifications of $\mathbb{G}_m^3$. More precisely, we study which smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type, i.e., for which smooth Fano threefolds $X$ one can find a boundary $B\in |-K_X|$ and an embedding $\mathbb{G}_m^3\hookrightarrow X\setminus B$. We prove that many important classes of smooth Fano threefolds are cluster type. For instance, a smooth Fano threefold which is the blow-up of either $\mathbb{P}^3$ or $\mathbb{Q}^3$ and is general in its deformation space is of cluster type. As a consequence, we show that among the $105$ families parametrizing all smooth Fano threefolds, the general element of precisely $87$ families is of cluster type. We prove that a general prime smooth Fano threefold of genus $7$ is not of cluster type. This is the only family whose general element is rational but not of cluster type. Finally, we prove that cluster type projective klt varieties are cylindrical and we give a criterion for such a cylinder to be anticanonically polar. Using this, we reduce the cylindricity problem for smooth Fano threefolds to the families $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.3$, $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.5$, and $\mathcal{N}^{\mathrm{o}}\,1.6$.
On the Pontryagin Maximum Principle for Rough Stochastic Differential Equations
Peter K. Friz; Ulrich Horst; Stefanos Theodorakopoulos; Huilin Zhang

We establish first- and second-order Pontryagin (a.k.a. stochastic) maximum principles for rough stochastic control problems with general nonlinear $\mathrm{Lip}^γ$-rough vector fields. This complements the dynamic programming approach of Friz-Lê-Zhang [FLZ26b], and extends the maximum principle of Horst-Zhang [HZ26] beyond affine rough vector fields. The paper concludes with applications to pathwise stochastic optimal control.
An upper bound of 61 for the Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$

We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 61. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers.
Reflection equations and Littlewood identities for spin Hall-Littlewood and $q$-Whittaker functions

We describe two-parametric Littlewood identities for inhomogeneous stable spin Hall-Littlewood and inhomogeneous spin $q$-Whittaker symmetric functions. These identities generalize the Littlewood identity found by Warnaar (2006) for the ordinary Hall-Littlewood polynomials. However, instead of Rogers-Szegö coefficients used by Warnaar, coefficients in our identities are given by products of Al-Salam-Chihara polynomials.
 Our proof relies on integrable lattice models. A key step includes three new solutions to the reflection and boundary equations for the fully fused six-vertex model. To find these solutions we use isomorphisms between tensor products of evaluation $U_q(L\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-modules, as well as covectors stable under a $q$-Onsager coideal subalgebra.
Fluid Problems Posed on Closed Hypersurfaces: Circumventing the Saddle-Point Structure

For a $d$-dimensional closed hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, we reformulate the (stationary) tangent Stokes, transient tangent Stokes, and transient tangent Navier-Stokes equations by replacing the divergence equation with a pressure Poisson equation, thereby circumventing their saddle-point structure. The pressure Poisson equation hinges on a commutator identity between the divergence and the surface diffusion operator, whose lower-order term depends on the Ricci curvature, and requires no boundary conditions for the pressure. We show that the reformulated operator is the composition of a linear, block-triangular data map with the primal operator. Consequently, each reformulation is well-posed if and only if the primal problem is, and solving it with arbitrary data amounts to solving the primal problem with a modified divergence datum. For hypersurfaces of class $C^2$ and data of the pressure Poisson equation in $H^{-1}$, the tangent Stokes reformulations can be posed in $H^1$-based spaces, which paves the way for conforming discretizations that do not require a discrete inf-sup condition.
Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities

For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplusΛ^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.

We study the relationship between semisimplicity and non-degeneracy for finite-dimensional Hopf triplets over a field of characteristic zero. The non-degeneracy condition appears in the construction of \(4\)-manifold invariants from Hopf triplets, and it was not known whether non-semisimple examples satisfying this condition exist. We prove that a Hopf triplet is non-degenerate if and only if it is semisimple.
Time-Periodic Chemotaxis in Shifting Environments: Propagation and Planar Forced Waves in $\R^N$

We study time-periodic Keller--Segel dynamics in a translating KPP environment. In the parabolic--elliptic regime, we prove global boundedness, identify the sharp speed \(c_*=2\sqrt{\bar a\,\bar r}\), establish persistence in the interior region \(|s|<c_*\), \(s\cdot e<c\), and derive the complementary sharp upper bounds; for a moving favorable slab, the sign of a principal Floquet exponent determines persistence or extinction under the stated weighted-resolvent condition. For every fixed \(τ\ge0\), under constant population diffusivity and sufficiently weak taxis, we further construct locally unique planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\). The main new analytic mechanisms are an exact Yukawa first-contact estimate, which controls the chemotactic drift at the KPP leading-edge scale without losing the sharp propagation threshold, and a two-sided weighted Fredholm--monodromy continuation framework for the temporally nonlocal signal equation, with explicit control of the far-field spectral gaps and the translational neutral mode. To the best of the author's knowledge, planar forced time-periodic waves in \(\mathbb R^N\) for shifting Keller--Segel systems have not been investigated in any previous studies; earlier forced-wave results are confined to substantially more restrictive settings, in particular one-dimensional parabolic--elliptic models. Thus the present construction provides the first multidimensional planar forced-wave theory for a time-periodic shifting Keller--Segel system with temporal signal memory.
Diameter Bounds and Finiteness of Graphs from Local Intersection Data

We extend the Bakry--Émery curvature framework on graphs, broadening its applications and strengthening the resulting diameter bounds. We study diameter bounds and finiteness for amply regular graphs, distance-regular graphs, $(s,c,a,k)$-graphs, and locally strongly regular graphs. In particular, for an amply regular graph with parameters $(v,k,λ,μ)$, we prove that \[{\rm{diam}}(G)\le4+8\log\frac{k}{λ+2}\] when $μ>2$ and $k\ge3λ^2/μ$, improving the previous linear bound $4k/(λ+4)$ to a logarithmic bound.
 We also address several related conjectures. In their monograph \emph{Distance-Regular Graphs}, Brouwer, Cohen, and Neumaier conjectured that every amply regular graph with $μ>1$, except the icosahedron, satisfies ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le2k/(λ+2)$. We confirm this bound when $μ>λ+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $μ=λ$. For amply regular graphs with $μ\geλ$ and $μ>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/μ+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture.
 In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when $s>2$, $c>2$, and $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $μ>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.
On extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function

We describe extended interpolation properties of the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function over an imaginary quadratic field. We have three applications. Firstly, we give an elliptic analogue of the Coleman-Ihara formula. Secondly, we extend Kato's explicit reciprocity law for elliptic units and give a proof of the Tamagawa number conjecture for critical Hecke motives. Finally, we prove a large part of the $p$-adic Beilinson conjecture for the Katz $p$-adic $L$-function.

We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $ζ(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $ζ$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.
Integral Forms of Twisted Quantum Affine Algebras and Quantum Frobenius

For twisted quantum affine algebras, we compare Lusztig's restricted integral form with the integral form generated by group-like toral elements and divided powers of real Drinfeld current modes. The two forms coincide over $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ outside type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$. In type $A_{2n}^{(2)}$, the smallest ordinary localization over which they coincide is $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{4r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n=1$, and $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}][Φ_{8r}(q)^{-1}\mid r\geq1]$ when $n\geq2$, where $Φ_k(q)$ are cyclotomic polynomials. In particular, no localization obtained by inverting finitely many nonzero Laurent polynomials suffices in this family.
Axiomatic Learning and Probabilistic Structures with first applications to variants of Arithmetic Machine Learning and beyond

We introduce the Axiomatic Learning Structures (ALS) and Axiomatic Probabilistic Structure (APS) in order to study the interactions of Machine Learning, Optimization, with research frameworks- which, we take the view, can be characterized at the core by the corresponding axioms. The ALS explores the interplays between structures that one is interested in Learning Theory such as Loss functions and the axioms of the objects and transformations involved in these functions. The APS studies the interaction between structures of interest in Probability Theory such as Gibbs distributions, equations with noise, etc. and the axioms of the corresponding objects and transformations. We also introduce in Section 6 Transformations-Axiomatic Based Learning (TABLe) on Mathematical data-sets. One feature of this approach is the ranking of transformations from a table for a certain task based on scores which reflect which transformations work better than others, similarly to when human investigators try various methods on a task. We also study structure recovery from noisy data. In particular, to exemplify the ideas, we consider loss functions which contain derivations and derivations-like transformations. As a first application we study recovery in the context of polynomials with integer coefficients using standard derivatives along with other types of derivations which appear in Arithmetic: the p-derivations which satisfy \textit{different axioms} from the usual derivatives. As a first application of the APS we study a class of noisy (partial/mixed) derivations equations. In the last sections, to provide further potential applications of this framework, we give an overview of an initial simplified Opinion Dynamics model and its (simultaneous) study of rules of updates.
On the interpolation property of Kupferer's Lubin-Tate regulator maps

Generalizing both [LZ14] and [ScV26, SaV24] we prove the interpolation property at Artin characters of Kupferer's regulator map [Ku20] over a fixed local field $L$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ for $p$ any prime. Since our methods cover the case $p=2,$ we in particular close a gap in the literature even for the (cyclotomic) 2-variable regulator map from [LZ14]. Moreover, we study big (dual) Bloch-Kato exponential maps for unramified towers and we use them to improve Colmez' reciprocity law in the Lubin-Tate setting from [SaV24]. Finally, we compare Kupferer's regulator map with the 2-variable regulator map of Loeffler-Zerbes when $L=\mathbb{Q}_p$.
CLT for quadratic additive functionals of three-dimensional and four-dimensional voter models

In this paper, we prove central limit theorems for the quadratic additive functionals of the three-dimensional and four-dimensional voter models. Our main results show that, under proper time-space scalings, the centered quadratic additive functional of the four-dimensional voter model converges weakly to a Brownian motion and that in the three-dimensional case converges weakly to a Gaussian process without independent increment. The proof of the main result in the four-dimensional case extends the martingale decomposition method. In the three-dimensional case, we introduce a quadratic fluctuation limit theorem which shows that the quadratic fluctuation density field of the voter model converges weakly to a generalized Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. Then our main result in the three-dimensional case follows from an argument where the quadratic additive functional is approximated by an integral of a test function with respect to the quadratic fluctuation density field. The duality relationship between the voter model and the coalescing random walk is repeatedly utilized in proofs of the main results. The proof strategies introduced in this paper are applicable in deducing CLTs for general additive functionals of three-dimensional and four dimensional voter models. We only deal with those with the quadratic forms to make our exposition easy to catch.
Square-root logarithmic bounds for the arithmetic complexity of factorial multiples

Assume that the Riemann zeta function has no zeros in $\Re(s)>1-δ$, $s\neq1$, for some fixed $0<δ\leq1/2$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, a positive multiple $m_k k!$ has arithmetic complexity $τ(m_k k!)\leq\exp(C\sqrt{\log k\log\log k})$, where $C$ depends only on $δ$. We first establish a smooth-number asymptotic at every sufficiently large center $x$ in intervals of length at least $x^{3/4}$. Combining this estimate with an established genus-two construction yields the arithmetic bound without Cheng's conjecture on smooth numbers in elliptic Hasse intervals. The bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

A graph $G$ is degree-truncated DP-$k$-colourable (respectively, degree-truncated $k$-choosable) if it is DP-$f$-colourable (respectively, $f$-choosable), where $f(v)=\min\{k,d_G(v)\}$ for every vertex $v$. Hutchinson proved that every $2$-connected maximal outerplanar graph other than the triangle is degree-truncated $5$-choosable. Lo, Wang, Zhou and Zhu strengthened this result by proving that every $2$-connected $K_{2,4}$-minor-free graph other than cycles and complete graphs is degree-truncated DP-$5$-colourable.
 Outerplanar graphs are precisely the $\{K_4,K_{2,3}\}$-minor-free graphs. We study how the truncation threshold grows when $K_{2,3}$ is replaced by $K_{2,t}$, while $K_4$-minor remains excluded. A bound independent of $t$ is impossible, as shown by the family $\{K_{2,n}| n\ge 2\}$. Let $\mathcal S_t$ be the class of $2$-connected $\{K_4,K_{2,t}\}$-minor-free graphs other than cycles. Writing $χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t)$ for the least truncation threshold valid throughout this class, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge3$, \[ \left\lfloor2\sqrt{2t}\right\rfloor \le χ^{\text{\sout{d}}}_{\mathrm{DP}}(\mathcal S_t) \le \left\lceil4\sqrt{2t}\right\rceil. \]
Wasserstein approximation of measures via orthogonal frames: statistical and computational complexities
Mateo Díaz; Nicolás García Trillos; Daniel López-Castaño; Congwei Yang

Dimension-reduction methods such as PCA identify a subspace capturing most of the variation in the data, but not a distinguished basis within it. Selecting a basis in which the samples are sparsely represented is a recurring task in unsupervised learning, addressed by methods in factor analysis, dictionary learning, and subspace clustering. We pose this task as Wasserstein approximation of the data distribution by measures supported on the axes of an orthogonal frame, which, in turn, reduces to a nonsmooth optimization problem over the orthogonal group $\mathrm{O}(d)$. We show that, under mild assumptions, both empirical risk minimizers and a locally initialized stochastic gradient method recover the population-optimal frame at the near-parametric rate $\widetilde{O}_d(n^{-1/2})$, where $n$ is the sample size. The main difficulty is that, although the population objective is smooth, the empirical objective is not-this mismatch precludes standard covering arguments. We overcome this issue by replacing Lipschitz continuity of the empirical gradient with a coarsely Lipschitz bound, a tool that may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments support our theoretical findings.
Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations

We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{α,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{β,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $α+β>1$ and $β$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $αp>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $β>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $β>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.
Helly theorems for lattice of flats of a matroid

A basis of a matroid is adapted to a flat if it contains a basis of the flat. We prove that a family of flats in a rank r matroid has a common adapted basis whenever every subfamily of at most r+1 flats does. The ground set and the family may be infinite; only the rank must be finite. This result, in particular, contains Klyachko's vector space Helly theorem for subspaces. As an application, we obtain a splitting criterion for tropical toric vector bundles on projective spaces. As a secondary application, we derive quadratic bounds for the Helly number for distributive generation in the lattice of flats.
Equivalence between rationality and modular invariance under $C_2$-cofiniteness

We prove that for a simple and $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, the rationality is equivalent to the modular invariance of the space of complete ordinary one-point trace functions of its irreducible modules. This proves a conjecture given by Dong-Ren in \cite{DongRen}, which is also the inverse theorem of Zhu's modular invariance theorem \cite{Zhu}.

We prove that a complete connected four-dimensional gradient steady Ricci soliton with positive curvature operator that is $κ$-noncollapsed at all scales admits an effective isometric $O(3)$ action preserving the potential function and having principal orbits diffeomorphic to $S^2$.
Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
Ricardo Torres Naranjo; Samuel Castillo Apolonio

We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $γ(t)=ζ_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leqζ_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $ζ_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an $ω$-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. \cite{Pinto_ejqtde}. The case $ζ_k=t_k$ reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of $ζ_k$ within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.
Holomorphic Cauchy Networks for Efficient Stationary Tail Computation in High-Dimensional Reflected Brownian Motions

Stationary tail computation for high-dimensional reflected Brownian motions (RBMs) remains computationally challenging. Building on NN4MGF's shared-coordinate basic-adjoint-relationship (BAR) framework, we develop Holomorphic Cauchy Networks (HCNs). Native complex-valued rational Cauchy subnetworks enforce holomorphicity on pole-free domains, removing sampled Cauchy-Riemann penalties and their input-derivative graphs. Exact origin anchoring and boundary-coordinate exclusion enforce structural identities, while anchored interactions represent dependent transforms. Under holomorphic-log assumptions, we establish simultaneous value and first-derivative approximation for the constrained architectures and a mixed-derivative lower bound for coordinate-only representations under nonzero cross-covariance. Closed-form real-axis derivatives and sequential backpropagation further control memory. On the same NVIDIA H100 NVL, the tested 30D HCN configuration uses approximately tenfold less peak allocated memory and has 9.7-fold lower mean update time than NN4MGF; extrapolation to the respective scheduled update counts gives a projected full-schedule update-time ratio of 58.2. With 64 million sampled base inputs per high-dimensional run, HCN reaches 50 dimensions on a laptop GPU with 6.367% mean relative error over thresholds 1 through 8. Degree-matched comparisons yield lower reported mean relative errors over the primary evaluation ranges, including 1.422% versus 6.684% on the 2D Harrison non-product benchmark. An exploratory 10D correlated example illustrates the interaction extension.
QESChunker: A Single Objective Unifies Overlapping and Non-Overlapping Chunking for RAG
Yifan Zhao; Qianyang Zhao; Xinyu Guan; kai wei; Yuming Deng

Chunking is a fundamental preprocessing step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), yet most existing chunkers rely primarily on heuristics. We introduce the Question--Evidence-Supervised Chunker (QESChunker), to our knowledge the first method for constructing static chunk indices from question--evidence supervision. QESChunker constructs document-specific chunk indices by optimizing over human-annotated or LLM-generated question--evidence pairs, without access to held-out test queries. We formulate non-overlapping and overlapping index construction through a unified question--evidence utility-maximization objective, turning chunking into a supervised combinatorial optimization problem. Under the non-overlap constraint, the objective decomposes over chunks and can be optimized exactly in polynomial time by dynamic programming. When overlap is allowed, the objective becomes monotone submodular; exact optimization is NP-hard, but our greedy achieves a $(1-1/\sqrt{e})$-approximation. Across two self-constructed and three public datasets, both variants outperform existing chunking methods in complete-evidence recall in nearly all evaluated settings, under the same overlap regime and a fixed hybrid retriever. These results recast chunking as supervised, budget-aware index construction for evidence retrieval.
NextEval: An Agent-Based Solver and Benchmark for Derivative-Free Optimization
Shuo Chen; Li Cui; Cunxin Huang; Ya-Feng Liu; Minghang Xie; Meng Xu; Zaikun Zhang

Derivative-free optimization (DFO) addresses problems where derivatives are unavailable or costly to obtain. This setting often arises in simulation-based and experimental applications, where evaluating the black-box objective can itself be costly. Thus, it remains a central challenge in DFO to effectively exploit accumulated observations to select informative evaluation points under a limited budget. In this light, we introduce the NextEval solver, an agent-based DFO solver, which integrates the capabilities of a large language model (LLM) to guide the sequential selection of evaluation points. Specifically, we establish a system that combines an LLM agent with a numerical environment. The environment provides tools for analyzing past evaluations and executing numerical methods, while maintaining a shared evaluation history and method-specific state to support continuation across method switches. Using observations and tool feedback, the LLM agent selects tools, configures their parameters, and allocates the evaluation budget, while numerical methods compute and evaluate candidate points. Building on this system, we also introduce NextEval Bench, a benchmark protocol for comparing agent configurations on shared DFO tasks using the same numerical tools under matched evaluation budgets and information constraints. Numerical results on low-dimensional DFO problems demonstrate that the NextEval solver outperforms the state-of-the-art DFO baselines in function-evaluation efficiency.
A Fibrational Framework For Multi-Conclusion Logics

The fibrational framework of Licata, Shulman, and Riley gives a uniform account of substructural and modal logics for single-conclusion judgments. This thesis extends it to a multiple-output setting in which cartesian resources may be used freely, while linear resources occur exactly once on either side of the turnstile. Judgments are indexed by descriptors: directed acyclic graphs generalizing the tree-shaped expressions of the original framework. Descriptor $2$-cells encode structural transformations, and explicit gates provide weakening, contraction, coweakening, and cocontraction at linear modes.
 We define a sequent calculus generated by two connectives, $F$ and $U$. We prove identity, invertibility, and cut admissibility. The mode and type theories present linear-non-linear $2$-polycategories, and the projection is a local discrete fibration and a fibration, with opcartesian lifts for one-output base morphisms. Two adequacy results validate the framework: its cartesian fragment recovers the Licata--Shulman--Riley calculus, and its purely linear fragment presents classical multiplicative linear logic.
 Finally, we relate indexed and fibrational semantics. After developing representability correspondences for multicategories and polycategories, we establish an equivalence between multi-indexed categories over a fixed representable base and multicategorical opfibrations over it, together with its biclosed bifibrational version. We also give a one-way construction from planar poly-indexed data to a planar polycategory.
Function spaces with compact-open topology need not be sober

We exhibit sober spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that the function space $[X \to Y]_K$ of continuous maps, equipped with the compact-open topology, is not sober; the codomain can be chosen to be the Sierpiński space $S$. Our construction builds on Isbell's complete lattice $M$, whose Scott space $ΣM$ is non-sober. Let $H = Q(M)$ be the set of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $ΣM$, ordered by reverse inclusion. Since $H$ is well known to be a spatial frame, the space $X = \mathrm{pt}(H)$ is sober with $\mathcal{O}(X) \cong H$. The key technical result is that sobriety of the space $H$ would entail sobriety of the original Scott space $ΣM$. This contradicts Isbell's example, and the desired counterexample follows.
A Fast Algorithm for Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition under the QT-Product with Applications to Color Video Processing
Daochang Zhang; Yue Zhao; Jingqian Li

Based on the complex representation of quaternion matrices, this paper revisits the quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (QT-SVD) under the QT-product and establishes the corresponding $z$-block circulant matrix decomposition. We develop an efficient implementation of the QT-SVD. Numerical experiments show that this implementation is substantially faster than QT-SVD based on the quaternion matrix SVD approach \cite[Theorem~2.3]{AMLzhang2022} while maintaining high numerical accuracy. We further apply the QT-SVD to color video encryption and reconstruction. Experiments on five DAVIS video sequences show that the QT-SVD achieves higher reconstruction quality and shorter decomposition times than the quaternion T-SVD \cite{tsvdarxiv} under the same processing procedure. Both methods exhibit comparable ciphertext statistics and differential sensitivity, while the QT-SVD introduces less additional distortion under the tested input perturbations.
On Solutions for Singular Toda System on Surfaces with Boundary
Zhengni Hu; Aleks Jevnikar; Sang-Hyuck Moon

This paper studies a singular Toda system with linear source terms on a compact surface $Σ$ with boundary $\partialΣ$. The aim is twofold. First, using isothermal coordinates and reflection arguments near the boundary, we perform blow-up analysis obtaining a compactness result. Second, by assuming that $\partialΣ$ has at least two connected components, we prove a general existence result via a min-max scheme combined with a retraction argument.
On an exponent-preserving duality for Coxeter multiarrangements of type $B_2$

In the theory of hyperplane arrangements, the study of logarithmic derivation modules is one of the most important subjects. If the module is free over a graded ring, the multiset of degrees of its homogeneous basis is called exponents. We utilize some basic theory of linear algebra to study the exponents of multiarrangements. As an application, we show a new exponent-preserving duality for the Coxeter multiarrangements of type $B_2$, which was conjectured by Torsten Hoge.
ATEMPO: Amortized Transfer Entropy Model Per-lag Over-Time
Emma Andrews; Konstantinos Kontras; Keane Ong; Maarten De Vos; Gianmarco Mengaldo

When one time series informs another, the delay at which that information arrives determines if models can utilize this relationship effectively. A source may be strongly predictive at one delay but uninformative at neighboring lags. Therefore, fixed input windows may obscure this structure by bundling informative and irrelevant history together. Transfer entropy (TE) can recover these delays by measuring how much a source's past tells us about a target beyond the target's own history. However, existing TE estimators require separate fits across source and conditioning depths, with further estimation on local windows to track delays over time. We introduce ATEMPO, a diffusion-based transfer entropy estimator amortized over lags and time. ATEMPO samples source and conditioning depths during training and conditions explicitly on temporal position, allowing a single score network to estimate the full TE surface without refitting. Differencing this surface recovers when information arrives. Across synthetic datasets with ground-truth TE, ATEMPO achieves the lowest mean relative error among baselines, and on datasets with known lags, ATEMPO achieves $0.98\pm0.04$ lag-detection accuracy. ATEMPO requires a single fit across source depths $K=6$ and target depths $L=3$, whereas existing estimators require 18 separate fits to evaluate the same $K \times L$ grid. On three systems with time-varying lag, ATEMPO is the only estimator to maintain perfect lag-detection accuracy across all evaluated window lengths. These recovered delays improve downstream forecasting: ATEMPO-selected inputs reduce MSE on WEATHER-5K by 7.25%, while 120 selected inputs outperform the benchmark's 240-feature default by 4.6%. Across three brain-computer interface tasks, using ATEMPO-selected lags achieves the highest or equal-best $R^2$, improving mean $R^2$ by 4.1% relative to the strongest competing baseline.
Resolvent Components of Completely Normal Elements and the Morgan-Mullen Conjecture

We study completely normal elements of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$, that is, elements that are normal over every intermediate field, through partial Lagrange resolvents. In these coordinates, complete normality splits into independent components, in a way closely related to Hachenberger's decomposition theory. Our main tool is a structure theorem for the components; together with a finite computation, it shows that every component has weight (the sum of the probabilities that its conditions fail) at most $3/4$, uniformly in $n$. Combined with the classical character-sum method, this gives an explicit sufficient criterion for the existence of a primitive completely normal element. We verify the criterion for all $n>q$ except $70$ pairs $(q,n)$, which we settle with explicit elements found by computer. Since the case $n\le q$ is due to Garefalakis and Kapetanakis, this confirms the conjecture of Morgan and Mullen (1996) that every $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ contains a primitive element that is completely normal over $\mathbb{F}_q$. The same estimates give two further results. First, Hachenberger's conjectured lower bound $(q-1)^{n'}q^{(p^a-1)n'}$ for the number of completely normal elements, where $p$ is the characteristic and $n=p^an'$ with $p\nmid n'$, holds for all pairs $(q,n)$; it was known for regular pairs. Second, primitivity and complete normality are asymptotically independent: as $q^n\to\infty$, the number of primitive completely normal elements is $(1+o(1))\,\varphi(q^n-1)/(q^n-1)$ times the number of completely normal elements (for fixed $n$ this was known). Our arguments for $n>q$ and for both further results, including every computer-assisted step, are formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib; the formalisation takes the case $n\le q$ and an explicit bound of Rosser and Schoenfeld as axioms and relies on Lean's compiler and interpreter for the large computations.
William Kalies; Konstantin Mischaikow; Robert Vandervorst

This note describes a novel approach to systematically characterize dynamics based on finite information. We present an algebraic framework for dynamics from which it is possible to deduce more traditional descriptors associated with the qualitative structures of the geometric theory of dynamical systems. The purpose of this paper is to indicate how this approach can be used to obtain interpretable characterizations of dynamics that are robust with respect to perturbations, in the context of models of multiscale and data-driven systems.
Hybridizing 0/1 Knapsack and Priority-Aware TSP for Vehicle Routing: an Applied Variant of the TSP with Profits
Aron da Silva Bezerra; Francisco Márcio Barboza

Distribution logistics with capacity constraints and service priorities can be modeled as a variant of the \emph{TSP with Profits} (TSPP), in which not all customers need to be visited and the selection of which customers to serve is part of the problem. This paper proposes an applied variant with two adaptations: (i) a 0/1 Knapsack objective function weighted by client priority squared ($v_i \cdot p_i^2$), and (ii) a priority bias in the Nearest Neighbor heuristic for the TSP, parameterized by $α$. The approach is evaluated on a scenario with 14 customers and a 1,100~kg capacity, complemented by a comparative experimental protocol against the classical greedy heuristic ($v_i/w_i$ ordering) and an integer programming solver. Results on the base scenario show 9 customers served, 96.4\% capacity utilization, and R\$~18,392.60 revenue, with all 5 excluded customers being low-priority. A sensitivity analysis of the priority exponent justifies the quadratic choice. The limitations of the hierarchical decomposition are explicitly discussed.
Constructions for Nearly Diagonal Book Ramsey Numbers

The Ramsey number $R(G_1,G_2)$ is the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for every graph $H$ on $n$ vertices, either $H$ contains a copy of $G_1$ or the complement $\overline H$ contains a copy of $G_2$. Ramsey numbers involving the book graphs $B_n$, which consist of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge, have attracted recent attention, especially in the ``nearly diagonal'' case $R(B_{n-1},B_n)$. Rousseau and Sheehan showed the upper bound $R(B_{n-1},B_n) \le 4n-1$ nearly fifty years ago, but no general matching lower bound construction is known. This paper gives several new infinite families of $n$ for which $R(B_{n-1},B_n) = 4n-1$.
 Some of the main results in this paper were found with assistance from the Station, a multi-agent AI system. These results also appeared in a larger work on autonomous mathematical discovery by the authors and Du in arxiv:2608.23691. This paper is a follow-up to that work: we give complete proofs of the book Ramsey results and discuss their connections to objects in combinatorial design theory.
Detailed balance and phase transition in Nash equilibria of mean-field Ising game
Ken Hiura; Hajime Koike; Kiyoshi Kanazawa

We study a finite-state mean-field game with entropic control cost. In the large population limit, we show that its stationary Nash equilibria satisfy the detailed balance condition and their distributions take the Gibbsian form with the value function playing the role of a Hamiltonian. We apply the entropic control cost to a ferromagnetic mean-field Ising game and investigate its stationary and non-stationary Nash equilibria. We find that the stationary Nash equilibria exhibit a second-order phase transition from disordered to ordered equilibria as temperature decreases. A center-manifold reduction yields non-stationary Nash equilibrium near the critical temperature and reveals the critical slowing down in the relaxation toward the stationary Nash equilibrium.
Failure of the congruence Hasse principle for commutators in orientable surface groups

Ghosh, Meiri and Sarnak showed that the commutator equation over $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfies a profinite local to global principle, and that for a prime $\ell\equiv\pm1$ mod $5$ it fails for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell])$ with a reciprocity obstruction. We extend the failure to surface groups. For the genus-$2$ surface group $Γ_2$ we construct an explicit representation $ρ:Γ_2\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$, where $K=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$ and $\mathcal{O}_{K,S}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2},\frac{1}{10}]$, whose quotients modulo the maximal ideals are the full groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ except in residue characteristic $3$, where the quotient has order $24$. For every $k\ge2$ the word $[a_1,b_1]^k$ is not a commutator in $Γ_2$, while its image is a commutator in every one of these quotients. The same holds for every surface group $Γ_g$ with $g\ge2$.
Quartic Keller Maps and Tameness in Three Variables

We study invertibility and tameness for polynomial maps of affine three-space of total degree at most four. We prove that every complex Keller map in this degree range is a polynomial automorphism and, independently, that every complex polynomial automorphism of total degree at most four is tame. The invertibility argument combines homogeneous factorization of the leading part, invariant rings of conic pencils, and residue obstructions on cubic fibers. The tameness argument uses a criterion based on a constant second directional derivative, low-degree coordinate classifications, and local tameness of plane polynomial automorphisms over a polynomial parameter ring. The invertibility conclusion extends to every field of characteristic zero.
