We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=π^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.
Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
Xinyu Bai; Wanshan Lin; Xueting Tian

Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.
Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
Ben S. Lambert; Oliver C. Schnürer

We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander.
Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression
Philip Bille; Inge Li Gørtz; Rikke Jessen; Jingxun Li; Simon Rumle Tarnow; Renfei Zhou
We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.
Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics

We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/Γ$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also obtain quantitative pointwise equidistribution for Haar-almost every point on each full expanding horosphere.
Numerical analysis of a Lax-Wendroff type lattice Boltzmann scheme for the advection equation
Thomas Bellotti; Filipa Caetano; François Dubois; Benjamin Graille

A linear monodimensional lattice Boltzmann scheme with three velocities tackling the advection equation is investigated. We prove that it is second-order accurate and provide necessary and sufficient stability conditions through an explicit formula involving the two relaxation parameters. Relying on existing results for finite difference schemes, we prove convergence for smooth initial data with initialization of the non-conserved moments at equilibrium. Several numerical simulations illustrate these theoretical findings.
Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
Shengyang Zang; Yingyu Zhao; Yunhao Zhao; Chen Zhou

We prove sharp bounds for the upper and lower intermediate dimensions of orthogonal and radial projections of compactly supported measures. Both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension. We obtain exceptional-set estimates using the entire source dimension function, with sharpness for explicit families. We also construct a fixed measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open direction sets, even when all source dimensions lie below the target dimension.
Beam Search for Error-Correcting Codes via Conditional Diffusion

We introduce a diffusion framework for neural decoding of error-correcting codes (ECCs). We interpret decoding as a conditional diffusion process that progressively predicts codeword bits while treating the physical channel observation as fixed side information. At each stage, a neural model estimates bitwise posteriors conditioned on the physical observation and the current noisy state of the codeword. We focus particularly on masked diffusion, for which the reverse process naturally induces a Maxwell beam search (MBS) procedure inspired by the Maxwell construction of Measson et al. Rather than committing to a single uncertain decision, the decoder maintains multiple candidate trajectories, removes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks the remaining candidates using accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities. We evaluate the framework across multiple code families on binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Experiments show competitive decoding performance across Polar, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes. The MBS decoder consistently improves upon the corresponding single-trajectory diffusion decoder and, in all evaluated settings, improves upon available neural decoding results.
Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss

We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.
Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules
M. Harper Langston; Pierre-David Letourneau; Dalton Jones; Roland Memisevic; Peter Scott; Mingu Lee; Richard A. Lethin; Christopher Lott; Fatih Porikli; Harris Teague

We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.
Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
Siyue Liu; Taihei Oki; Chao Xu

Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by Hörsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of Hörsch et al.
Triangle-Free Sets in Exact-Distance Hamming Graphs
Bence Csajbók; Padmini Mukkamala; Zoltán Lóránt Nagy

Let $T_q(n,r)$ be the largest size of a vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph of the graph on $[q]^n$ whose edges join words at Hamming distance $r$. We study this quantity for fixed alphabet size and fixed distance, with particular emphasis on the ternary cube. Alphabet restriction transfers the binary fixed-distance theorem of Balogh, Chen, and Li to give $T_q(n,2h)=O_h(q^n/n^h)$. We extend the known distance-one formula and distance-two order to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, obtaining $T_q(n,1)=2q^{n-1}$ and $T_q(n,2)=Θ_q(q^n/n)$, and establish $T_3(n,4)=Θ(3^n/n^2)$. For general fixed distance, we prove \[ T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}\!\left( \frac{q^n\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{(r+\lfloor r/2\rfloor)/2}} \right)\qquad(q\ge3), \] while we show that $T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}(q^n/n^{\lfloor(q-1)r/q\rfloor})$ holds for prime-power $q$ and $r\ge2$ via the extended BCH parity-check constructions. At distance three, we construct coordinate weights avoiding bounded-coefficient three-term relations and obtain \[ T_q(n,3)\ge q^n/[n\exp(O_q(\sqrt{\log n}))]. \] Our main ternary construction combines cap partitions, multicolor triangle Ramsey colorings, and a quadratic map to obtain \[ T_3(n,3)=Ω\!\left( \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\,3^n\right). \] A coordinate-line counting argument gives the complementary upper bound $T_3(n,3)\le(5/27+O(n^{-1}))3^n$, together with an explicit bound for every fixed $q\ge3$. Whether the ternary density tends to zero remains open.
Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions

We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.
AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.
On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.
Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups

We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.
Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique

We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.
Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
L. G. S. Duarte; L. A. C. P. da Mota

The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=φ(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(φ,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a Möbius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.
Neural network enhancement of the Born approximation
J. Ma; A. Desai; T. Lahivaara; P. Monk

We examine the use of neural networks in conjunction with the Born approximation for solving the inverse scattering problem for a penetrable medium in the frequency domain. The goal is a fast method for determining the refractive index of a scatterer from multistatic far-field measurements at one frequency. We present a new neural network model that seeks to improve on our previous results in by sharpening the reconstructed images. In addition, we present two other networks motivated by the corrected Born method that avoid the need to invert the regularized Born operator. These latter algorithms will be important for future three dimensional applications when the inverse Born approximation is difficult to compute, or when near-field measurements are used. Computational results illustrate that the new corrections to the Born approximation can provide an accurate and flexible approach to the inverse scattering problem.
The restricted Hurwitz action on cameral decompositions of Coxeter elements

Given a dual Coxeter system (W, T) of rank n, the Hurwitz action of the braid group on the reduced T-decompositions of a Coxeter element is transitive. When we choose a geometric representation of W, the reflections with respect to the n walls of one given chamber form a generating set S that we call cameral. An ordering of S is called a cameral decomposition and the product a cameral Coxeter element, which depends only on the quiver obtained by orienting the Coxeter diagram with vertices S according to the ordering. We show that the reduced decompositions of a cameral Coxeter elements for which the underlying set S satisfies that (W, S ) is a Coxeter system, are necessarily cameral, and we count the number of chambers from which a cameral Coxeter element can be obtained. We show that one can go through all these chambers using the restricted Hurwitz action on the set of cameral decompositions, which is generated by transpositions of adjacent commuting reflections and by the Garside element δ of the dual Garside structure, which acts by a quiver mutation of the orientation of the Coxeter diagram.
Polarization on Bounded Euclidean Spaces and More General Compact Groups
Sharang M. Sriramu; Lampros Gavalakis; Ioannis Kontoyiannis; Aaron B. Wagner

We establish polarization for memoryless sources taking values on the unit-perimeter circle, or on more general compact groups, under Arıkan's polar transform. For sources with finite differential entropy, all but an $O((\log N)^{-1/12})$ fraction of the conditional differential entropies in successive cancellation order lie within any fixed positive distance of zero, where $N$ is the block length. Examples indicate that the true polarization rate is indeed very slow: an inverse-logarithmic rate does not underestimate the polarization speed at moderate block lengths.
G-ORACLE: A Fast Geometric Method To Explore All Near-Optimal Designs for Energy Systems

Modeling to Generate Alternatives (MGA) methods explore the near-optimal solutions of energy system optimization models (ESOMs), i.e., alternative planning pathways whose cost lies within a small predefined slack of the optimum but which can differ substantially in technology composition, regional distribution, and environmental impacts. Among MGA methods, ORACLE uniquely guarantees convergence to the near-optimal set within a targeted tolerance by iteratively refining inner and outer polytope approximations. At each iteration, given a trial point, it solves a problem as hard as the ESOM to find the nearest near-optimal solution to it. However, the trial point is obtained by solving a bilevel problem whose solution time grows rapidly with the number of iterations and eventually dominates the computational cost of the method. To eliminate this bottleneck, we present G-ORACLE, which exploits the fact that an optimal solution of the bilevel problem is always attained at a vertex of the outer approximation. G-ORACLE therefore replaces the bilevel problem with incremental vertex enumeration by the double description method and one convex projection per vertex, while retaining the convergence guarantee of ORACLE. A supporting-hyperplane check further avoids unnecessary recomputation of these projections as the inner approximation grows. We evaluate G-ORACLE on an electricity-only PyPSA-Eur model, exploring the near-optimal space of the installed capacities of six generation and two storage technologies. While ORACLE's bilevel problem exceeds 20 minutes at iteration 64, G-ORACLE performs the trial-point search in at most 14 seconds throughout 240 iterations, leaving the ESOM solves as the only significant computational cost.
Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem

We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.
A Proximal Gradient Method for Nonconvex Nonsmooth Optimization with Applications
Jose M. M. Brito; Felipe Lara; Yinjun Yuan

We study a proximal-gradient method for the sum of a convex smooth function $g$ and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth, strongly quasar-convex regularizer. The gradient step is weighted by the quasar-convexity parameter, so, for step sizes in the descent range, the iteration decreases a weighted objective, while the unweighted sum serves for comparison. We establish a geometric envelope around every global minimizer of the unweighted objective, with an explicit radius independent of the step size; a common minimizer yields global linear convergence. We also prove that every critical point $u$ of the weighted objective lies within an explicit multiple of $\|\nabla g(u)\|$ from every global minimizer of the unweighted objective. Together with an optimized composite comparison, this yields asymptotic distance bounds. An example shows that the two objectives can have different critical points. For power-regularized least squares with powers between zero and one, descent provides a confinement ball for the sharp local modulus, and support identification combined with a KL argument yields whole-sequence convergence.
The totally nonnegative wonderful compactification of G is a ball

Let $\overline{G}$ denote the wonderful compactification of a semisimple algebraic group $G$ of adjoint type. We use contractive flows to show that the totally nonnegative part of every $G \times G$ orbit closure of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed Euclidean ball. In particular, the totally nonnegative part of $\overline{G}$ is homeomorphic to a closed ball.
Bistability with equal and independent removal in small bimolecular networks

We classify two-species mass-action networks with at most three internal directed reactions on $\{X,Y,2X,X+Y,2Y\}$, positive inflows, and linear removal of both species. Among the 681 networks up to species exchange, exactly 27 admit two distinct positive hyperbolic attracting equilibria. The same 27 admit bistability with equal removal rates and with independently chosen positive removal rates. Each is minimal under reaction deletion. We give rational equal-removal witnesses for all positive cases and all-parameter exclusions for the remaining 654. The proof combines nullcline geometry, polynomial sign tests, resultant root bounds, and exact flux-cone decompositions. A separate rational-arithmetic implementation verifies the complete classification and its equilibrium certificates.
A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces

Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $δ\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-δ+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $δ$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$. Such a subspace is maximum $h$-scattered if and only if the kernel of $A$ contains no nonzero vector whose expansion with respect to an $\mathbb{F}_q$-basis of $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ has rank weight at most $h+1$. When $\gcd(n,s)=1$, $R$ is a field, and a first-moment argument, counting these vectors up to multiplication by $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*\mathbb{F}_{q^s}^*$, shows that with positive probability the kernel contains none of them if $s>h(n-h-2)$. When $d=\gcd(n,s)>1$, $R$ is a product of $d$ fields, and vectors vanishing in some factors lie in the kernel with larger probability. We control them by proving that, for an $(h+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $D$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, the elements of $D\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ vanishing outside $k$ given factors, $0<k<d$, form an $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-space of dimension at most $(h+1)k/d$, with equality only if $D$ is linear over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ larger than $\mathbb{F}_q$. Taking $s=gr/(h+1)$ gives the bound on $r$. Finally, if $(n-h-1)\mid(h+1)$, then for every $r$ satisfying the above inequality there is an $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ of dimension $\lfloor rn/(h+1)\rfloor$, without a divisibility condition on $rn$.
A complete Kähler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone

We construct complete smooth Kähler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the Kähler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.
Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation

The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $ω_ϕ(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.
Total eight-colorings of maximal planar graphs of maximum degree six

We prove that every finite simple maximal planar graph of maximum degree at most six admits a total eight-coloring. We first show that every proper vertex four-coloring of a subcubic graph extends to a total five-coloring. A curvature inequality for boundary walks then gives a matching decomposition of four-connected triangulations with degrees five and six, extending their prescribed vertex four-colorings to total eight-colorings. In a minimum counterexample, two local boundary colorings force the degree-four vertices to have disjoint neighborhoods. A characterization of the local extension obstructions permits these vertices to be restored simultaneously. The proof uses Hamiltonian-connectedness of four-connected planar graphs and Kardoš's Hamiltonicity theorem for three-connected cubic planar graphs.
Discrete WKB approach to density profiles in inhomogeneous two-band free-fermion chains
Federico Finkel; Artemio González-López; Martín Zapata

We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.
Score-Preserving Continual Lasso under Task Shift
Jingyi Guo; Runze Li; Lingzhou Xue

Continual learning (CL) aims to learn from sequential tasks while mitigating catastrophic forgetting when historical data are no longer accessible. We study continual learning for high-dimensional sparse linear regression, where $\ell_1$ regularization creates a difficulty absent from continual ridge regression: that recursively reusing an $\ell_1$-penalized estimator can propagate earlier shrinkage and accumulate regularization bias across tasks. We propose score-preserving continual Lasso (SP-CL), which separates sparse estimation from state transmission by preserving the historical squared-loss score. Under squared loss, its cumulative estimator exactly recovers a full-history Lasso minimizer. When task coefficients coincide, it inherits the full-history sparse rate. For related task-specific coefficients, SP-CL uses a regularized current-task correction that leaves the transmitted state unchanged and attains the offline source-assisted rate under an oracle related-task condition. We also derive Overall/BWT/FWT decompositions that distinguish historical information loss, task conflict, and current-task specialization, and validate the resulting regimes in simulation.
Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order

We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$ -Δu=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0 \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, \tag*{$(*)$} $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that problem $(*)$ admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove compactness of the solution set of $(*)$ by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is nondegenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set of $(*)$ is finite. Our results give a negative answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].
Simple homotopy types of smooth four-manifolds with finite fundamental group

We construct closed smooth $4$-manifolds with finite fundamental group which are homotopy equivalent but not simple homotopy equivalent, even after taking a connected sum with copies of $S^2\times S^2$. Our explicit examples have remarkably large fundamental groups; in particular, the smallest examples we obtain have fundamental groups of order roughly $10^{10^{42}}$.
Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes

Simplified spectral models predict dimension-dependent superlinear convergence for gradient methods, but the corresponding behavior of actual iterations remains only partially understood. Historical methods introduce an additional difficulty: the gradients defining the step sizes differ from those receiving them. We study this offset for cyclic reuse of historical Ritz step sizes on strictly convex quadratics. Within the existing limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR) family, a rolling cyclic Ritz (RCR) rule reuses $m$ historical Ritz values $\ell$ times per cycle, ending with a complete sweep. At $q=m+1$ active distinct eigenvalues, an exact delayed recurrence gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence with an explicit rate and exceptional weights. Nonempty open basins also exist for $m+1<q\le2m$ and $\ell\ge4$. Rebuilding the history from each cycle-start gradient costs $m$ additional updates and gives sampled cyclic Ritz reuse (SCR) a cycle-end map determined by the current weights. Under uniform sampling bounds, SCR converges doubly exponentially almost everywhere when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{q-1}{m}$. Increasing $\ell$ admits larger $q$ for fixed $m$. The guarantee extends to history-dependent choices from finite sampling menus under a bound on the number of admissible sampling sequences. Geometrically spaced decisions retain the SCR condition and rate range. Every update is counted, including sampling; a numerical illustration compares finite-tolerance update counts.
Spectral convergence associated with Weil's quadratic form

Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we study a distinguished self-adjoint extension of the differentiation operator on a Hilbert space defined by the Weil quadratic form localized to a finite interval. The local quadratic form is determined by data from finitely many places, without requiring the zeros of the Riemann zeta function as input. We prove that the positive eigenvalues of this extension converge to the distinct positive ordinates of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function as the interval expands. We also prove that the associated normalized spectral entire functions converge locally uniformly on the complex plane to the canonical product over these distinct ordinates. The key step is an identity expressing the inverse of the local extension as a compression of the inverse of a global self-adjoint operator.
Necessary and Sufficient Criteria for Global PID Regulation of Nonlinear Uncertain System

Although classical PID control is widely used in engineering practice, identifying all PID gains that guarantee global regulation of nonlinear uncertain dynamics remains challenging. For a class of second-order nonaffine systems under one-sided derivative bounds, we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for global PID regulation: a fixed PID controller globally regulates the entire infinite-dimensional uncertainty class if and only if it regulates a single boundary linear system. Applying the Routh--Hurwitz criterion to this boundary linear system yields the exact admissible PID gain region. To establish this equivalence, we prove a structured Markus--Yamabe theorem for third-order integrator chains under uniform derivative-ratio conditions. Its proof combines a two-dimensional storage function constructed via viscosity solutions of a Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a scalar comparison argument. We further show that the same PID gain region remains exact for multidimensional affine systems under symmetry assumptions on the state partial Jacobians and the input matrix.
Non-equilibrium density fluctuations for the stirring process with weak boundary dynamics
Panagiota Birmpa; Patrícia Gonçalves; Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis

We consider the one-dimensional stirring process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We investigate the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the system, starting from a product measure associated with a smooth initial profile. The limit Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process is given in terms of the Laplacian and gradient operators acting on test functions satisfying time-dependent Robin boundary conditions that are obtained by linearizing the boundary conditions in the hydrodynamic equation. A central ingredient in our analysis is the derivation of sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree for the centered occupation variables; these bounds were proved in the companion article \cite{birmpa2025nonequilibriumfluctuationsstirringprocess}.

Scenario trees are widely used to discretize multistage stochastic programs into forms that are tractable for numerical optimization. Yet, traditional scenario-tree construction methods are typically based on statistical similarity between the original uncertainty process and its discretization, and may fail to preserve the aspects of the uncertainty that matter most for decision-making. This paper shows that, under a fixed probability measure and deterministic feasibility constraints, the gap between the optimal value of the original multistage stochastic program and that of its scenario-tree approximation decomposes exactly into a sum of nodewise regret terms, each measuring the optimality loss at a particular node. This decomposition provides a clear target for scenario-tree construction: minimizing total regret across the tree. Motivated by this result, we propose a practical two-phase construction method for repeated stochastic optimization. In an offline phase, computationally inexpensive surrogates for decision regret are learned from data, and in the online phase, these surrogates guide scenario-tree construction. The resulting framework retains the structured optimization and constraint-handling capabilities of multistage stochastic programming while exploiting learned information about the uncertainty to make more effective use of a limited scenario-tree budget. Numerical experiments on multistage stochastic storage and production-planning problems show that, for a fixed tree size, the proposed method constructs higher-quality scenario trees and achieves better closed-loop performance than traditional scenario-tree construction methods.
Random nodes with positive weights: Richter-Tchakaloff rules and optimal positive quadrature

We show that independent random points support exact quadrature rules with positive weights. For any $n$-dimensional space $V$ of integrable functions a constant multiple of $n\log n$ points sampled from a suitable density yields, with high probability, positive weights which integrate the functions in the space exactly. They are the result of a weight adaptation procedure which requires an explicit $L_1$-norm discretization result that is proved on the way. Combining the random rules with a subsampling step, we show that positive quadrature rules with constantly oversampled nodes achieve the best possible worst-case error bound in terms of the singular numbers of the embedding into $L_2$.
A genus-two spectral curve of the Riemann $Ξ$-function: Real Structure and Certified Arithmetic Separation of Periods

We associate a compact genus-two real spectral core with a transverse logarithmic-derivative discriminant of the Riemann $Ξ$-function. Directed interval arithmetic certifies its branch geometry, a real $P_{\mathrm{III}}(D_6)$ scalar-normal-form realization, and associated Kummer and Shioda--Inose models. Their certified heat motion yields generic local nonresonance and Diophantine separation, while explicit Farey windows impose denominator barriers of $1{,}036{,}003$ and $140{,}769$ throughout $|κ|\le3\times10^{-10}$ in the heat time $κ$. Avalanches of the Abelian sandpile on the hierarchical lattice
Luca Cattani; Leandro Chiarini; Alessandra Cipriani

We study the Abelian sandpile model on a sequence of finite fractal graphs: the hierarchical, or Migdal--Kadanoff, lattices. Our first main result consists of matching power-law tail bounds for the avalanche and the uniform wave started at certain "pivotal" vertices. We also establish a limiting result for the pivotal reach of the avalanche and, finally, a scaling limit for the size of a uniform wave started at a vertex of high degree.
The Martingale Property in Volterra Volatility Models
Julien Guyon; Thibault Jeannin; Benjamin Jourdain

We study martingality and strict local martingality in a broad class of stochastic and path-dependent Volterra volatility models and explain the underlying mechanisms. Our martingality criteria allow rough kernels and rely on non-accessibility of an explosive direction or one-sided growth bounds on the Girsanov drift. For smooth kernels, we derive sufficient conditions for strict local martingality from an explosion criterion allowing multiplicative noise, coupled factors and general initial input curves. Our results recover classical criteria and yield new results for Volterra and path-dependent models.
Realizable Cohomology Classes of Dihedral and Generalized Quaternion Groups
Sutirtha Datta; Jyotirmoy Ganguly; Rohit Joshi

We compute the Chern classes of irreducible representations for the dihedral groups $D_{2n}$ and the generalized quaternion groups $Q_{2^n}$. Utilizing these computations, we investigate whether every even-dimensional class in the integral group cohomology of these families can be realized as a Chern class of some complex representation. It turns out that this realizability question answers in the affirmative for the generalized quaternion groups. In contrast, it turns out that the answer for dihedral groups is erratic.
Sharp asymmetric vertex-Ramsey properties of graphs

In 1992, Łuczak, Ruciński and Voigt showed that for any graph $H$, a parameter $m_1(H)$ - called the 1-density - governs the threshold at which the binomial random graph $G(n,p)$ inherits the vertex-Ramsey property. It is an open question whether the Lie algebra $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of a block of a finite group algebra $kG$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of prime characteristic $p$ is simple only if the block is nilpotent with an elementary abelian defect group of order at least $3$. We show this to be the case if $B$ has a normal abelian defect group. Another open question is whether $\mathrm{HH}^1(kS_n)$ is a solvable Lie algebra, where $S_n$ denotes a symmetric group on $n$ letters. We give some general solvability criteria for $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ of blocks $B$ with a normal defect group, and, making use of results of Chuang-Kessar and Chuang-Rouquier, we deduce that if $B$ is a block of a symmetric group algebra with an abelian defect group, then $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is solvable.

The formula has error $O_\varepsilon(U^{1/2+\varepsilon})$, real parts of all four shifts in $[3/64,5/64]$, and imaginary parts of absolute value at most $U^{1/4}$. For a fixed real smooth weight supported in $(1,101/100)$, we obtain an error $O_\varepsilon(x^{-1/16+\varepsilon})$ in the correlation sum with weight $W(n/x)^2/n$. Adding the Riemann hypothesis improves this error to $O_\varepsilon(x^{-3/8+\varepsilon})$. Two nonnegative time weights have the same diagonal term and opposite coefficients for the difference four. We deduce the logarithmic asymptotic for the weighted prime-pair sum $B_4$ and an asymptotic for the second finite difference of integrals of squared increments of the truncated Chebyshev function. The latter is connected to a logarithmically weighted Möbius approximant in the Nyman--Beurling criterion by finite identities.

For $1<p<q<2$, we determine the optimal power exponent in the scalar supporting-line inequality and obtain a larger explicit sharpness interval. The proof pairs opposite logarithmic displacements and controls the nonlinear deficit by a quadratic reference energy of the transformed function. Its translation estimate allows a positive contribution at bounded scales to absorb negative contributions at remote scales. Concentrating tests prove strict loss of homogeneous sharpness near both finite-energy endpoints, and angular variations give concrete bounds for the first sharpness threshold. We extend the method to flat singular sets and regional half-space energies, retaining the distinction between ambient finite-energy conditions and finiteness of the homogeneous candidate. We also treat the complementary order $p>q$, including flat-subspace inequalities and a complete alternative proof for point singularities. All sharpness sequences belong to the specified smooth test classes, and every positive optimal constant extends to their completion in the difference norm.
A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every $\ell_p$ Norm

We establish an $Ω(d)$ lower bound on the competitive ratio of convex body chasing in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $\ell_p$ movement costs for any $p \in [1, \infty)$. Previously, the best known lower bound for general $p$ was $Ω(\max\{\sqrt{d}, d^{1-1/p}\})$, established by Bubeck et al. (2019); a linear lower bound was known only for $p = \infty$, realized by the standard construction of chasing faces of a hypercube. Our lower bound strictly improves on the prior bound for every fixed $p \in [1, \infty)$ and shows that the functional Steiner point algorithm of Sellke (2023) - which has competitive ratio $O(d)$ - is asymptotically optimal for every $\ell_p$ norm. Our lower bound is based on the recursive construction of Bubeck, Coester, and Rabani (2023) for metrical service systems, which gives a lower bound of $Ω(r^2)$ for requests of size $O(r)$ in that setting. We show that requests in their construction, each comprising a set of discrete points in a graph metric, can be mapped to the vertices of convex requests in a $(2r+1)$-dimensional vector space while approximately preserving movement costs up to a factor of $O(r)$, which establishes the lower bound.

Takeru Hasegawa; Naoto Mitsume; Shota Deguchi; Mitsuteru Asai; Tetsuya Kanagawa

Interactions between ultrasound and microbubbles underlie a range of biomedical and industrial applications, yet predicting how the physical parameters of the medium and bubbles govern nonlinear wave propagation remains difficult. This study proposes a parameter estimation framework that combines a Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers (KdVB) equation, describing weakly nonlinear wave propagation in a bubbly liquid, with a physics-informed neural network (PINN). The contributions are threefold. First, the PINN reproduces the reference solution of the governing equation in the forward problem, with a near-zero prediction error at the initial time that confirms the initial condition is enforced exactly as intended. Second, prior to inverse estimation, a sensitivity analysis is introduced that quantifies, at both the coefficient and solution levels, how each of eight physical parameters influences the KdVB equation, allowing the expected difficulty of estimating each parameter to be assessed in advance. These results establish a general framework for identifying and estimating the physical parameters governing nonlinear wave propagation in bubbly liquids from observed waveform data.
An Invitation to Algebraic Methods in Quantum Theory
Peter T. J. Bradshaw; Jonte R. Hance

In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.
How much do increasing events occur disjointly?

We establish two general quantitative lower bounds on the gap in the classical BK inequality for increasing events. The first is an analogue of Talagrand's quantitative FKG inequality (1996) and depends on the influences. The second is specific to the BK inequality and involves both the influences and the probabilities of symmetric disjoint pivots.
Weighted decoupling inequalities via fractal bilinear Kakeya estimates
Decoupling inequalities for the parabola are obtained for weights in physical space. The decoupling iteration relies on a fractal bilinear Kakeya estimate. We record applications to exponential sums.

For $β\ge0$, let $A_1^{(β)}$ be the class of weights satisfying $$ [w]_{A_1^{(β)}}:= \sup_{0<\varepsilon\le1} \varepsilon^β[w]_{A_{1+\varepsilon}}<\infty. $$ These classes satisfy $A_1\subsetneq A_1^{(β)}\subsetneq\bigcap_{p>1}A_p$ for $β>0$. For every $α\ge0$, we prove that $w\in A_1^{(β)}$ if and only if $$ w\left(\left\{M_{L(\log L)^α}f>λ\right\}\right) \le C\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|f(x)|}λ \left[ \log\left(e+\frac{|f(x)|}λ\right) \right]^{α+β} w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x. $$ The least constant $C$ is comparable to $[w]_{A_1^{(β)}}$. Also, we obtain corresponding characterizations for Calderón--Zygmund operators and their commutators.
Approximating the Gibbs Measure of Spherical Spin Glasses to Within $o(N^{-1/2})$ in the Replica Symmetric Phase
Brice Huang; Andrea Montanari; Huy Tuan Pham

We study the magnetization vector of mixed spherical spin glasses in a weak external field, in the replica symmetric phase. We derive a coordinatewise expansion of the magnetization which includes the leading cubic correction to the quadratic approximation, with an error that is $o(N^{-1/2})$ per coordinate. We also prove a corresponding high-moment bound for the full vector. Finally, our companion paper applies these estimates to the effective Hamiltonian obtained by restricting a tilted spherical spin glass to a narrow band around a TAP critical point. The resulting sharp approximation is designed for applications in which normalized Wasserstein accuracy is insufficient, including total-variation sampling by stochastic localization.
Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
Takayuki Hibi; Francesco Navarra; Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank. In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.
Lior Gishboliner; Sepehr Hajebi; Xiangyu Li

We prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu that for a $3$-graph $H$, the off-diagonal Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$ if and only if $H$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the "depth-$t$ iterated blowup" $\textsf{B}_t$ for an integer $t\geq 0$. Here, the $3$-graphs $\textsf{B}_t$ are defined recursively: $\textsf{B}_0$ has one vertex, and $\textsf{B}_t$ for $t\geq 1$ is obtained from the disjoint union of three copies of $\textsf{B}_{t-1}$ by adding all transversal hyperedges.
Split Frobenius Groups, Equational Domains, $\mathfrak{X}T$- and $CS\mathfrak{X}$-groups

We investigate conditions under which a semidirect product $G=HN$, and in particular a restricted wreath product, is an equational domain. For a variety of groups $\X$, we study semidirect products of $\XT$-groups (groups where $\langle A, B\rangle \in\X$ for any two $\X$-subgroups $A$ and $B$ with nontrivial intersection) and $\CSX$-groups (groups where all maximal $\X$-subgroups are malnormal). We pay particular attention to split Frobenius groups and investigate conditions under which such groups are $\XT$- or $\CSX$-groups.
Dimension-free bounds for maximal operators associated to log kernel and applications
Mingming Cao; Honghai Liu; Zengyan Si; Haibin Yan

Let $M_ψ$ be the maximal operator associated to $ψ(x)=-\ln(1-|x|^2)$. We obtain dimension-free bounds on $L^p(\mathbb R^d)$ for $M_ψ$, $1<p\le\infty$. We show that the weak $L^1$ estimate does not hold for $M_ψ$, but does hold for the corresponding lacunary maximal operator $M_ψ^D$. An weak $L\log L$ type estimate for $M_ψ$ is obtained, which seems to be the right substitution for the weak $L^1$ estimate. Estimates for $M_ψ$ are applied to dimension-free estimates for maximal Riesz transforms obtained by Mateu, Verdera, Orobitg and Pérez.
Hausdorff dimension of canonical height spectra

We study the Hausdorff dimension of the closure of the canonical height values associated to finite compositions of two rational maps. For rational maps with common periodic critical points, a nonzero local--global height discrepancy gives a nonempty set of starting points with positive-dimensional spectra. For polynomials, equality of the normalized logarithms of the leading coefficients at every place forces dimension zero; a single-place discrepancy gives positive dimension under boundedness at the other places. The spectrum dimension gives a lower bound for the growth exponent of the number of distinct orbit points of bounded height. At the degree exponent, positive Hausdorff measure gives matching growth bounds for multiplicatively dependent degrees. For independent degrees, a restriction of the covering intervals and a Diophantine rotation estimate give a lower bound with logarithmic loss of exponent strictly less than \(1/2\). Quadratic monomial examples show that the spectrum dimension can depend on the starting point even when both individual orbits are infinite.

We construct quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators with Gevrey potentials for which the Lyapunov exponent is discontinuous in the spectral energy. More precisely, let \(α\in\R\setminus\mathbb Q\) satisfy the Diophantine condition \(\|kα\|_{\T}\geqγ|k|^{-τ}\) for all \(k\in\Z\setminus\{0\}\), with \(γ>0\) and \(τ\geq1\). For bounded-type frequencies (\(τ=1\)), the regularity range \(\mathfrak s>2\) is sharp up to the endpoint \(\mathfrak s=2\), since the Lyapunov exponent is known to be continuous in energy for \(1<\mathfrak s<2\).
The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns

We prove that the free energy of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $α$ and temperature $T$, and we give it as an explicit variational principle. The Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation maps the model onto $N$ Ising spins coupled to $M=αN$ Gaussian hidden units, whose radius, the empirical variance of the hidden layer, is a thermodynamic variable with an entropic cost. At fixed radius the model is an Ising--spherical spin glass with Gaussian couplings, which we solve. The principle (i) reproduces the Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky theory as its replica-symmetric restriction, (ii) identifies $T_g=1+\sqrtα$ as the rigorous boundary of the annealed region, (iii) selects a unique spin-glass solution of the AGS equations, and (iv) gives the radius an equation of state. Moreover, (v) below $T_g$ we prove that replica symmetry is broken throughout: the instability of the AGS solution reduces to the zero-field de Almeida-Thouless condition of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.

For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(ξ)\|_p=\|ξ|_E\|_p$ for every $ξ\in\ell_d^p$. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.
Inverse problems and continuity of heat content coefficients

We consider the small-time asymptotic expansions for the Dirichlet and Open heat contents of convex planar domains. We prove that the small-time asymptotic expansion for the Open heat content can determine a triangle among triangles, a parallelogram among parallelograms, and an acute trapezium among acute trapezia of the same height. In addition, for a sequence of convex polygons converging to a convex set with smooth boundary in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ in the small-time asymptotic expansions of the Dirichlet and the Open heat contents converge to those of the limiting set. While, for a sequence of convex sets with smooth boundary converging to a convex polygon in the sense of Hausdorff, we show that the coefficients of order $t$ do not converge to that of the limiting polygon.
The effect of the permeability in interface problems: impermeable barriers and free diffusion

Focusing on reaction-diffusion models with an interface region dividing the domain, we study the stability of systems as the permeability parameter approaches zero or infinity under Kedem-Katchalsky boundary conditions imposed on the membrane or interface region. These boundary conditions establish that the flux across the interface manifold is proportional to the density jump across that region, with the constant of proportionality defined as the permeability parameter. This analysis is carried out for both the well-known symmetric case, where permeability is identical in both directions across the membrane, and the asymmetric case, where it depends on the direction of the flux. For the asymmetric case, we obtain novel and surprising results that reveal a richer variety of behaviors in this class of interface problems and that differ from the scalar models.

We consider a kinetic model of predator-prey dynamics in which predation is characterized by a sequence of behavioral transitions. Prey and predators are described by distribution functions in phase space, with the predator population further structured into internal states corresponding to inactive, active, and saturated individuals. We show that different macroscopic functional responses emerge from distinct mechanisms governing predator activation. More precisely, activation driven uniquely by pairwise encounters leads to a saturating Holling type II response, whereas activation additionally modulated by local prey density produces a generalized sigmoidal Holling type III response. This is achieved by means of a diffusive scaling and a formal hydrodynamic limit, from which we derive a closed reaction-diffusion system of Rosenzweig-MacArthur type for the prey and total predator spatial densities.

We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).

Since classical algorithms for computing such functions can be computationally expensive, neural network approximations have recently emerged as an alternative. A central difficulty with establishing such neural network based approaches for symmetric polyconvexity is the additional monotonicity property. As we show, the corresponding weight restrictions on ReLU-based input-convex networks do not yield universal approximation of the lifted representers. Here, we introduce symmetric polyconvex neural networks (SPCNNs) for constitutive modeling and approximation of symmetric polyconvex envelopes. The deep architecture combines convexity with the monotonicity required of a representer in the space of minors. We prove a universal approximation theorem for symmetric polyconvex energies, without requiring isotropy, and quantify the number of affine pieces attainable by the lifted network and derive reduced architectures for isotropic energies. Numerical examples illustrate stress-based regression and approximation of the symmetric polyconvex envelope of a double-well potential. Symmetric polyconvexity is guaranteed by construction, while the accuracy of the fitted energies and envelopes is assessed numerically.

We study spectral sequences as an obstruction theory to deforming cohomology classes via the Rees construction. A filtered complex is interpreted as an equivariant family over the affine line, in which higher spectral sequence differentials arise as obstructions to lifting cohomology classes through infinitesimal neighborhoods of the special fibre. This leads to various geometric and module-theoretic degeneration criteria. We give various applications to $\mathrm{Ext}$ spectral sequences for complex Lagrangians and the formality results of Melani-Rubió amongst others. For double complexes, we revisit the Khovanov-Qi decomposition on the Rees side and introduce a two-parameter Rees construction over the affine plane. The higher differentials of the two associated spectral sequences correspond to torsion modules supported on the thickened coordinate axes. We obtain degeneration criteria in terms of these modules and an intrinsic characterisation of the $\partial\bar\partial$-lemma.

These zeros form a $Γ(1)$-invariant set that descends to the modular orbifold $Y(1)$. This turns out to be the maximum of the negative logarithm of the modulus of finitely many linear functions supported on the relevant geodesic segments, and we finish the proof by showing that the associated measure has no atoms and making explicit, on each open segment, the distributional Laplacian of this function in terms of the argument measure. The non-atomicity allows us to conclude a sublinear growth rate in the weight for the total order of all Eisenstein series at a given point in $Y(1)$, and weak convergence also of the non-orbifold measure to the same limit.
Affine and cyclotomic Brauer categorification via $\imath$-Kac--Moody $2$-categories: the integral type $\operatorname{AIII}$ case
Mengmeng Gao; Hebing Rui; Linliang Song; Jun Wu

Continuing our work on the half-integral case, we construct generalized nilpotent $2$-representations of the integral quasi-split type $\operatorname{AIII}$ $\imath$-Kac--Moody $2$-category from affine Brauer actions with dot spectrum exactly $\mathbb Z$ on locally Schurian $\mathbb C$-linear categories. Conversely, nilpotent $2$-representations on such categories yield affine Brauer actions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb Z$. At the fixed vertex $0$, we directly define corrected generators and verify the nil-Brauer and mixed relations. For $\mathbf u$-admissible integral parameters at arbitrary positive level, we prove an isomorphism between the locally unital algebras of the cyclotomic Brauer category and a cyclotomic quotient of the principal $2$-representation. This gives compatible $\mathbb Z$-gradings on the category and its endomorphism algebras, providing a Brauer analogue of the graded realization of type $A$ cyclotomic Hecke algebras. Over algebraically closed fields of odd characteristic $p$, we also obtain both constructions with spectrum contained in $\mathbb F_p$, for the mixed affine datum restricted to its spectral weight subgroup.
Numerical approximation of probabilistically strong solutions to the stochastic harmonic map heat flow
Robert Lasarzik; Stefan Metzger; Maximilian E. V. Reiter

We study the stochastic harmonic map heat flow into the sphere driven by a Stratonovich noise term that formally preserves the spherical constraint by construction. Starting from a fully discrete, implementable numerical scheme, we prove its convergence to the novel solution concept of probabilistically strong, analytically energy-variational solutions. This yields the first existence result for probabilistically strong solutions in the three-dimensional setting on the prescribed stochastic basis. In addition, we establish weak-strong uniqueness and illustrate our theoretical findings with numerical experiments.
Contextual Decision Making: Predictive or Generative
L. Jeff Hong; Weihuan Huang; Xinyao Li

Contextual decision making uses observed covariates to guide decisions under uncertainty. Two natural approaches are predict-then-optimize (PtO), which learns the conditional expected objective, and generate-then-optimize (GtO), which learns conditional uncertainty and optimizes using generated scenarios. We study when each approach is preferable by examining how the choice of learning target affects statistical accuracy and optimization tractability. Although PtO learns a narrower target, our regret bounds show how differences in smoothness can offset GtO's additional dimensional burden. Exploiting smoothness also raises an optimization tradeoff: within the class of nonnegative-weight PtO methods studied, a lower bound limits the gains from additional smoothness, while more flexible methods may introduce signed weights and lose the guarantee of preserving convexity. GtO preserves scenario-wise convexity, but requires learning a richer object and generating scenarios for optimization. Synthetic experiments and a real case study illustrate how these tradeoffs vary with data availability and problem structure. Together with the scope for reusing a model across tasks, our findings provide practical guidance for choosing between the approaches without identifying a universal winner.
New approaches to the Erdős Distinct Subset Sums Problem

We present a new method of reproving the best known lower bound of the Erdős distinct subset sums problem. Although our lower bound is asymptotically the same as in Dubroff, Fox and Xu, it is slightly better for the case when \(n\) is odd. Besides, we also provide a new lower bound on the second largest element \(a_{n-1}\).
Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable. We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers.
On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices

For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.
Local rigidity for the sharp Nash inequality

Let $V$ be a nonempty relatively compact open subset of a smooth Riemannian manifold $(M^n,g)$ without boundary. We prove that $C_{\mathrm N}(V,g)\ge C_{\mathrm N}(\mathbb R^n)$ and $\int_V \mathrm{Sc}_g dμ_g\ge0$ imply $\mathrm{Rm}_g=0$ on $V$, where $C_{\mathrm N}$ denotes the optimal constant in the Nash inequality and $\mathrm{Sc}_g$ denotes the scalar curvature. This improves an earlier rigidity result of Druet, Hebey, and Vaugon [Int. Math. Res. Not. (1999), no. 14, 735--779].
Biderivations of Null-Filiform and Filiform Zinbiel Algebras

A biderivation of an algebra is a bilinear map which is a derivation in each argument. We describe all biderivations of finite-dimensional complex null-filiform and filiform Zinbiel algebras. For the n-dimensional null-filiform algebra, every biderivation is determined by an arbitrary value at its generating pair; the space of biderivations has dimension n and consists entirely of symmetric maps. For the three standard filiform families, we give explicit bases and determine their symmetric and skew-symmetric parts. We also treat all filiform algebras of dimensions at most four, including the exceptional families not covered by the classification in dimensions at least five. A three-dimensional algebra admits a three-dimensional space of skew-symmetric biderivations, two of which have values outside its annihilator. Up to isomorphism, it is the unique complex filiform Zinbiel algebra with this property. The proofs use generators, annihilator-valued maps, a truncated polynomial model, and conformal endomorphisms of bilinear forms.
Distortion-Rate Outage Probability for Non-ergodic Classes of Sources
Dongmin Park; Ibrahim Abou-Faycal; Razane Tajeddine

The concept of outage has been commonly used in the context of transmission rates over non-ergodic channels. For those channels, one channel state or realization may be encountered for the whole transmission duration of a codeword. In the dual setting of source coding and whenever source statistics are not ergodic, we define in this work the notion of outage; we discuss related properties, consider the special case of compact source classes and provide examples.
Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification

We study squared-error estimation when a nuisance parameter is unidentified on a submodel but affects a target that vanishes there. For models with higher-order profile expansions, we give sufficient conditions under which the largest critical-path minimax risk is the exact asymptotic minimax risk over the full parameter space. An efficient observable feature, negligible calibration error and stable recovery yield one estimator attaining the leading constant uniformly, with the profile coordinates unknown. The estimator uses calibration estimates, a local feature mean and an empirical recovery feature. The constant is expressed through a bounded-normal decision problem. We verify the conditions in two models. In centered Gaussian logistic errors-in-variables regression with one surrogate and two unknown variances, we determine the fifth-order global coefficient risk and its exact constant. A sparse extension separates variance-decomposition uncertainty from direction estimation and specifies when the scalar constant is preserved. In a degree-balanced replicated-network model, we determine the sixth-order global edge-contrast risk when block proportions are unknown. Triangles identify a parameter combination; a bowtie supplies the additional information needed for the contrast.
Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture

We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction. We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module. This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.
StarRTT: An End-to-End Real-Time Framework for Blind Zone-Free RTT Prediction in Starlink LEO Satellite Networks
Jaeyong Lee; Seongjin Jeong; Yusang Park; Hyunho Hwang; Sangmin Han; Wonjae Shin

Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations such as Starlink require frequent handovers due to high orbital velocities, resulting in substantial Round-Trip Time (RTT) fluctuations. Accurate RTT prediction can mitigate these fluctuations, yet it fundamentally relies on continuously updated serving- satellite information. Existing serving-satellite identification methods typically complete identification only at the end of each scheduling cycle, creating an identification blind zone that limits real-time prediction. To overcome this limitation, we develop StarRTT, an end-to-end real-time framework that eliminates the blind zone by integrating per-second serving-satellite identification with RTT prediction. Within this framework, we propose Real-Time Long Short-Term Memory (RT-LSTM), an LSTM-based RTT prediction model designed to capture both non-stationary RTT evolution and time-varying geometric relationships among the serving satellite, user terminal, and gateways. Specifically, a historical LSTM encodes historical RTT observations and real-time serving-satellite and gateway-relative features, while a future LSTM processes Two-Line Element (TLE)-propagated future features of the identified serving satellite up to the next scheduling instant. Under strict real-time back-testing, RT-LSTM achieves a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.405 ms averaged over all 15 prediction horizons and 15 reference time-slot indices, reducing the error by 4.3 %, 11.6 %, and 22.1 % compared with the existing baseline models, LSTM, StarNet, and Attention-based Spatiotemporal Model (ASTM), respectively. Notably, the reduction over LSTM reaches 12.5 % at the scheduling instant, highlighting the benefit of real-time serving-satellite information when recent RTT observations are limited.

Our approach is based on bi-Lagrangian geometry. Building on the work of O.~E.~Barndorff-Nielsen and P.~E.~Jupp~\cite{Barndorff}, we show that a statistical divergence naturally induces a bi-Lagrangian structure, hence a para-Kähler structure. Within this framework, the Riemannian metric $g^D$ and the pair of dual connections $(
abla^D,{}^*
abla^D)$ of Eguchi's construction are induced by the para-Kähler structure: $g^D$ is the restriction to the diagonal of the para-Kähler metric $G$ of signature $(d,d)$, while $
abla^D$ and ${}^*
abla^D$ are obtained, through the two natural projections, from the Bott connections of the two transverse Lagrangian foliations, which are themselves the restrictions of the Levi-Civita connection of $G$ (the Hess, Künneth or bi-Lagrangian connection). This perspective shows that the statistical structure associated with a divergence is not merely the formal outcome of successive differentiations, but the manifestation of an underlying bi-Lagrangian geometry. Our approach thus provides an intrinsic and unified understanding of Eguchi's construction, highlights the connections between information geometry, symplectic geometry and para-Kähler geometry, and opens new research perspectives at the interface of these fields.
Stochastic predator-prey compartment model with cyclic and non-cyclic transition pathways and mortality
Thomas M. Michelitsch; Ayten D. Baher; Michael Bestehorn; Andrzej F. Nowakowski; Alejandro P. Riascos; Bernard A. Collet

We study variants of a stochastic SEIRS-SEID compartmental model incorporating presymptomatic infectiousness and disease-related mortality, with independent compartmental sojourn times drawn from arbitrary distributions, in particular Weibull distributions. We consider a large population of agents that occupy the states (compartments) S (susceptible to infection), E (exposed: infected but asymptomatic during the latency period and already infectious, including diseases with presymptomatic infections), I (infected and infectious, with symptoms), R (recovered, immune, and non-infectious), or D (dead). From a stochastic perspective, we elucidate the connection between compartmental sojourn-time distributions and the appearance of fractional operators in the evolution equations: fat-tailed compartment waiting-time distributions necessarily lead to fractional derivatives. For cyclic transition pathways we obtain an explicit expression for the expected number of infection cycles that an agent survives. Our model is validated by a combined Monte Carlo -- Runge -- Kutta simulation scheme and random-walk simulations on Barabasi-Albert networks. It has cross-disciplinary applications beyond epidemiology, including wildfire spreading, certain classes of chemical reactions, population dynamics, finance, economics, and biology.
