Building on fixed-movement estimates, we obtain quantitative normal approximations for an empirically normalized statistic by controlling its random denominator and the independent movement clock. A permutation comparison preserves the diffusive Kolmogorov rate, while variance matching permits third-order Zolotarev estimates. We also derive self-normalized Cramér-type moderate deviations. For regularly varying step-size tails, we obtain uniform precise large deviations and establish the necessity of the diffusive and critical threshold orders. Further applications of the clock representation yield large deviation principles for Weibull-type and light-tailed step sizes, and a precise light-tailed expansion in the balanced case.
Conditional Reflected Backward Stochastic Differential Equations

In this paper, we introduce a new type of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (reflected BSDEs), referred to as conditional reflected BSDEs, in which the conditional expectation of the Y-component of the solution with respect to a given sub-σ-algebra appears in both the generator and the obstacle. Under a Lipschitz condition on the loss function with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution for both the case of Lipschitz generator and the case of quadratic generator, bounded terminal value and bounded loss function. When the generator has quadratic growth and the terminal value and loss function are unbounded, we establish the uniqueness with the help of θ-method. Finally, a penalization approximation scheme holds under an additional monotonicity structure imposed on the generator and the loss function, without any restriction on the Lipschitz constants of the loss function.
Mixed sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values with restricted indices

We study arithmetic sums of infinite multiple zeta-star values subject to upper or lower bounds on their indices. Let $η(\mathcal D_q)$ be the image, under the zeta-star correspondence, of the admissible infinite index sequences with all indices at most $q$, and let $\overline{η(\mathcal T_p)}$ be the closure of the image of the sequences with all indices at least $p$. We prove that $η(\mathcal D_q)+\overline{η(\mathcal T_p)}$ is an interval exactly when $p\leq q$; in that case it is $[ζ^\star(\{q\}^{\infty})+1,\infty)$. We also show that sums of two upper-bounded sets are half-lines, even with different bounds, whereas sums of two lower-bounded sets are never intervals. The proofs combine a uniform product estimate with natural gap constructions. Lateral thickness handles the diagonal case $p=q\geq3$, while a non-strict local bridge--gap criterion treats $p=q=2$ directly. Compact truncations and explicit omitted intervals yield the remaining assertions.
Optimal Dividends and Proactive Capital Injection over a Finite Horizon
Ran Xu; Zuo Quan Xu; Xueying Zhang

We study a finite-horizon dividend and capital-injection problem for a Brownian surplus process with time-varying financing costs. Under a classical passive-injection policy, capital is supplied only at the solvency boundary. Anticipated increases in financing costs may instead make it optimal to inject capital while reserves remain strictly positive. We characterize this proactive financing mechanism through an auxiliary Dynkin game for the marginal value of liquidity. The game identifies an endogenous lower financing boundary and an upper dividend boundary, and yields restrictions on intervention timing and comparative statics with respect to the financing-cost path. Under a regular intervention-band condition, we recover the control value by spatial integration of the game value and verify that the optimal policy is two-sided reflection between the two boundaries. We establish this condition for a canonical class with decreasing marginal dividend rewards, increasing marginal financing costs, and a compatible piecewise affine terminal marginal value. Strictly decreasing financing costs eliminate positive-reserve financing contact and reduce the marginal game to a one-player stopping problem. Numerical examples illustrate the optimal policies and the effects of anticipated financing conditions on shareholder value and intervention thresholds.
Rigidity of Pseudoconvex Neighborhoods and Ohsawa--Takegoshi Extension

Let $Y$ be a holomorphic section of a holomorphic submersion with one-dimensional fibers over a connected compact complex manifold. Assuming that its normal bundle is unitary flat, we prove that $Y$ admits a fundamental system of locally pseudoconvex neighborhoods if and only if it admits a holomorphic tubular neighborhood. The proof uses the sharp Ohsawa--Takegoshi extension theorem. As an application, we rule out such neighborhood systems in Ueda's example of class $(γ)$.
Pappus configurations in the Hall plane
Stefano Lia; John Sheekey; Geertrui Van de Voorde

In this paper, we investigate Pappus configurations in the finite affine Hall plane. In particular, we show that for any two lines $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and for any triple of points on $\ell_1$ there is a triple of points on $\ell_2$ that are contained in a Pappus configuration, thus improving on the results of [F. Lazebnik and L. Leshock. On Pappus configurations in Hall planes. Des. Codes Cryptogr. 90 (2022), 1203--1219.].

We classify isolated singularities of nonpositive, $k$-admissible classical solutions to $k$-Hessian equations without radial symmetry assumptions. For $1\le k<n/2$, we consider $F_k[u]=(-u)^p$ with $1<p\le nk/(n-2k)$. Below the Serrin exponent, we obtain fundamental-solution asymptotics and characterize removability by the vanishing of the leading coefficient. At the Serrin exponent, we determine the exact logarithmic correction and its universal coefficient for every nonremovable singularity. In the critical dimension $k=n/2$, we establish logarithmic asymptotics and a removability criterion for $F_k[u]=f(x,u,\nabla u)$ with continuous sources satisfying $0\le f(x,s,ξ)\le C|ξ|^\ell e^{-αs}$, where $α>0$ and $0\le\ell<n$. The proofs combine Hessian-measure compactness, Wolff-potential estimates, a global Bôcher theorem, and a bounded-variation analysis of spherical extrema.
Refined Cramér-type moderate deviations by Stein's method under dependence
Hui-Lin Liu; Song-Hao Liu; Dawei Lu

In this paper, we establish refined Cramér-type moderate deviations for dependent random variables at any fixed order $m\geq3$. Combining higher-order Stein identities with exponential tilting, we obtain cumulant-corrected tail approximations with explicit error bounds for boundedly supported kernels. Our main application gives a fourth-order expansion under bounded local dependence, reaching an $O(n^{3/10})$ deviation range under standard normalization with fixed dependence parameters. It improves on previous work in both deviation range and applicability, and also covers bounded $m$-dependent sequences without an independent-base representation. Further applications to the generalized combinatorial central limit theorem and the Curie-Weiss model also extend some earlier results under permutation and mean-field dependence.
Widom asymptotics for spatial compressions of Schrödinger spectral projections

We establish a Widom trace formula for spatial compressions of exact spectral projections of semiclassical Schrödinger operators. The potential is smooth near a compact classically allowed region, and the observation domain lies strictly inside that region. For every continuous spectral function with positive power decay at both endpoints, we obtain a trace formula at scale $h^{1-n}\log h^{-1}$ whose coefficient separates into a boundary integral and a universal spectral functional. This yields the exact von Neumann and Rényi entanglement asymptotics for every fixed positive order, and proves their universal ratios to the particle-number variance. The proof combines commutator estimates in every fixed positive Schatten class with a local trace formula obtained from a boundary-adapted normal form and a Hardy model. In dimensions $n\ge2$, a positive partition and the known variance asymptotic control the grazing contribution; in one dimension all boundary Fermi points are transverse. A harmonic-oscillator counterexample shows that continuity and weighted integrability alone are insufficient for the trace formula.
Inviscid Limit Problem for Radially Symmetric Stationary States of Viscous and Heat-Conductive Ideal Gas

We study the zero-viscosity limit of radially symmetric stationary solutions for the inflow and outflow problems for a viscous and heat-conductive polytropic ideal gas in the exterior of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \geq 3$), under prescribed boundary and far-field conditions. The far-field velocity is assumed to be zero, and the solutions are considered in a sufficiently small neighborhood of the far-field state. In the zero-viscosity limit, the viscous terms disappear from the momentum equation, while the heat-conduction term remains in the energy equation. For the outflow problem, we prove that the viscous stationary solution converges uniformly to the corresponding stationary solution of the heat-conductive inviscid system, with convergence rate $O(μ)$. For the inflow problem, a boundary layer appears near the inner boundary. We show that the viscous stationary solution is uniformly approximated by the superposition of the limiting stationary solution and a boundary-layer profile. Here, the boundary layer appears only for the density and velocity, whereas no boundary-layer appears for the temperature. Moreover, for any $α\in (0,1)$, the approximation error is of order $O(μ^α)$.
Construction of Galois modules describing ideal class groups and applications to Iwasawa theory

For a finite Galois extension of number fields, the ideal class groups of intermediate fields do not behave well under taking Galois coinvariants in general. In this paper, we construct a Galois module whose Galois coinvariants explicitly describe the ideal class groups of the intermediate fields. As an application, we demonstrate how this construction naturally yields some results in classical Iwasawa theory.
Pontryagin-Thom, $π_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors

Segal computed $π_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(Γ_k)$ of finite étale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(Γ_k)\toπ_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $π_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $π_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $Γ_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.
Time-periodic solutions of an SIS epidemic model
Fang Li; Pengfei Song; Kexin Zhang; Maolin Zhou

We prove the existence of strictly positive, nonstationary time-periodic solutions for the spatially heterogeneous SIS epidemic model with standard incidence. On a bounded interval with Neumann boundary conditions, we construct smooth, time-independent transmission and recovery rates satisfying \(β(x)>γ(x)>0\), together with diffusion coefficients \(d_I>d_S>0\), such that periodic solutions coexist with the unique endemic equilibrium for every prescribed positive total population. Thus, pointwise dominance of transmission over recovery does not ensure convergence to equilibrium. Our approach combines an inverse construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium with a coefficient path that preserves both the equilibrium and the pointwise inequalities. A change in the number of unstable eigenvalues along this path yields small-amplitude periodic solutions through a center-manifold reduction and a generalized Hopf bifurcation argument. The proof uses an AI-assisted construction of an unstable endemic equilibrium under the pointwise condition $β>γ>0$.
General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $ω$-Chains

Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $ω$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $ω$-chains. We then introduce the lifting property for posets with no maximal element and show that a poset can be partitioned into $ω$-chains if and only if it has the lifting property.
Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models

We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.

A learner's present predictions do not fully determine how it will learn next. We study the dynamics of hidden learning structure through two related operations. Fiber Regulation Theory (FRT) describes protected repair of existing function and the learning responses left available after repair. Fiber Acquisition Theory (FAT) describes the formation and renewal of trainable structure, distinguishing neutral installation, access to a learning signal, and additional functional directions. The two operations also constrain one another. A repair obligation can force a change in a learning channel, while acquired features can make new protected repairs feasible or reduce the minimum coefficient cost of existing ones. We characterize joint admissibility and response reachability, and give a finite supervised-learning construction in which the two operations together produce a favorable response absent from either operation alone. We implement protected head repair and fixed-capacity LoRA renewal in Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, under replay and output distillation. Across two training trajectories differing in seed and within-task example order, the coordinated policy achieves higher teacher-forced Exact than either separate policy in all four comparisons. It also has the lowest macro NLL under both learning rules on the second trajectory. The implementations realize structure-conditioned self-regulation within specified information and action constraints: accessible state readouts and arrived evidence guide repairs and structural renewals, and ordinary learning continues from the modified state.
Ramified convolution and monodromy bases for symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras

We realize the positive enveloping algebra of a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra by convolution on a ramified preprojective species over $\mathbb{C}((t))$. The coefficients are alternating traces of tame monodromy on representation flag varieties. We prove the relative Serre relations modulo classes induced from proper finite extensions. Monodromy evaluations at compatible generic points of the central reductions yield an integral basis respecting the top and socle crystals. The basis is unchanged by scaling the symmetrizer, induces bases of integrable representation lattices, and agrees with Lusztig's semicanonical basis when the Cartan matrix is symmetric. We prove the acyclic convolution conjecture of Geiß--Leclerc--Schröer for all symmetrizable Cartan matrices and all positive integral symmetrizers. Finally, we give a counterexample to the Support Conjecture of Geiß--Leclerc--Schröer and compute a ramified lift for which monodromy restores the Serre relation.
Proofs of Li, Wang and Guo's conjectures on (signless) Laplacian spectral radius
Hongzhang Chen; Jianxi Li; Xiaoyun Lv

Let $μ(G)$ and $q(G)$ be the Laplacian and signless Laplacian spectral radii of a graph $G$. Li, Wang and Guo (2026) conjectured that, if $H$ with $|V(H)|\geq 1$ is an induced subgraph of a graph $G$, then $μ(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}μ(H_v^t)$ and $q(G)\le\max\limits_{v\in V(H)}q(H_v^t)$, where $t=e(G)-e(H)$ and $H_v^t$ is the graph obtained from $H$ by adding $t$ pendant edges to $v\in V(H)$. We prove this conjecture by establishing a spectral comparison theorem for a broader family of positive semidefinite graph matrices which includes the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. We also characterize all equality cases for the prescribed subgraph $H$ with $e(H)\geq 1$ and $t\geq 1$.
Non-trivial intersecting families for direct products
Jian Wang; Biao Wu; Huajun Zhang

A family of sets is intersecting if any two of its sets intersect, and non-trivial intersecting if there is not any element which appears in every set of the family. The study of intersection problems (or Erdős-Ko-Rado problems) on families of sets is one of the most important topics in extremal combinatorics. A natural extension of the Erdős-Ko-Rado problem in direct products setting was introduced by Frankl, and developed by Alon and Katona et al. In 2018, Kwan, Sudakov and Vieira [J. Combin. Theory, Ser. A 156 (2018), 44--60] determine the maximum size of a non-trivial intersecting direct product family under the assumption that the sizes of all parts are sufficiently large relative to the set sizes in all parts. Meanwhile, they raised the question of whether this result holds for the size of each part which depends only on its corresponding set size, and the question of characterizing the extremal families. In the present paper, we answere these two questions. Furthermore, the bounds on the size of each part in our result are best possible.1
Every tournament of dichromatic number $10 k^2$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood has dichromatic number more than $k$

The dichromatic number of a tournament is the minimum number of colors needed to color the vertices so that no directed cycle is monochromatic. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2025) asked whether every tournament with dichromatic number $2k$ has a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number at least $k$. We answer their question negatively by finding an example with dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$. Furthermore, this quadratic bound is tight up to a constant factor; we show that for every integer $k \geq 1$, every tournament of dichromatic number $Ω(k^2)$ contains a vertex whose out-neighborhood induces a subtournament of dichromatic number more than $k$. This improves the previous best bound $\mathcal{O}(k^2\log k)$ due to Colinot and Newman (2026). To show this, we prove that every tournament of fractional dichromatic number $c$ has a dominating set of size at most $5c-1$. The proof uses Brouwer's fixed point theorem.
Stability for the adjoint Finner inequality and improved lower bounds on the $k$-plane transform

We establish stability properties of near-extremisers for the Loomis--Whitney inequality and its adjoint, presenting our results in the general framework of Finner. In particular, we show that a function nearly achieves equality in the adjoint Finner inequality if and only if it is near to being an indicator function of a cartesian product. As an application, we obtain new lower bounds for the classical $k$-plane transform on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$, modestly improving those obtained recently by Tao and the first author. We also present an alternative approach to such improvements based on stability in the setting of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality and the theory of fusion frames. We conclude with an interpretation of our $k$-plane transform estimates as adjoint forms of the continuous Brascamp--Lieb inequalities.
Neural Vector Field Transformations: Learning the Flow of Autonomous Systems by Conjugation to Explicitly Integrable Reference Flows

We represent the flow map of an autonomous ODE $\dot x=f(x)$ as a conjugate $Φ_t=F_θ^{-1}\circΨ_t\circ F_θ$ of an explicitly integrable reference flow $Ψ_t$ by an invertible neural network $F_θ$, the neural vector field transformation. The representation is an exact flow for every parameter value and inherits the phase portrait of the reference. A $C^1$ conjugacy preserves the eigenvalues of equilibria, the periods and Floquet multipliers of periodic orbits and the frequency-amplitude relation of centers, so these invariants must be learnable parameters of $Ψ$. We give parametrized reference flows with explicit integral curves, show that an action-angle reference is Hamiltonian only if its learnable frequency map is a gradient, and show that an orientation-preserving $F_θ$ cannot reverse the rotation sense of the reference, so it must be fixed before training. The main contribution is a training recipe: a push-forward equation residual made relative to $|f|$ and sampled log-uniformly in $|x|$ around an equilibrium, with the anchors $F_θ(0)=0$, $DF_θ(0)=I$; a symplectic transformation with the gradient-form frequency map; and invariants initialized from the field or data. With it the full spectrum of a three- and a six-dimensional nonlinear sink is recovered (eigenvalue deviation $8.3\times10^{-3}$ and relative error 2.3%, three seeds each), and the action-angle variables of a four-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian system with frequency maps and actions correct to a median of 0.09% and 0.22%, and an exactly symplectic flow. On a dispersive system a time-input network is eight times more accurate inside its horizon, and the data-only identification of the Van der Pol oscillator yields a conjugacy on the data region with the Floquet exponent 17% off; an oracle run with the true invariants frozen attributes this to the expressivity of $F_θ$.
Encoding Trees: A Method for Producing a Variable-Length Prefix Code From Sets of Arbitrary Size

In this work we formalize a new class of binary trees called encoding trees. We extend this structure in two ways, through labelling to create the class of labelled encoding trees, and pruning to create the class of pruned encoding trees. We discuss how these two extensions can be combined to create the the class of pruned labelled encoding trees. Using the supplementary results that we prove about these classes of trees, we construct a code that uses pruned labelled encoding trees to convert a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets to a binary string. We prove that this code is a variable-length prefix code that can process any valid string of symbols from the given sequence of non-empty sets. Furthermore, we construct a code from the class of pruned labelled encoding trees that goes in the opposite direction, from binary strings to a string of symbols from a sequence of non-empty sets of arbitrary symbols. We prove that this code is also a variable-length prefix code that can process any binary string of any length, provided that the sequence of non-empty sets is sufficiently long. We provide an equation that establishes the minimum sequence length to encode any binary string of a given length, based on that length.

We consider Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(s, χ)$ where $χ$ is a quadratic character to modulus $q$. We show that for $χ$ even (resp. odd) $L(σ, χ)\neq 0$ for all $σ>0$ provided that $q\leq 10^{9}$ (resp. $q\leq 10^{10})$. In particular, this result rules out Siegel--Landau zeros for such $L$-functions. Combined, these results improve on previous work by nearly four orders of magnitude. We also list some applications of this work.
Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds

A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.
On the Number of Iterations in a Kruskal-Type Process

Motivated by the Kruskal counting procedure, this paper investigates a combinatorial elimination process defined on a deck consisting of $m$ copies of each value $1,2,\ldots,n$. Starting from an arbitrary arrangement of the $mn$ cards, the process repeatedly removes a number of consecutive cards equal to the value of the first remaining card. This generates a sequence of elimination steps whose length determines $T$, representing the total number of iterations required to exhaust the deck. The main objective of this paper is to analyze an upper bound $σ(m,n)$ for $T$, valid for every initial configuration of the deck, and to show that this bound is attained by a specific configuration.
A logarithmic regularity criterion for the axisymmetric Navier-Stokes equations

For axisymmetric solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb R^3$, the circulation $Γ=ru^θ$ obeys a maximum principle, and the resulting a priori bound on $Γ$ is scale-invariant. Nonetheless, the global regularity problem remains completely open. The sharpest known regularity criteria in terms of the circulation are slightly subcritical, namely $|Γ|\lesssim(\log r^{-1})^{-k}$ near the symmetry axis; Lei and Zhang proved regularity for $k=2$, and Wei later lowered the exponent to $k=3/2$. In this note, we strengthen the criterion further to $k=5/4$. The argument follows the usual route of energy estimates for the quantities $ω^r/r$ and $ω^θ/r$, but now with a sharper bound on the vortex stretching term in the equation for $ω^r/r$, in which the loss is proportional only to the square root of the number of scales between the inner vortex core and the far field.
Affine $G$-multibiquandle modules for colored links I: representability of coloring functors and color-profile polynomials

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with identity, let $G$ be an abelian group, and fix $u\in R[G]^\times$. For each component-labeled oriented link diagram $(D,σ)$, we construct a finitely presented $R[G]$-module $M_u(D,σ;R[G])$ with a universal affine coloring $U_{D,σ}$. Every affine coloring with values in an $R[G]$-module factors uniquely through $U_{D,σ}$ by a module homomorphism. Thus the module represents the affine coloring functor. Each specified colored Reidemeister move induces a unique module isomorphism compatible with coloring transport, and the module isomorphism class is a colored-link invariant. The representing modules and universal colorings commute with arbitrary scalar extension, without a flatness assumption. For classical links, simultaneous rescaling of the component labels removes the common deformation unit. For any multibiquandle, associated-biquandle colorings decompose into fibers indexed by component labelings. For finite targets and palettes, we define a color-profile polynomial recording the joint distribution of fiber sizes and numbers of palette labels used, and prove its invariance under oriented link isotopy. In the affine case, the representing modules determine these fibers, and their specialized dimensions determine the coloring counts over finite fields. The color-profile polynomial is not determined, in general, by the full unweighted distribution of coloring-fiber sizes. It therefore retains information beyond the associated-biquandle coloring count.
A Jump-Modified Wasserstein Gradient Flow for Maximum Mean Discrepancy with Energy Kernels
Ansh Desai; Jason Liu; Srujan Roplekar; Matthew Rosenzweig

We study a jump-modified Wasserstein gradient flow of the squared maximum mean discrepancy generated by the energy kernels $K(z)=-|z|^q$, $0<q<2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$ as well as the one-dimensional range $1\le q<2$. Under subcritical density and finite-moment assumptions, we prove global well-posedness. The added jumps transfer mass toward smaller values of the first variation and dissipate the same MMD energy as the transport term. Under our hypotheses on the target and jump rates, every Borel probability measure with finite MMD energy and zero jump dissipation is equal to the target. Combining this rigidity with compactness and a second-moment identity yields convergence to the target from finite-second-moment data, without additional uniform-in-time density or moment assumptions. We also construct a global collision-free particle process whose energy is nonincreasing along each path. A quantitative mean-field estimate applies to general initial empirical approximations, including deterministic configurations; propagation of chaos for exchangeable data and long-time target approximation follow as consequences.
On Finite Groups with Element Order Set of Width 3
Eric Min; Chloe So; Yong Yang; Eddy Zhang; Mengtian Zhang; Cody Zhou

We study finite groups in which every element order is divisible by at most three distinct primes. We determine the possible nonabelian composition factors, prove that a nonabelian simple group with this property has at most $15$ prime divisors in its order, and deduce that $ρ(G)\leq192$ for every finite group $G$ with $α(G)\leq3$.
Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion

We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.
Mutual transformations of arbitrary ternary qubit trees by Clifford gates

It is shown that ternary qubit trees with the same number of nodes can be transformed by the naturally defined sequence of Clifford gates into each other or into standard representation as one-dimensional chain corresponding to Jordan-Wigner transform.
Deterministic Causal Quantization with Representative States and Bounded Error

We study deterministic causal quantization with pathwise error at most $\varepsilon$, using $ω$ shared representatives updated from transmitted addresses alone. For a midpoint realization with first-in, first-out replacement, we compare address entropy rates with process $\varepsilon$-entropy, the least entropy rate of any block quantizer meeting the same constraint. From $\varepsilon$-separated initialization, the gap is at most two bits per sample for every stationary source with finite scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy, without density, independence or mixing assumptions. A causal address-tree argument extends this comparison to any synchronized quantizer with cell overlap $m$, giving $\log_2 m$ bits. Lattice initialization with consistent boundary ownership realizes uniform grids with sharp one-bit scalar and process comparisons. Under an entropy condition and finite Fisher information rate $J$, the gap is at most $2J\varepsilon^2/(π^2\ln 2)$; general initializations add a term of order $ω\varepsilon\sqrt{J}$. The scalar grid estimate gives a nonasymptotic form of Rényi's theorem. Since a grid is causal, the price of causality is at most $\min\{1,2J\varepsilon^2/(π^2\ln 2)\}$ bits per sample, versus the high-resolution squared-error loss $\tfrac12\log_2(πe/6)$. These bounds certify $\varepsilon$-entropy brackets for autoregressive Laplace and Gaussian sources. For memoryless sources, the optimal causal rate equals the scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy. For a stationary process on finitely many $2\varepsilon$-separated centers, adding independent uniform noise of width $2\varepsilon$ gives exact Shannon lower-bound equality at every block length, attained by storing those centers. This includes histograms with finitely many bins. Storing two non-lattice centers beats every uniform grid of the same cell width by half a bit per sample.
Three BMO-type Spaces Characterizing Chord--Arc Curves
In this note, we introduce three BMO-type spaces on a locally rectifiable Jordan curve and prove that it is a chord-arc curve if and only if these spaces coincide with equivalent norms.
Second largest eigenvalue thresholds for the vertex-connectivity of regular graphs

Let $λ_2(G)$ and $κ(G)$ denote the second largest adjacency eigenvalue and the vertex-connectivity of a graph $G$. For a non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$, Fiedler's inequality $λ_2(G)\ge r-κ(G)$ shows that $λ_2(G)<r-t$ forces $κ(G)\ge t+1$. The best such bound is known for $t=1$, by Zhang and Wang, and for $t=2$ with $r\ge4$, by Zhang. In this paper, for every $r\ge3$ and every integer $t$ with $2\le t\le r-1$, we give an upper bound on $λ_2(G)$ that forces an $r$-regular graph $G$ to satisfy $κ(G)\ge t+1$, and we determine exactly when this bound is best possible. For $\frac{r+2}{2}\le t\le r-1$, Fiedler's bound $r-t$ is already best possible. For $2\le t<\frac{r+2}{2}$, it is replaced by one of two explicit algebraic numbers, and the sign of an explicit polynomial $W(r,t)$, which never vanishes, decides which one applies. Each of the two numbers is attained exactly when $(r,t)$ satisfies an explicit arithmetic condition, and every extremal graph then consists of two cliques and an independent cut of size $t$. In this range our bound also improves a bound of Zhang that holds for every such $t$.

Let $\text{inv}(T)$ be the inversion index of the tournament $T$. Answering a question of Behague, we show that $\text{inv}(T_1\to T_2)=\text{inv}(T_1)+\text{inv}(T_2)$ does not even hold asymptotically.
Optimal Rényi and Logarithmic Additive Functional Entropy Estimation

We characterize the minimax sample complexity of estimating Rényi entropy from independent samples on an alphabet of size at most $k$, when the known order $α>1$ may vary with $k$. For every fixed additive accuracy $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and success probability $2/3$, we prove matching bounds with constants independent of $k$ and $α$. For $1<α<\log k$, the rate is $Θ_\varepsilon(αk^{1-1/α}X_α(k,\varepsilon))$, where a monotone scalar inequality defines $X_α$ at noninteger orders. The bounds remain uniform as the order approaches one or an integer, or grows with the alphabet. Integer orders below $\log k$ have rate $Θ_\varepsilon(αk^{1-1/α})$; orders at least $\log k$ and min-entropy have rate $Θ_\varepsilon(k\log k)$. We extend the analysis to logarithms of positive additive functionals. For every fixed continuous $f$ satisfying $f(0)=0$, $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$, and $f(x)\sim ax^r$ at zero, with $a>0$ and $r>1$, estimating $-β^{-1}\log\sum_i f(p_i)$ at fixed accuracy, for fixed $β>0$, has sample complexity $Θ(k^{1-1/r})$ for integer $r$ and $Θ(k/\log k)$ otherwise. A replication reduction preserves the sampling experiment and transfers the rates for powers. Smooth flat functions show that regularity alone does not determine the complexity. The upper bound combines polynomial approximation, Gamma count statistics, and an independent pilot, with a global affine correction near order one. The lower bound uses interpolation to construct positive mean-one priors and controls their distinguishability and entropy separation after normalization. Exact count-variance identities and weighted approximation duality connect the two arguments.
Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds

We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients. Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls. For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.
Diffusion Sensitivity Geometry and Strong Duality for Optimal Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs

Existing approaches to differential privacy in diffusion models rely on loose sensitivity bounds and isotropic Gaussian noise, leading to unnecessary estimation error. We develop a framework for the optimal privacy-utility tradeoff of ideal diffusion denoisers, replacing conservative bounds with exact sensitivity characterizations and provably optimal noise calibration. First, we show that worst-case sensitivity over datasets of arbitrary size can be characterized exactly using only two records. For a data domain of size $m$, this reduces the analysis to at most $m(m-1)$ constraints, regardless of dataset size. Our characterization can be arbitrarily tighter than conventional diameter-based sensitivity bounds, revealing potentially unbounded improvements in noise calibration. Second, we obtain exact privacy guarantees for Rényi, approximate, and Gaussian differential privacy, as well as mutual-information privacy for binary records, avoiding the looseness of previous generic privacy conversions. Finally, we show that the minimum achievable weighted mean-squared error can be computed through a semidefinite program and prove strong duality, providing certificates of global optimality.
The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups

This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2πi}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2π(k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).

We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.
From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning

Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to Gács and Körner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.
On the automorphisms of Pick bodies

We determine the biholomorphic automorphisms of the Pick body associated with finitely many distinct points in a Carathéodory hyperbolic domain. Every automorphism is the composition of a common disc automorphism applied to all coordinates and a coordinate permutation preserving the Pick body. The proof uses the quotient Banach algebra of interpolation data, its generalized von Neumann inequality, and the fact that its symmetric part consists precisely of the constant vectors. For nodes in a polydisc, we introduce minimal effective coordinate tuples and identify the admissible permutations with the automorphisms of a lower-dimensional polydisc that preserve the projected node set. This yields a direct-product description of the automorphism group, with one factor equal to the automorphism group of the disc and the other finite. We also give the resulting descriptions for nodes in the disc and the bidisc.
Universality of approximate message passing under a fourth-moment tail condition

We prove state evolution for approximate message passing (AMP) with rectangular random matrices whose entries are independent, centered, and variance-normalized. The row and column dimensions grow with a ratio that converges to a positive finite limit. The entry laws may differ across coordinates and dimensions, and we assume uniform integrability of the fourth powers of the rescaled entries. For entries sampled independently from a fixed law, a finite fourth moment suffices, with no requirement for higher moments. The nonlinearities are continuously differentiable and globally Lipschitz, with bounded continuous first state derivatives. The signal and noise have independent and identically distributed coordinates with finite moments of all orders, and are independent of each other and of the matrix. At every fixed number of iterations, empirical averages of pseudo-Lipschitz functions of order two converge in probability to the limits specified by Gaussian state evolution. These averages include empirical second moments and products of trajectory coordinates. The proof combines an aggregate bound on third derivatives with randomized Lindeberg replacement and operator-norm truncation, without matching third moments or invoking a non-Gaussian universality theorem. We also show that independence of complementary projected components for every deterministic rank-one constraint pair characterizes Gaussian entries. This identifies the limitation of extending Gaussian conditioning identities to independent non-Gaussian matrices. Finally, a variance-profile example shows that average variance normalization alone does not ensure the homogeneous state evolution limits.
Asymptotics of Masur-Veech volume of strata of quadratic differentials with many simple poles

We provide large $n$ asymptotics of the Masur-Veech volumes for strata of quadratic differentials of the form $\mathcal{Q}_g(n,d_1,\dots,d_k,-1^{n+D-4g+4})$, where all positive integers $d_i$ are fixed and $D=d_1+\dots+d_k$. Our formulae are particularly explicit in genus $1$. For the two series of non-varying strata $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,-1^n)$ and $\mathcal{Q}_1(n,1,-1^{n+1})$ we give simple closed formulae for the volumes for any $n$.
Same Gaps, Different Sets: A Survey on Complimentary sets and their Dimensions
Nicolás Angelini; Carlos Cabrelli; Ursula Molter

Let a=\{a_n\} be a non-increasing sequence of positive real numbers adding up to $1$. Cutting out of the unit interval disjoint open gaps of lengths $a_1,a_2,\dots$, one for each term, leaves a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero, and since the gaps can be placed in infinitely many ways, there are infinitely many such sets. We call them the \emph{complementary sets} of $a$ and write $\mathfrak{C}_a$ for the family of all of them. Every set in $\mathfrak{C}_a$ is compact and totally disconnected, and all of them share the same gap lengths; what distinguishes one from another is only the arrangement of the gaps. Among them, the perfect sets are exactly the Cantor sets with those gaps, and they form a distinguished subclass. The central question of this survey is what such a rearrangement can change and what it cannot. The answer depends sharply on the notion of size: the box dimensions are constant on $\mathfrak{C}_a$, while the Hausdorff dimension attains every value in a closed interval whose endpoints are realised by two distinguished members, the Cantor set $C_a$ built by placing the gaps in a Cantor-like pattern, and the countable decreasing rearrangement $D_a$. We survey how this dichotomy persists, and how the roles of $C_a$ and $D_a$ are exchanged, across the intermediate dimensions of Falconer, Fraser and Kempton, the Assouad-type and $Φ$-dimensions, and the Hausdorff and packing $h$-measures associated with a general dimension function; we also describe the almost sure behaviour of a randomly rearranged complementary set, where a sharp threshold in the depth of the scales examined separates two incompatible regimes. A final part restricts attention to the Cantor subclass and turns to the dynamical description of the sets C_a.
We show that homology, puncture, and symplectic polynomials of a pseudo-Anosov map arXiv:1001.5094 are invariants of the mapping class, as well as of the conjugacy class.
On Euler's abelian relation of the web induced by the forgetful maps on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M_{0,n+3}}$: the case when $n$ is even

In a previous paper ${\bf [P1]}$, for every $n\geq 2$, we studied the curvilinear web $\boldsymbol{\mathcal W}_{0,n+3}$ on the moduli space $\boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}$, defined by the $n+3$ forgetful maps $ \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+3}\rightarrow \boldsymbol{\mathcal M}_{0,n+2}$, with particular emphasis on its abelian relations. In particular, when $n$ is even, we conjectured an explicit formula for its Euler abelian relation. This relation is constructed à la Gelfand-MacPherson from an invariant differential form representing the appropriate power of the Euler class of the tautological bundle of the Grassmannian manifold $G_2^{\mathrm{or}}(\mathbf R^{n+3})$ of oriented $2$-planes in $\mathbf R^{n+3}$. In this note, we obtain an explicit antisymmetrized formula for Euler's abelian relation for every even $n\geq 2$, and prove that it coincides, up to the explicit factor $-(n+1)(n+2)/2$, with the formula conjectured in ${\bf [P1]}$, which is therefore established for all even $n$.
On the Road Again: How the $N$-Lane TASEP and Local Reservoirs Drive Jamming in Axonal Transport

Intracellular transport by molecular motors along microtubules is essential for cellular function, particularly in neuronal axons where track disruption drives neurodegenerative disease. We develop an \(N\)-track totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) model where motors reversibly detach into local off-track states. Using mean-field, continuum, and fast-switching approximations, we derive an effective nonlinear transport equation for total motor density. This reduced model retains the classical TASEP phase structure but reveals that increasing \(N\) shifts the boundaries between low-density, high-density, and maximal-current regimes. Crucially, under source-driven boundary conditions reflecting constant cargo production, the entrance density undergoes a saddle-node bifurcation when the production rate exceeds the network's transport capacity, \(N/4\). This triggers persistent cargo accumulation that propagates throughout the domain. Our results establish a physical mechanism by which gradual microtubule degradation drives a transition from efficient transport to jammed pathological states.
The domination number of the $k$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$
Nathaniel Chinman; Antonio Cortijo; Beatrice Pedroni; Ian Seong; Lucy Stenger

This paper is about token graphs and domination number. Let $G=(X,E)$ denote an undirected graph that is connected, with no loops or multiple edges, vertex set $X$, and edge set $E$. Pick a positive integer $k\leq \vert X\vert$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, denoted by $F_k(G)$, is defined as follows. The vertex set $\mathcal{X}$ consists of all $k$-subsets of $X$. Two vertices $x,y\in \mathcal{X}$ are adjacent whenever the symmetric difference of $x$ and $y$ consists of two vertices that form an edge in $E$. In this paper, we compute the exact value for the domination number of $F_2(K_{m,n})$ where $K_{m,n}$ is the complete bipartite graph with parameters $m,n$. We present some bounds for the domination number of $F_k(K_{m,n})$ when $k\geq 3$.
Functional limit theorems for self-interacting random walks
Elena Kosygina; Laure Marêché; Thomas Mountford; Jonathon Peterson

We consider a wide class of nearest neighbor self-interacting random walks on $\mathbb{Z}$ and show that, under mild conditions, their scaling limits at the process level can be uniquely identified and constructed directly from the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem for their local times, i.e., the joint convergence of rescaled local time ``curves'' of the walks stopped at certain stopping times together with the merge and absorption times of these ``curves'' to a concatenation of coalescing reflected-absorbed diffusions and their merge and absorption times. We apply our results to polynomially self-repelling walks introduced and studied in the mid-90s by B. Tóth, and to ``true'' self-avoiding walks with bond repulsion. The first application solves a problem that has been open since Tóth's work: it gives a construction and first properties of a new family of processes, polynomially self-repelling motions, as scaling limits of polynomially self-repelling walks. These processes were simultaneously and independently constructed from flows of correlated powers of Bessel processes by Y. Yu. The second application strengthens an earlier result on convergence of rescaled ``true'' self-avoiding walks to the ``true'' self-repelling motion of B. Tóth and W. Werner, and streamlines its proof. Our results can be thought of as an ``inversion'' of the augmented joint Ray-Knight theorem to get a functional limit theorem for self-interacting random walks.
Boot-AVT: Asymptotically Anytime-Valid Testing with Degenerate U-Statistics via Bootstrap
Jixuan Liu; Long Feng; Liuhua Peng; Zhaojun Wang

Many nonparametric tests are based on $U$-statistics that are degenerate under the null hypothesis. We develop Boot-AVT, a bootstrap procedure for asymptotically anytime-valid testing with these statistics. Using Brownian scaling and time inversion for the limiting Gaussian chaos process, we show that logarithmically penalized maxima over observed and future sample sizes have a common limiting null distribution. A quadratic multiplier bootstrap estimates the corresponding critical values. We also develop Boot-AVT-Multi for joint testing with multiple kernels. For both procedures, we establish uniform consistency of the bootstrap critical values, explicit bounds on size distortion, and asymptotic size $α$ over an unbounded monitoring horizon as the monitoring start tends to infinity. Under fixed alternatives, we derive finite-horizon power bounds and establish power one with finite expected stopping times. Simulation studies evaluate finite-sample size and power in goodness-of-fit, two-sample and independence testing, and real-data analyses compare stopping times.
Lieb-Robinson bounds via the Combes-Thomas estimate
Tali Braester; Haochen Luo; George Peykanu; Sergii Solomakha

This paper studies quantum spin systems: networks of spins coupled by local interactions. The Lieb-Robinson bound predicts that in these systems, information propagates at an essentially finite speed. We produce a new proof of this result. Our approach relies on a spectral bound on entries of resolvents of band matrices, the Combes-Thomas estimate, rather than on the standard path-counting argument.
Kinetic Mean-Field Planning via Schrödinger Bridges: Existence, Penalization, and Consistency Bounds
Erhan Bayraktar; Zhiyan Ding; Hiroaki Horikawa

We study a mean-field planning problem for a swarm of interacting, non-cooperative agents whose dynamics are stochastic and kinetic. The noise acts on the velocity only, and the interaction (of Cucker-Smale type for instance) enters through the drift. For a fixed flow, the problem reduces to a Schrödinger bridge problem, and we first prove the existence of an equilibrium by a Schauder fixed-point argument. Then we replace the hard terminal constraint by a penalty function and show that equilibria of the penalized problems converge, along subsequences, to an equilibrium of the original problem. Since equilibria are not unique in general, we instead quantify the consistency error, which measures how far an equilibrium of the penalized problem is from being an equilibrium of the original one. The rate is of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the relative-entropy penalty. The proof relies on the quantitative stability of entropic optimal transport and on a pointwise linear growth bound on the score of the degenerate reference dynamics, which is of independent interest.
The Octonionic Rational Wave Numbers: Non-Associative Sequence Algebras, Moufang Loops, and Exceptional $G_2$ Symmetries

We generalize discrete rational wave numbers (arXiv:2609.23233) to the octonionic rational wave numbers $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ over Cayley's octonions $\mathbb{O}$. Rather than assuming higher imaginary units, all rational wave number spaces $\mathbb{C}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{H}^\mathbb{Z}, \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ are derived constructively from two scalar primitives: the coordinate advance $E_Z$ and phase calibration $E_{\bar{1}}$. Their closure under pointwise multiplication, inversion, and rational roots generates an infinite divisible Moufang loop on the sequence ring $\mathcal{S}_\mathbb{O} := \mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$, terminating strictly at $\mathbb{O}^\mathbb{Z}$ via sedenionic zero-divisor excision. By Artin's Theorem, pairwise compositions remain strictly associative, whereas three-wave interactions generate an intrinsic non-associative curvature quantified by the associator $[u, v, w] = (uv)w - u(vw)$. We define a real-valued sequence inner product that bypasses the Jordan--von Neumann--Wigner obstruction, establishing the orthonormality of the seven Fano coordinate primitives. We establish three principal theorems: (1) The Invariant Hexagonal Mesh Theorem, proving that cumulative integration exhibits a scale-invariant bifurcation at $n=6$ governed by the root system of $G_2 = \operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{O})$ and its $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ stabilizer subgroup; (2) The Algebraic Phase Jitter Theorem, showing that Catalan parenthesization trees across non-Fano triads produce an irreducible zero-point phase fluctuation, yielding an algebraic origin for vacuum jitter; and (3) The Rational Loop Closure Theorem, proving that rational frequencies select closed finite Moufang sub-loops, while irrational frequencies yield topologically dense, non-closing trajectories. This provides an autonomous, discrete algebraic foundation for non-associative geometry and fundamental physical symmetries.
A Model-Free Continuous-Time RL Algorithm from Discrete-Time Off-Policy Data with End-to-End Guarantees
Chaorui Yao; Yuming Paul Zhang; Lin Yang; Yuhua Zhu

In this paper, we study continuous-time reinforcement learning, where the state follows an unknown stochastic differential equation but only a fixed off-policy batch of discrete-time transitions is available. Standard discrete-time Q-learning becomes problematic as the sampling interval shrinks, because differences between action values vanish. Continuous-time alternatives, such as Deep Advantage Updating and martingale q-learning, preserve the action signal but jointly learn a value function and an action-dependent critic. Building on the PhiBE-Q formulation (arXiv:2606.21925), we develop a model-free PhiBE policy iteration (PhiBE-PI) framework that uses a single state-action critic while preserving the continuous-time action-ranking scale. At each iteration, the framework learns the critic directly from sampled increments and uses it to improve the policy. The same batch is reused throughout, without explicitly estimating the drift or diffusion. We further develop an implementation under linear function approximation and establish a local end-to-end suboptimality guarantee for the learned policy. Our analysis quantifies how errors from time discretization, function approximation, and finite-sample policy evaluation propagate through policy iteration. It accounts for the dependence of successive policies on the reused data, so the guarantee does not require a fresh batch at each iteration. Moreover, we identify a bias-variance trade-off: smaller sampling intervals improve the approximation to the continuous-time problem but can increase statistical error at a fixed sample size. Thus, finer time discretization does not necessarily lead to better policy performance.
Strong gradient absorption and initial decay prevent blow-up

Consider positive classical solutions of the Cauchy problem for $u_t-Δu=u^p-μ|\nabla u|^q$, with sufficiently smooth initial data $u_0$, in the strong absorption regime, namely $q\ge p>1$ and $μ>0$. It has remained a long standing open problem whether finite time blow-up can occur if $u_0$ decays at space infinity. We here solve this problem, showing that the answer in negative. To this end, we establish a novel, universal Bernstein-type gradient estimate, of independent interest, valid only in the range $q\ge p$. Moreover, the decay assumption on $u_0$ turns out to be essentially optimal. Indeed we show that the solution blows up in finite time whenever $u_0$ has a positive limit at infinity, and we determine the blow-up behavior of $u$ at space infinity under an additional assumption.
Mixed finite element methods for a heat-assisted model of sedimentation

A model for the consolidation-sedimentation process incorporating thermal effects is analysed. The model is motivated by novel applications to heat-assisted sedimentation of mineral suspensions. A system of convection-diffusion equations for the concentration and temperature are coupled to flow equations for the volume-average velocity and pressure. The model is supplemented with Dirichlet and mixed boundary conditions. A quasi-stationary approach of the system is analysed by means of a mixed variational formulation, where additional variables such as the pseudostress tensor and variables for the gradient of the temperature and concentration are introduced. The existence and uniqueness of the system is shown making use of the Babu{\v s}ka-Brezzi theory and Banach's fixed-point theorem, under hypotheses of smallness of the data and additional regularity on the solutions. A discrete formulation based on finite element spaces is proposed and analysed, and the existence of solutions is achieved thanks to Brouwer's fixed-point theorem. Additionally, Céa and a priori estimates are derived for the mixed formulation. Finally, numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the performance of the model and to confirm the theoretical rates of convergence.
Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian

We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. We discuss some rigidity consequences, as well as an extension to the higher-order GJMS operators.
"Massive" Conformal Field Theories and application to Nambu-Goto string

I describe the recent progress in understanding diffeomorphism invariant two-dimensional theories with dimensionful parameters which have nevertheless traceless improved energy-momentum tensor and turn out to be conformal invariant. An example is the Liouville theory with the additional four-derivative terms arising from the Nambu-Goto string and telling apart the Nambu-Goto and Polyakov strings. Its exact solution in embedding dimension d=4 is consistent in contrast to the Polyakov string and described by the (4,3) unitary minimal model. Talk at Irina Aref'eva Conference "Perspective Directions in Quantum Field Theory and Superstrings", Moscow 12-17 October 2026.
Algebras with bounded multiplicities of the central cocharacters
Wesley Q. Cota; Luiz H. S. Matos; Breno O. Souza

Let $A$ be an associative PI-algebra over a field of characteristic zero. The central polynomials of $A$ give rise to a sequence $\{χ_n^z(A)\}_{n\geq 1}$ of $S_n$-characters, called its central cocharacters. A natural problem is to understand which algebraic properties of $A$ are imposed by bounds on the multiplicities occurring in the decompositions of these cocharacters into irreducible characters. We prove that these multiplicities are bounded by one if and only if there exist scalars $(α,β)\neq(0,0)$ such that $α[x_1,x_2]x_1+βx_1[x_1,x_2]$ takes values in the center of $A$. This provides a central analogue of the Ananin-Kemer theorem for ordinary cocharacters. We also characterize the algebras whose central cocharacter multiplicities are uniformly bounded.
Hilbert-Kunz multiplicities of powers of ideals and normalized Hilbert coefficients
Tran Nam Trung; Hoang Le Truong

We give negative answers to two questions of Smirnov on Hilbert coefficients of Frobenius powers and Hilbert-Kunz multiplicities of ordinary powers. We construct complete normal Cohen-Macaulay hypersurfaces whose maximal ideals have normalized Hilbert coefficients of every index at least three tending to minus infinity. We also construct isolated normal F-pure non-Cohen-Macaulay singularities whose maximal ideals have convergent normalized coefficients but do not satisfy the proposed eventual polynomial formula. For every Noetherian local ring of positive characteristic and dimension $d\geq2$, we prove convergence of the second normalized Hilbert coefficient and a three-term asymptotic expansion with remainder $o(n^{d-2})$. Thus coefficient convergence always holds in dimension two, and index three is the first possible failure in higher dimensions. Both questions have positive answers for every ideal primary to the maximal ideal in a local ring of finite F-representation type.
Physics-Informed Mixed Integer Programming Methods for Optimal Patch Antennas
Ruben Hoeksma; Jesse van Rhijn; Marc Uetz; Wick Wijnholds

Antennas come in various shapes and sizes, as their performance characteristics are very much dependent on their exact shape. Coming up with a shape that matches desired design characteristics has, up until this moment, been largely the domain of metaheuristics and local optimization methods. While these methods are convenient, they generally provide no performance guarantees and rarely allow to enforce hard design constraints. In this paper, we show how Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) can be used to optimize the shape of so-called patch antennas. The methodological focus is to show how underlying laws of physics allow to derive effective bounds on variables as well as new cutting planes. These greatly improve the effectiveness of the underlying basic MIP model, enabling the automated design of practically relevant patch antennas for a wide variety of applications.
A sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines

We construct a sporadic simplicial arrangement of $51$ lines in the real projective plane. It is obtained from the icosahedral arrangement $\mathcal{A}(21,2)$ by adjoining the $30$ images of the line $y+\sqrtφ\,z=0$ under the rotation group of the icosahedron, where $φ=(1+\sqrt5)/2$. Its intersection multiplicities are $t_2=120$, $t_3=190$, $t_5=36$, and $t_6=15$, with all other $t_r$ zero. These counts give equality in Melchior's inequality and hence prove simpliciality. The arrangement is irreducible, belongs to neither of the two known infinite families of irreducible simplicial arrangements, and is not supersolvable. It therefore disproves the $37$-line bound for sporadic arrangements conjectured by Cuntz and Mücksch. We give explicit coordinates, a finite incidence certificate, a geometric explanation of the parameter $\sqrtφ$, and a standalone exact-arithmetic verifier.
Hecke Orbits on Globally Drinfeld-Uniformized Shimura Varieties Are $p$-adically Nowhere Dense

Fix a projective unitary Shimura datum satisfying Varshavsky's global Drinfeld uniformization hypotheses at a place $v\mid p$ of its reflex field $E$. Let $\mathcal{S}h$ be the base change of the Shimura variety to $\mathbb C_p$ at a sufficiently small neat finite level. We prove that for every closed reduced algebraic subvariety $Z\subset\mathcal{S}h$ with $\operatorname{dim} Z<\operatorname{dim} \mathcal{S}h$, the $p$-adic closure of its full finite adelic Hecke orbit has empty interior in $\mathcal{S}h(\mathbb C_p)$. At certain compatible levels, the nowhere density theorem also holds for Shimura varieties associated with a related PEL datum having the same adjoint datum as Varshavsky's. Moreover, for every rational prime $p$ and every integer $d\geq2$, there is a projective unitary Shimura variety of dimension $d-1$ satisfying these uniformization hypotheses at a place above $p$ for which the nowhere density theorem holds.
Tree-independence number VIII. 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number
Maria Chudnovsky; Julien Codsi; Ajaykrishnan E S; Daniel Lokshtanov; Ilya Maier

A three-path-configuration is a graph consisting of three pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths, the union of every two of which is an induced cycle of length at least four. A graph is 3PC-free if no induced subgraph of it is a three-path-configuration. We show that 3PC-free graphs have logarithmic tree-independence number, which is asymptotically best possible.
Kirszbraun's Intersection Property and Nonexpansive Extensions

This paper aims to present the historical development of the extension problem of nonexpansive maps in Euclidean and Hilbert spaces, and to serve as a comprehensive guide to this specific area. Such extensions are based on a geometric property of the intersection of closed balls in Euclidean spaces, known as the Kirszbraun intersection property. Subsequently, a number of authors have extended this property to Hilbert and other spaces. All these results are discussed in this paper, but the paper itself is not a mechanical compilation of already known proofs. The material has been developed with an emphasis on the natural connections between all these results and the corresponding concepts involved in them. Furthermore, most of these results are presented with new simplified proofs. Last but not least, the paper also contains some new results related to this extension problem.
From Wheel to Jahangir graphs: spectra and energy under structured edge deletion
Diego Bravo; Florencia Cubría; Annabella Zapattini

The energy of a graph, introduced by Gutman, is defined as the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix. In this work we study how the energy of the Wheel graph $W_n$ changes when a specific set of spokes is removed. The resulting graphs are precisely the Jahangir graphs $J_{m,n}$, where m divides n, and which may also be viewed as the Cycle graph $C_n$ together with an additional vertex adjacent to certain vertices of $C_n$ in a cyclic pattern. We determine the spectra of $J_{2,n}$, $J_{4,n}$, and $J_{6,n}$ by exploiting a factorization of their characteristic polynomials arising from equitable partitions. This yields explicit closed formulas for their energies. Moreover, under certain conditions, we establish the following monotonicity chain: \[\mathcal{E}(C_n) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{6,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{4,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(J_{2,n}) \;\leq\; \mathcal{E}(W_n).\]
The Prevalence of Straight Shots in Control Space for Reaching Optimal Quantum Performance
Yiyou Chen; Gabriele Herr; Herschel Rabitz

Gradient-based algorithms are often applied to identify an optimal control for maximizing a quantum objective functional by following a steepest ascent path to the top of the control landscape. In contrast, this paper explores straight shots through control space where movement along such a path corresponds to a less demanding monotonic complete climb up the landscape for the optimal objective value. Existing studies of control landscapes have revealed the presence of straight shots, but identifying them required computationally intensive stochastic methods. In this paper, we introduce a non-stochastic straight-shot search algorithm (STSA) that identifies a large class of straight shots. We apply STSA to numerically generate more than 10,000 distinct straight-shot optimization paths and analyze their statistical distribution for each of the objectives of (i) state-to-state transitions, (ii) general observables, and (iii) unitary transformation generation. The results show a decrease in the nearest-neighbor distances among straight shots as the sample size increases, suggesting their prevalence in control space. We further conjecture that the starting locations of the straight-shot pathways on a landscape level set may form connected neighborhoods, motivating future investigation into their underlying topological structure. The present paper focuses on the use of STSA for locating massive numbers of straight solutions. However, the STSA is not a high-efficiency algorithm in its present form, but the discovered prevalence of control straight shots leaves open future advances to accelerate the discovery of straight shots as optimal controls.
Self-Supervised Tuning of Low-Fidelity Optimization Models via High-Fidelity Feedback
Gonzalo E. Constante-Flores; André H. Quisaguano-Paredes; Asha Ramanujam; Rishabh Gupta; Can Li

Low-fidelity (LF) optimization models are widely used in large-scale operations because they can be solved efficiently and reliably, but they often exhibit systematic errors relative to high-fidelity (HF) formulations that better capture physical and operational constraints. Existing learning-based approaches typically rely on supervised or semi-supervised training with HF solutions, which are expensive to compute and may not align with HF operational objectives. We propose a self-supervised framework that parameterizes LF optimization models directly from HF feedback. The low-fidelity problem is embedded as a differentiable optimization layer and trained end-to-end, while a HF correction problem evaluates its solution and provides gradient information through its dual variables, without requiring HF solution labels. We evaluate the framework on optimal power flow, optimal gas flow, and pooling problems, spanning different sources of low- and high-fidelity mismatch. Across all three applications, the self-supervised approach improves objective quality and feasibility over untuned LF models and generally outperforms semi-supervised training. The learned parameterizations also generalize to unseen operating conditions and, for network applications with up to 30,000 nodes, to systems not encountered during training.
DSINC beyond Heston: the 3/2 and other non-affine stochastic-volatility models

This paper extends the damped-sinc (DSINC) method for American options beyond the affine Heston class to general one-factor stochastic-volatility models. We show that the collapse identity, which reduces the early-exercise integral to a single spectral integral, remains valid for these models. Damping between zero and one is admissible whenever the discounted spot is a nonnegative local martingale. An Itô transformation of the volatility factorizes the conditional characteristic function and identifies a natural coordinate for approximating the exercise boundary. The 3/2 model admits closed-form joint transforms in terms of Kummer functions, while uncorrelated SABR admits a Bessel representation. When a practical closed-form transform is unavailable, the required volatility integral is computed directly by solving one backward equation per frequency, without a grid in the log-price. Through a known change of volatility coordinate, this approach also accommodates correlated SABR. Tests on the 3/2, SABR, GARCH and lognormal-volatility models show agreement with fine finite-difference benchmarks to within one basis point of the strike. Computational cost is comparable to or lower than that of our finite-difference implementation, except for the slower Hankel implementation of uncorrelated SABR.
Methods for Deriving Nonlinear Kinetic Equations from the Dynamics of Quantum Systems

The article outlines key topics related to deriving kinetic equations and, in general, to the relationship between the evolution equations governing quantum many-particle systems. The main issues being considered are the mathematical origin of quantum kinetic equations, novel methods for deriving kinetic equations from hierarchies of evolution equations for quantum systems, specifically focusing on kinetics within the framework of the evolution of observables, and the generalization of the quantum kinetic equation specified by non-separable initial states.

We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hatμ(2^k)|^σ< \infty$ for any $σ> 0$, where $μ$ is the Cantor measure.
Subset sums of power values over Galois rings

Let $R=GR(p^m,p^{mf})$, where $p$ is prime, $q=p^f$, $m,f\geq1$, $d\geq2$ and $p\nmid d$. We count $n$-element subsets of $P=\{x^d:x\in R\}\setminus\{0\}$, the set of distinct nonzero $d$th-power values, with a prescribed sum. For fixed $m,d,n$ with $n\geq3$, the count equals \[ q^{-m}\binom{|P|}{n}(1+O_{m,d,n}(q^{1-n/2})) \] as $q\to\infty$ through admissible prime powers, uniformly over all targets and with both $p$ and $f$ allowed to vary. For fixed $m,d$, we also classify uniform relative equidistribution at the remaining positive sizes: it fails at $n=1$, and at $n=2$ it holds along an admissible sequence if and only if, for all sufficiently large terms, $\gcd(d,q-1)=1$ and $(m\geq2\text{ or }p\ne2)$.
Kobayashi completeness of pseudoconvex domains: finite type and a smooth counterexample

We prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^N$ with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo one-type is Kobayashi complete. As a separate consequence of our criterion of completeness and an estimate of Diederich--Fornæss, we prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We then show that smoothness alone does not imply completeness: there exists a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary and a global smooth plurisubharmonic defining function whose Kobayashi and Carathéodory distances are incomplete.
A counterexample to Gale's conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$

It is known that for every partition of the sphere $S^2$ of unit diameter into four parts, the largest diameter of a part is at least $\sqrt{(3+\sqrt{3})/6} = 0.88807\dots$, and this bound is attained. The conjecture of D.~Gale (1953) asserts that no set in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a larger ratio. In this paper, we construct a $101$-point set $V\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ such that every partition of $V$ into four parts contains a part of diameter greater than $0.88928 \, \operatorname{diam} V$.
Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space

We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.
Short sums of the Möbius function over function fields
Etienne Fouvry; Igor E. Shparlinski; Ping Xi

We develop a new method which allows us to estimate, with a power saving, sums of the M{ö}bius function over function fields ${\mathbb F}_p(X)$. The sums run over monic polynomials with all other coefficients in short intervals, of length below the Pólya--Vinogradov threshold $p^{1/2}$. A classical result of L. Stickelberger (1898) reduces this question to bounding character sums with polynomial discriminants which are inhomogeneous multivariate polynomials. Variants of Burgess's method with non-linear shifts {\it {à} la carte} are introduced to go beyond the Pólya--Vinogradov range, combined with a stratification result of J. Xu (2020) for complete character sums.
A Matroidal Framework for Random Access in Linear Codes
Daniella Bar-Lev; Hiram H. López; Gretchen L. Matthews; Flavio Salizzoni

We study random access in linear codes when codeword symbols are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement. A code is recovery balanced if the expected number of samples required to recover a codeword coordinate is the same for every coordinate. We express the recovery expectations in terms of the associated matroid and derive a coordinatewise identity relating these values for a code and its dual. This proves that a linear code is recovery balanced if and only if its dual is recovery balanced, establishing a conjecture of Gruica et al. We further define the recovery balance for arbitrary matroids and show that asymptotically almost every sparse paving matroid is not recovery balanced.
