Starting from a traditionally learned Duffing dynamics, we find a homoclinic pulse as a plausible localized extreme scenario. Next, since the same equation also appears in the stationary nonlinear Schrodinger system, with the coordinate interpreted as space instead of time, this pulse becomes a standing soliton. We then retrain the first stage using a geometry-agnostic neural representation, enabling the learned dynamics to be lifted to higher-dimensional space to obtain higher-dimensional solitary profile, known as Townes soliton. Finally, with a Liouville system, we demonstrate that dynamics learned from data on a (1+1)-dimensional Lorentzian quasi-manifold can be transferred to a (2+0)-dimensional Euclidean manifold to identify an instanton. Our approach can be applied to other coherent spatiotemporal structures, including kinks, rogue waves, compactons, peakons, and potentially even singularities, with applications in risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection.
Liouville Theorems for Semilinear Parabolic Equations Involving the Nonlinear Gradient Term

In this paper, we prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^q$ via the integral Bernstein method, where $q=2p/(p+1)$ is critical and $M<0$. As an application, we can establish a universal priori estimate for this equation by using the doubling lemma. These results generalize the previous work of Liang and Zhang. We can also prove the Liouville-type theorem for equation $u_t-Δu=u^p+M|\nabla u|^2$, which corresponds to the supercritical case.
Claims of emergence in AI should be grounded in information decomposition

When a language model develops capabilities not traceable to its individual components, when a multi-agent AI system outperforms each agent on its own, or when a human-AI pair succeeds where either fails in isolation, AI researchers describe it as a case of ``synergy'' or ``emergence''. However, these are usually informal assessments not supported by a theoretical framework, making these claims impossible to compare or even meaningfully dispute. Here we argue that \emph{information decomposition can serve as a unifying formal framework to operationalize assessments about synergy in AI systems}. Information decomposition provides a way to distinguish qualitatively different \emph{types} of information, including unique information available from individual components, redundant information shared across multiple components, and synergistic information accessible only from parts taken together. This gives claims of emergence a precise, falsifiable criterion: a system's behavior is emergent only if it carries synergistic information about task-relevant outcomes. We apply this lens to attention heads, autonomous agents, and human-AI teams, showing how it organizes existing knowledge across scales and substrates, while also generating cross-level conjectures that siloed fields would miss.
A single generation theorem for simple unital $C^*$-algebras with CPoU and comparison

In this note, assuming the finite factor generation theorem obtained by OpenAI, we demonstrate that if a separable simple unital $C^*$-algebra $A$ with nonempty trace space, has the strict comparison for positive elements, and its uniform tracial completion has complemented partitions of unity (CPoU), then $A$ is singly generated.
Gal Binyamini; Avner Kiro; Gady Kozma; Jonathan Pila

We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.
On the Geometry of Low Rank Correlation Matrices
Olivier Bisson; David Loiseaux; Xavier Pennec

Correlation matrices of bounded rank form a stratified space whose factor representations lie in a product of spheres. Using the orbit-type description of the rank stratification, we prove that padding factors preserves the Riemannian geometry of each fixed-rank stratum and the intrinsic length metric of every rank-bounded subset. In the reduced model, a Sylvester equation describes the mechanical connection and its horizontal lifts. We derive sectional-curvature formulas and bounds, characterize zero-curvature directions, and determine the connection's holonomy groups. In particular, a flat rank-two connection can have nontrivial dihedral holonomy. For geodesics subject to a rank bound, rank cannot decrease in the interior of a minimizing segment with maximal-rank endpoints; the local excess over the unconstrained quotient distance is controlled by a dimension-independent cubic estimate. Finally, we compute the exact change of measure between quotient Riemannian volume and Euclidean surface volume in the off-diagonal entries. Coarea yields explicit factor densities for both normalized uniform laws.
We prove that the reduced C*-algebra of Thompson's group $F$ is $\mathcal{Z}$-stable and selfless.
On the stability of displacement energy in toric manifolds

We present a quantitative exploration of the behaviour of displacement energy of Lagrangians under stabilization. In particular, we completely characterize the displacement behaviour of toric fibres in Fano 4-manifolds. Our approach relates the geometry of the moment polytope's caustic to the structure of the (bulk-deformed) superpotential and to the presence of symmetric probes.
Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees

We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $γ>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $Δ_j(\mathcal H)\leqγb^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $Δ_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.
ACM, almost Ulrich, and Ulrich vector bundles arising from Frobenius

Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$ over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We investigate ACM, almost Ulrich (both ACM and weakly Ulrich), and Ulrich properties of the sheaves of locally exact and closed $i$-forms $B_X^i$, $Z_X^i$. These cohomological properties are closely related to the fundamental concepts of Frobenius splitting and ordinarity. Joshi studied the sheaf $B^1_X$ in this context in \cite{MR3920911, MR4206787}, including ACM and almost Ulrich twists of $B^1_X$. However, varieties with Ulrich twisted $B_X^1$ have not been classified for $n\ge2$. We classify subcanonical polarized varieties with initialized ACM $B^i_X(aH)$ for $i=1, n$ and prove that, for $n \ge 2$, varieties with ACM $B^i_X$ for all $i \le \left\lceil\frac{n}{2}\right\rceil$ are ordinary. When $X$ is ordinary with trivial $Ω^1_X$, almost Ulrich twists of $B^i_X$ and $F_*^e(Z_X^i(aH))$ are determined. We classify polarized varieties $(X,H)$ with $B_X^i(aH)$ Ulrich when $n=1, 2$, and establish strong necessary criteria for $n \geq 3$, together with an example. We also prove that $Z_X^i(aH)$ is never Ulrich. Finally, we classify polarized abelian varieties with Ulrich $B^1_X \otimes L$ allowing twists by arbitrary line bundles.
Backward Homogeneous Heat Equation with $Ψ$-Caputo Time Derivative and Spectral Fractional Laplacian
Nelson R. Ojeda; Ruben D. Spies

In this work, we study a fractional diffusion model in time and space, formulated in an open and bounded domain, involving a Caputo fractional derivative of order $μ\in(0,1)$ with respect to a time scale function $Ψ$, together with a spectral fractional Laplacian operator of order $s\in(0,1)$. The associated direct problem is analyzed, as well as the inverse problem of temporal reconstruction from final data, which is inherently ill-posed. Through a spectral representation, the instability of the problem and the effect of the choice of the function $Ψ$ on the amplification of spectral modes are examined.
Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations

This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.
Existence of Ulrich bundles on polarized surfaces and weakly Ulrich bundles on polarized varieties in positive characteristic

In their seminal paper \cite{eisenbud2003resultants}, Eisenbud and Schreyer asked whether every smooth projective variety admits an Ulrich bundle with respect to each very ample polarization. This question has stimulated extensive research for more than two decades. Recently, Anghel \cite{anghel2026smooth} constructed counterexamples over $\mathbb C$ in dimension two, and Lopez \cite{lopez2026existence} extended this nonexistence result to higher dimensions. In this article, we study the existence problem for sufficiently large multiples of a fixed polarization and derive applications in positive characteristic. Over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, we prove that every polarized smooth surface admits an Ulrich bundle and every polarized smooth variety admits a weakly Ulrich bundle. Consequently, the Chow forms of surfaces (resp. varieties) admit linear determinantal (resp. determinantal) representations. Moreover, for every such polarized surface, the cone of cohomology tables of coherent sheaves coincides with that on $(\mathbb{P}^2, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1))$.
Hyperbolic comparison and rigidity for the hyperspherical radius

We prove Gromov's hyperbolic hyperspherical radius comparison and rigidity conjectures in all dimensions $n\ge3$, without the spin assumption. Let $(X^n, g)$ be a smooth, oriented, connected, compact Riemannian manifold with nonempty smooth connected boundary $S$. If ${\rm Sc}_g\ge -n(n-1)$ and $H_S\ge (n-1)\coth R$ for some $R>0$, then ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)\le\sinh R$, with equality if and only if $(X^n,g)$ is isometric to the closed hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$. Under the same curvature bounds, every smooth $1$-Lipschitz map of nonzero degree from $S$ to the boundary of the hyperbolic geodesic ball of radius $R$ extends to an isometry of the fillings. Here, $g_S$ is the induced boundary metric, $H_S$ is the mean curvature of $S$ with respect to the outward unit normal, and ${\rm Rad}(S,g_S)$ denotes the hyperspherical radius.
Real-analytic standard families and rotational invariant curves

In this paper we study one-parameter families of exact standard maps of the form $$\widehat{f}_{k,g}(\widehat{x},\widehat{y}) =\bigl(\widehat{x}+\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x}) \bmod 1,\widehat{y}+kg(\widehat{x})\bigr),$$ where $k$ is a real parameter and $g:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic, 1-periodic and has zero mean. The most famous example is when $g(\widehat{x})=\frac{\sin(2π\widehat{x})}{2π}$. In this case, the closed subset $A_{\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}\subset \mathbb{R}$ of values of $k$ for which $\widehat{f}_{k,\sin(2π\cdot)/(2π)}$ has rotational invariant curves is conjectured to be a closed interval. Much has been done towards this conjecture, both numerically and analytically. But a complete proof has not yet been achieved. Our approach here goes in the opposite direction: we construct a function $θ:\mathbb{T} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the above conditions, such that $A_θ$ is not an interval: It contains at least 2 different connected components, which are non-degenerate closed intervals.
The Art of Toda Brackets-A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
Yoshihiro Hirato; Jin-ho Lee; Toshiyuki Miyauchi; Juno Mukai; Mariko Ohara; Juxin Yang

This book has several fundamental aims, one of which is to serve as a reference book for computing unstable homotopy groups using methods of the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. It plays a fundamental role in dealing with composition relations of homotopy classes. This book brings together in Appendix A.3 all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained using the art of Toda brackets as the principal tool, with explicit generators. It also explains in Appendix A.2 the conventions used to name the generators. The book mainly presents calculations of the $2$-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ for all $23\leq i\leq 28$ and all $n,$ as well as some $π_{29}(\mathit{SO}(n)),$ with explicit generators, while retaining two possible group structures for $π_{28}(\mathit{SO}(11)).$ In degree $29,$ the cases $7\leq n\leq14$ remain under investigation. The odd-primary components of the homotopy groups $π_i(\mathit{SO}(n))$ in the above range can be computed with little effort; these computations essentially amount to looking up the relevant entries in existing tables.
Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology

We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Zúñiga, are given.
Scaling limits for peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane

We construct and study peeling explorations of the Brownian half-plane by successively revealing hulls of fixed radius. We prove that for any peeling process, as the radius of the hulls tends to zero, the sequence of discovered hulls converges to an explicit family of Brownian disks. We also consider the particular case of what we call nearest-neighbour peeling explorations, where the center of each new hull is chosen on the outer boundary of the previously discovered hull, naturally giving rise to an exploration curve. We provide scaling limits results for these curves, jointly with the convergence of the associated boundary-length and volume processes.
Do Neural Models Prefer Their Submodels?
Alvaro Ribot; Yulia Alexandr; Anna Seigal

A neural model is the set of functions that can be expressed by a given neural network architecture. Neural models contain natural submodels, such as those obtained by setting some neurons to be inactive. We study the geometry of neural models and ask whether they prefer their submodels. By this we mean whether local minimizers of the loss function lie in a given submodel. We introduce a geometric framework to determine if this occurs. For shallow multilayer perceptrons, we show that subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are never preferred. For deep multilayer perceptrons, we give conditions under which subnetworks with inactive hidden neurons are not preferred. For lightning self-attention, lower-rank submodels are usually not preferred, but we identify examples where they are because they lie on a boundary of the model. Our results show that, aside from a few exceptions, preference for submodels cannot be explained by the geometry of the neural model, and must instead come from other sources such as training dynamics.
Tao Chen; Yunping Jiang; Linda Keen

We consider the family of transcendental meromorphic functions with finitely many singular values, none of whose asymptotic values is infinity. We prove that transversality holds at any boundary point of a shell component in a dynamically natural slice of the parameter space at which an asymptotic value is a prepole.
Brunn-Minkowski inequality for p-capacity of compact sets

We prove the capacitary Brunn-Minkowski inequality for arbitrary nonempty compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, and every $1<p<\infty$, with no assumption of convexity, connectedness, interior, or boundary regularity. For $1<p<n$ the inequality is for the variational $p$-capacity. For $p>n$ it is for the capacity determined by the constant term at infinity of the normalized $p$-harmonic Green's function with pole at infinity, and for $p=n$ for an outer regularization of this quantity, which agrees with it for $n$-regular sets and in the plane is a constant multiple of logarithmic capacity. In particular, it holds for Newtonian capacity of all compact sets in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq3$, and for logarithmic capacity of all planar compact sets. Previously these inequalities were known for convex sets and, for logarithmic capacity, for planar continua. When both capacities are positive, equality holds for $0<λ<1$ if and only if the filled sets, obtained by adjoining the bounded components of the complement, are convex and equal up to translation and dilation. This characterization is new for nonconvex sets, even for Newtonian and logarithmic capacity.
Determinant characters and multiplicative solubility of finite skew braces

Let $B$ be a finite skew brace. We prove that if the additive derived subgroup $(B,+)'$ is nilpotent, then the multiplicative group $(B,\cdot)$ is soluble. In particular, this holds for finite skew braces with supersoluble or metabelian additive group.
Convergence and semisimplicity of big quantum cohomology of flag varieties
Changzheng Li; Zhaoyang Liu; Tony Yue Yu; Chi Zhang

We prove the folklore conjecture that the big quantum cohomology of a flag variety $G/P$ of general Lie type is convergent near the large-radius limit and is generically semisimple. The convergence relies on a slightly modified version of Iritani's reconstruction theorem, together with Cauchy's formula that avoids directly taking the non-equivariant limit at the origin. Generic semisimplicity follows from a surprising application of the big quantum $D$-module mirror symmetry for $G/P$ established by the first, third and fourth authors jointly with Hinault and Zhang. Moreover, we prove the regularity conjecture on the big quantum cohomology of $G/P$ formulated by Perrin and Smirnov, which implies generic semisimplicity.
Bounded Symbols and One-Component Inner Functions

Let $θ$ be a nonconstant inner function, we prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_θ=H^2\ominusθH^2$ admits a bounded symbol if and only if $θ$ is one-component, that is, if $\{z\in\mathbb D:|θ(z)|<r\}$ is nonempty and connected for some $r\in(0,1)$. This establishes the previously open necessary direction and resolves a conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi, and Timotin. For every non-one-component inner function, we construct a sequence of norm-one rank-one truncated Toeplitz operators whose infimal $L^\infty$-norms over all representing symbols tend to infinity. The quantitative lower bound is obtained by forming two inner divisors from angularly separated parts of the zero set and singular measure. The argument applies without restrictions on the Blaschke or singular parts of $θ$. The order of this lower bound is sharp, already for a family of degree-two Blaschke products. A continuation argument for local inverse branches produces the required sequence of points. Consequently, every non-one-component model space supports a trace-class truncated Toeplitz operator without a bounded symbol. Combined with known equivalences, the characterization also yields geometric criteria for weak factorization and for continuous-symbol representations of compact truncated Hankel operators.
A Convex Feasibility Problem for Which Douglas-Rachford Converges Only Weakly

We provide two closed, convex sets with nonempty intersection and an initial point for which the Douglas-Rachford algorithm converges weakly but not strongly. This resolves an open question as noted earlier by Aragón Artacho, Borwein and Tam (2014, Remark 2.2). Our construction is a simple lift of a recent construction by Bauschke and Tung concerning firmly nonexpansive operators.
Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
Jiangdong Ai; Mingyu Liu; Zhiyu Song

Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(π(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $π(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(π(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(π(P)+ε)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(π(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $π_d=π(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)λ_d\leπ_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $λ_d$ is the vertex Turán density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-π_d=\exp(-Θ(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\leπ_2\le2.15121$.
Near-blowup asymptotic analysis and analytical extension for the inviscid primitive equations
Charles Collot; Slim Ibrahim; Lingjun Qian

The primitive equations widely approximate the Navier--Stokes equations in large-scale geophysical fluid dynamics. Their finite-time singularity formation-which occurs exclusively in the inviscid case-sheds light on the mechanisms driving small-scale creation. Building on \cite{Collot2023}, which constructed 2D horizontally odd solutions where the on-axis derivative $\partial_X u(t,0,Z)$ blows up at rate $(T-t)^{-1}$ with boundary concentration scale $|\ln (T-t)|^{-1}$, this paper characterizes this blow-up as forming between hyperbolic stagnation points. We derive precise asymptotic expansions for on-axis derivatives beyond leading order, identifying a horizontal concentration scale of $(T-t)^{3/2}$ characteristic of generic Burgers' singularities. Furthermore, we justify the 2D solution's expansion near the symmetry axis by proving $(T-t)^{3/2}$ is a universal lower bound on the radius of analyticity.
Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture

We show that the uniform random $d$-regular graph model on $n$ vertices is, in total variation distance, asymptotically close to the union of $d$ uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, provided that $n$ is even and $ω(1) = d \leq n^{1/10}$. This confirms a conjecture by Hollom, Lichev, Mond, Portier, and Wang for this range of parameters. This result has a couple of interesting consequences. First, this shows that random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exhibit sprinkling properties for some range of parameters, thereby confirming a conjecture by Isaev, McKay, Southwell and Zhukovskii in that range. Second, we give a short alternative proof of the upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture in the sparse regime.
On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices

A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of Östergård--Paavola and Ó Catháin--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.
Budgeted Admission from Timestamped Capacity Records in Shared Clusters

A cluster admission gate can receive a capacity record that no longer matches current schedulability. We study one exogenous binary schedulability unit under a bound on the joint probability of admission and unavailability. For a symmetric Markov state, we derive the stationary admission frontier for a fixed observation delay and apply finite likelihood allocation to a delay-tagged delivered record. A one-sided exact binomial endpoint calibrates each fitted policy, and exact enumeration confirms the per-policy confidence target in every tested parameter cell. A separate deterministic guard charges every unresolved admission against the realized allowance and bounds unavailable-state admissions at every prefix under truthful outcome feedback. An executable admission procedure composes the allocation and guard. The controlled system binds source sampling, NATS delivery, randomized admission, Kubernetes objects, and API-derived outcomes in one append-only record. Independent audit finds no missing event, identity mismatch, or state mismatch in the completed functional block. A separate CPU request-accounting check preserves Job and Pod identity across an unschedulable-to-complete transition.
Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces

We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. A note on the cube inequality
In this note, we adapt ideas from No. 336 of OpenAI's October 6, 2026 mathematics release to prove the weighted cube inequality in all dimensions.

We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.
Near Optimal Finite Model POMDP Approximation of Controlled Diffusion with Partial Information
Yunus Emre Demirci; Somnath Pradhan; Serdar Yüksel

We study continuous-time stochastic control problems under partial information. Our main contributions are the following: (i) We show near optimality, under finite horizon as well as discounted infinite horizon cost criteria, of piece-wise constant control policies obtained via solutions to discrete-time partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) approximations, constructed via Euler-Maruyama approximations of both state and observation processes; (ii) we obtain several regularity properties of such POMDP approximate models; and (iii) using these regularity properties, we arrive at near optimal finite model approximations. (iv) These culminate into our main result which is that an optimal solution for the approximate finite POMDP model is near optimal for the original diffusion with partial information.
Avoiding abelian squares with three colours in the continuous setting
Ville Salo; Ingrid Vukusic; Charlie Wilson

An $n$-colouring of the real line is a Lebesgue measurable function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to A$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ colours. An abelian square for $f$ is a finite interval $U\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ where every colour shows up in the left and in the right half of $U$ with exactly the same Lebesgue measure. It is known that every $2$-colouring contains an abelian square. On the other hand, Alon, Grytczuk, Laso{ń}, and Michałek (2009) proved that there exist $4$-colourings that avoid abelian squares, while the question for $3$-colourings remained open. We construct a $3$-colouring that avoids abelian squares, disproving a conjecture of Laso{ń} (2015). However, in contrast to the case of 4-colourings, the set of 3-colourings that avoid abelian squares is meagre. We show this using an argument based on the KKM lemma.
Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge--Ampère Equation

We establish an interior $C^2$ estimate for locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solutions of the complex Monge--Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$ under weak quadratic growth bounds on sufficiently large balls, where $f$ is positive and Dini-continuous. We assume a distributional lower bound for the Laplacian of $f^{1/n}$. The main ingredient is a pseudo-$C^2$ estimate using the Green-function averaging error, valid also when $f$ is nonnegative. As an application, we prove that every entire Bedford-Taylor solution of $\det(u_{i\bar j})=1$ with weak quadratic growth is a real quadratic polynomial, resolving a conjecture of Gábor Székelyhidi.
Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems

Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.
Thin-Layer Dichotomy in Three-Phase Mullins-Sekerka Flow: Gap Dynamics and Composite Interfaces

We study the thin-layer limit of the Mullins-Sekerka flow in concentric circular geometries at fixed wave number $k$, contrasting a two-phase annulus with a genuine three-phase layer. A dichotomy emerges: for $k\ge2$ the rates blow up like the inverse thickness when the same phase lies on both sides of the layer, whereas between two different phases the matrix governing the linearized Fourier mode extends analytically to zero thickness. Both cases share the singular Dirichlet-to-Neumann factor of the thin annulus and differ only in whether the Gibbs-Thomson law forces an order-one potential difference across it. In the three-phase case the pure thickness-modulation rate stays below the logarithmic growth rate of the mean thickness, for every $k\ge1$ and all positive tensions, and, after projection onto the mean displacement and the outer interface, the collapsed pair moves as one interface carrying the sum of the two tensions. All statements concern the instantaneous fixed-mode linearization. The singularity is a property of the phase coupling, not of the thin geometry.
A General Construction of Strict Models in HoTT
Niyousha Najmaei; Niels van der Weide

Homotopy type theory (HoTT) provides a natural setting for studying the metatheory of type theory, as it comes with additional extensionality principles compared to ordinary Martin-Löf type theory. In particular, it is especially suitable for developing semantics of type theory, where one distinguishes two kinds of models: strict models, which give us sound interpretations, and pseudomodels. Pseudomodels are useful as they occur prevalently and can be turned into strict models by constructions called strictifications. However, the commonly used strictifications do not translate well to HoTT, as they require assumptions that are generally not satisfied by concrete examples of models. We show how to carry out the universe model construction, due to Voevodsky, in HoTT. Under this construction, every pseudomodel together with a universe type closed under enough type formers gives rise to a strict model. We also show how to interpret type formers in the resulting model assuming that the universe is closed under them. Finally, we demonstrate that this construction generalises existing instances of strict set models in the literature, and we apply it to more examples, yielding presheaf models and assembly models of type theory in HoTT. Our results are formalised in Rocq using the UniMath library.
Sebastian Reboul; Lorenzo Croissant; Hélène Halconruy

In reinforcement learning, one presumes the action set to be known ahead of time, and, thus, one must know if any state-action pairs are not permissible ahead of computations. In some applications, determining this action mask is the main computational bottleneck. Isolating this problem to highlight its core properties, we study how to combine the search for an optimal policy with the learning of the mask itself, under a linear MDP model in which each attempted action reveals the exact value of a linear score determining its validity. In this framework, we first construct an algorithm based on deterministic optimistic optimization and show that it is minimax optimal, which we show is also computationally efficient. However, it is sub-optimal on non-degenerate instances, as we show. We propose an alternative, which is also computationally efficient, which plans its exploration strategy. This algorithm admits a formal interpretation as an analogue of information-directed-sampling for deterministic feedback, which may be of independent interest. Finally, we study an application of this framework to transfer learning, where the invalid action set changes over time.
Economic resources, sporting efficiency and uncertainty: a global test on the 2026 FIFA world cup

A related paper (arXiv:2610.06967) developed a stochastic optimization framework in which football performance combines GDP/population-based potential with a latent mean-reverting efficiency process. The framework was applied to a cross-section of the 24 national teams participating in AFCON 2025. This paper applies the same methodology to the full 48-team 2026 FIFA World Cup, extending the analysis beyond Africa without modifying the underlying model. Using GDP, population, FIFA ranking data, and complete tournament outcomes, it evaluates the framework against a global sample spanning all six confederations. Two findings emerge. First, GDP and population explain only 9 percent of single-tournament performance variance, compared with 33 percent for FIFA points. This gap is consistent with the model's distinction between systematic performance and match-specific idiosyncratic shocks. Second, using the less noisy FIFA-points measure, the African pattern persists globally: Morocco, Senegal, Argentina, Croatia, Portugal, and Uruguay emerge as leading GDP-relative over-performers. Conversely, several major economies, including the United States, Germany, Japan, and South Korea, underperform their GDP-implied potential. As in the related paper, we interpret the residual as a symmetric, non-structurally identified conditional performance residual, rather than an SFA-consistent efficiency estimate. We also quantify the extent to which its cross-country variance mechanically reflects the underlying performance measure. The GDP-rank/simulated-performance-rank correlation is robust to the choice of the model's unidentified dynamic parameters across a wide grid.
Attracting Rotations Obstruct Almost-Global Consensus on Spheres over Strongly Connected Graphs

We study discrete-time consensus on the Euclidean unit sphere, where weighted combinations of neighboring states are normalized to unit length. For symmetric weights on connected undirected graphs and ambient dimension $d\ge3$, earlier results establish instability of non-consensus fixed points under suitable weight conditions. For directed graphs on the unit circle, earlier results show that fixed points other than consensus and antipodal configurations occur only for a measure-zero set of weights. We show that these conclusions do not extend directly to general strongly connected directed graphs in higher dimensions. First, we construct full-rank non-consensus fixed points whose tangent eigenvalues all equal one, showing that strict linear instability need not hold. In a separate construction, for every $d\ge3$, we present a sparse strongly connected graph admitting full-rank fixed points on an open set of its permitted weights. Our main result establishes robust counterexamples to almost-global consensus: attracting rotating motions exist for $d=2$ with every $n\ge3$ and for $d=3$ with every $n\ge6$. These motions are locally asymptotically stable modulo common rotations and have asymptotic phase. They persist on open sets of strictly positive weight matrices. For each such matrix, an open set of initial configurations approaches neither consensus nor any fixed configuration. Thus the absence of full-rank non-consensus fixed points does not ensure almost-global convergence to consensus.
Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits for Positive Factorial Multiples

Let $τ(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ τ(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.
First-Order Mean Field Games with Time-Measurable and $C ^{1,1}$ Hamiltonians: Analysis and Approximation
Elisabetta Carlini; Valentina Coscetti; Francisco J. Silva

We introduce and analyze a numerical framework for a class of first-order, non-local Mean Field Game (MFG) systems with two sources of low regularity: the time-dependent data are merely measurable, and the Hamiltonian is only of class $C^{1,1}$ with respect to the momentum variable. The proposed method combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation with a Lagrange--Galerkin discretization of the continuity equation. Temporal measurability is handled by averaging the data over the time-grid intervals and using the stability theory of $L^1$-viscosity solutions. The limited regularity of the Hamiltonian is addressed through arguments from nonsmooth analysis, based in particular on Clarke's generalized differential calculus. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to some subsequence, to a solution of the MFG system. As a consequence, the numerical approximation also provides a constructive existence result. Under a monotonicity assumption on the coupling terms, we show that the solution to the MFG system is unique, implying the convergence of the whole sequence of discrete solutions. Finally, numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions illustrate the robustness of the method, including a linear--quadratic example with a running cost that is discontinuous in time and for which we compute an exact solution.
A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions

We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $Ω(n)$ and $Ω(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Teräväinen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $ω$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.
Optimal power concavity of the variational mean curvature via singular $1$-Laplace problems
Marco Gallo; Francesco Petitta; Marco Squassina

Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded convex domain and let $H_Ω\leq 0$ denote its variational mean curvature, in the sense of Barozzi, Gonzalez and Tamanini [PAMS, 1987]. We prove that $-H_Ω$ is harmonic convex, that is $1/H_Ω$ is a convex function in $Ω$, and that the exponent $-1$ is optimal in the class of convex domains. This strictly improves the concavity of $H_Ω$ obtained by Alter and Caselles [Nonlinear Anal., 2009], who also proved, by geometric methods, a closely related property for the classical mean curvature under Minkowski interpolation of convex bodies. Our approach is analytic: the result is deduced from a concavity property of the solution of the singular $1$-Laplace Dirichlet problem $$\begin{cases} -Δ_1 u = {u^{-γ}} & \quad \hbox{in $Ω$}, \\ u = 0 &\quad \hbox{on $\partial Ω$}, \end{cases}$$ for $γ\in (0,1]$, whose unique positive solution is $u=(-H_Ω)^{-1/γ}$. We show that $u^γ$ is concave, and we obtain this by proving that the solutions $u_p$ of the approximating problems $-Δ_p u_p = u_p^{-γ}$ are $\frac{p-1+γ}{p}$-concave on every bounded convex domain, without any boundary regularity, and then letting $p\to 1^+$. Explicit examples show that no Hölder continuity of $H_Ω$ up to $\partialΩ$ holds uniformly in the class of convex domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary.
Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations

Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.
Area gaps for minimal surfaces in spheres

In this paper, we prove that a linearly full minimal $2$-torus in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 5$ must have area $>2π^2$, and that a linearly full closed minimal surface in $\mathbb{S}^N$ with $N\geq 9$ must have area $>8π$. These results verify the Willmore conjecture and the generalized Willmore conjecture in higher codimension for minimal surfaces. The area gaps are obtained by applying the Cheng--Li--Yau comparison theorem and deriving a lower bound of the heat trace, where the monotonicity of the shifted normalized Riesz mean is used. We also establish a volume gap above the balanced Clifford product for linearly full closed minimal $n$-submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^N$ when $n=3$, $N\geq 9$, or $n\geq 4$, $N\geq 3n-1$.
Generative Diffusion Models for Secure UAV-ISAC with Real-Time Target Tracking
Homa Nikbakht; Yonina C. Eldar; H. Vincent Poor

Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms with integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) are prime candidates for surveillance missions, in which a dual-function drone tracks a mobile target and alerts a ground station when the target enters a protected region. Such alerts generate event-triggered communication traffic. By observing the change in the traffic, an eavesdropper (Eve) can therefore learn in real time whether the target is detected inside the protected region without decoding any message. Existing physical-layer security techniques protect the message content or hide that a transmission occurs, but the composition of the traffic remains exposed. We formulate the threat as traffic-composition covertness and propose a keyless diffusion-based transmission scheme that hides the triggered traffic. The scheme superposes the beamformed information streams of the UAV with a message-agnostic safeguard waveform generated by a conditional denoising diffusion implicit model. Training shapes the safeguard distribution such that triggered and non-triggered slots become statistically indistinguishable at Eve. The legitimate user shares no secret key with the UAV. We formulate the joint design as a rate maximization under covertness, reliability, and sensing constraints, with the sensing accuracy measured by the posterior Cramér-Rao bound (PCRB) of the beam-dependent tracking problem. Our numerical results show that, with multiple transmit antennas and an Eve signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of $5$~dB, a learned Eve stays near the blind guess of $0.5$ for every safeguard beam split, a detector that knows the safeguard model reaches $0.71$ to $0.73$ inside Bob's main lobe and $0.53$ to $0.55$ outside it, while the average position PCRB varies only between $0.59$ and $0.70$~m$^2$.
Stability of 2D MHD with Only Horizontal Dissipation near a Background Magnetic Field on $\mathbb{R}^2$
Jiahong Wu; Mengxin Yan; Ning Zhu; Yi Zhu

Whether the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with dissipation in only one direction are stable in $H^2$ on the whole plane is a well-known open problem: without transverse dissipation, a cubic interaction fails to be time-integrable. We show that a magnetic field removes this obstruction. For the 2D incompressible MHD equations on $\mathbb R^2$ in which both the viscosity $ν$ and the magnetic diffusivity $μ$ act only in the horizontal direction, we prove the global nonlinear $H^2$ stability of every background field $γe_2$ aligned with the non-dissipative direction, with a stability threshold that is explicit in $ν$, $μ$ and $γ$. The stabilizing mechanism is genuinely nonlinear: at the linear level the background field produces no damping at all in the vertical direction. Instead, in Elsässer variables the obstruction becomes an interaction between Alfvén waves travelling in opposite directions, and we identify nonlinear dissipative quantities that measure the overlap of these waves and are time-integrable although neither wave decays. We then sharpen the threshold by a space--time div--curl estimate for balance laws in the $(t,x_2)$-plane. For $ν=μ\leq1\leqγ$, the admissible perturbations are of size $ν^{2/3}γ^{1/3}$, improving the direct scale $ν$ and growing without bound as the background field strengthens.
Space-time large deviations for continuum birth-and-death processes
Benedikt Jahnel; Jonas Köppl; Yannic Steenbeck; Alexander Zass

We establish a space-time large deviation principle for the empirical process of spatial birth-and-death dynamics in the continuum with area interaction at arbitrary inverse temperature, including the free evolution. The good rate function is the dynamical specific relative entropy with respect to the dynamics, and the result holds on the space of space-time stationary laws on the Skorokhod path space, equipped with the topology of weak convergence. For the time marginals of the empirical process, we identify the rate function in terms of the Hellinger distance between the birth and the death measure of the observed point process, which vanishes exactly at the translation-invariant Gibbs point processes. This proves a continuum version of conjectures of Dai Pra and Handa, and connects space-time large deviations with entropy production.
Nonequivalence of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear and $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear generalized Hadamard codes for odd primes

The $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes are subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{α_1}\times\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}^{α_2}$, and they can be seen as linear codes over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ when $α_2=0$, as $\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive codes when $α_1=0$, and as $\mathbb{Z}_2\mathbb{Z}_4$-additive codes when $p=2$. A $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear generalized Hadamard (GH) code is a GH code over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ which is the Gray map image of a $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-additive code. For every prime $p$, there are recursive constructions of $\mathbb{Z}_p\mathbb{Z}_{p^2}$-linear GH codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ with $α_1\neq0$ and $α_2\neq0$, and of $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes $\bar H_p^{t_1,\dots,t_s}$. We show that the kernel blocks of a nonlinear code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ give equivalent punctured codes, and that these punctured codes are linear. Any of them is called the derived code of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. We also determine the ranks of the codes $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ and $\bar H_p^{t_1,t_2}$. For odd $p$, the rank of $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ depends on the Bernoulli numbers modulo $p$. By comparing the derived codes and the ranks, we show that, for odd $p$, no code $H_p^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to any of these $\mathbb{Z}_{p^s}$-linear GH codes. For $p=2$, a nonlinear code $H_2^{t_1,t_2}$ is equivalent to a $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard code if and only if $t_2\geq2$. Finally, we count the nonequivalent codes in the union of both families.
An Erdős-Szekeres-Type Result on Permutation Patterns

We construct an infinite set of patterns $(p,q)$ where $p$ is an almost increasing permutation and $q$ is an almost decreasing permutation, such that the exponential growth rate of permutations avoiding $(p,q)$ is 2. This extends a classical result of Erdős and Szekeres.
Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts

Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.
Gaussian Fluctuations of the Gradient of the Fréchet Function and Nonstandard Asymptotics of Sample Fréchet Means

We establish a central limit theorem for the gradient of the population Fréchet function in local Euclidean coordinates on a metric space. Assuming a unique population mean, a consistent measurable sequence of sample means, semiconcavity and moment bounds for the squared distance functions, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity of the population Fréchet function, we prove an asymptotic linear representation for the gradient of the population Fréchet function evaluated at the sample mean. The leading term is the negative empirical average of the gradients of the squared distance functions at the population mean; these gradients exist almost surely under our assumptions. On connected complete Riemannian manifolds, uniqueness of the population mean, existence of a $(2+η)$-moment, and local $C^{1,α}$ regularity suffice, and the leading term is expressed through the logarithm map. To control the empirical process uniformly over a neighborhood where squared distance functions may be nonsmooth, we use one-sided partial derivatives of the squared distance functions. The key estimate is a polynomial bound on the $L^2$ bracketing numbers of the resulting function classes. We also give a sufficient condition for the regularity of the population Fréchet function through probability bounds for neighborhoods of cut loci. We then show how the local behavior of the population Fréchet function transforms these Gaussian fluctuations into limit distributions for suitably rescaled sample Fréchet means, allowing for anisotropic scaling and non-Gaussian limits. Polynomial, logarithmic, and oscillatory examples illustrate the applicability and limitations of this approach.
Karthik Prakhya; Zimeng Wang; Alp Yurtsever

We propose adaptive primal-dual subgradient methods for constrained convex optimization. Our first method applies an AdaGrad-style step-sizes to the dual problem and recovers primal solutions by averaging the associated Fenchel-type oracle outputs. It achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ convergence for the dual objective residual, primal objective residual, and feasibility gap in the nonsmooth regime, while automatically improving to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ when the dual objective is smooth. We further develop an accelerated variant, which retains the $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ nonsmooth rate while achieving $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence in the smooth regime under mild assumptions. These guarantees require no prior knowledge of the underlying regularity. We demonstrate the empirical performance of the proposed methods on optimal transport and semidefinite relaxation of the Max-Cut problem.
Ordered Trees with Linear Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers
Lior Gishboliner; Artur Kravtsov; Xiangyu Li

We characterize the following three classes of ordered trees: $\qquad$ (1) trees $T$ satisfying $R_<(T,K_n)=O(n)$; $\qquad$ (2) $χ$-bounding trees; $\qquad$ (3) Ramsey-good trees. In particular, we show that the first two classes coincide. The second characterization answers a question of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt, and the third resolves a problem of Balko and Poljak. In our proof, we also introduce several novel constructions of ordered graphs with sublinear independence number, giving lower bounds on $R_<(F,K_n)$ for various ordered forests $F$.
Twisted group codes of dimension 2 and 3

It is known that all group codes of dimension at most $3$ are permutation equivalent to abelian group codes. We prove that twisted group codes of dimension at most $3$ are monomially equivalent either to an abelian group code or to an irreducible constacyclic code, and in the second case we describe the code explicitly by means of a trace map. Monomial equivalence cannot be replaced by permutation equivalence, and the second case cannot be avoided: the ternary tetracode is an ideal of $\mathbb F_3[x]/(x^4+1)$ but it is not monomially equivalent to any group code. More generally, we give two infinite families, in dimensions $2$ and $3$, of irreducible constacyclic codes which attain the Griesmer bound, whereas every group code with the same length and dimension has smaller minimum distance.
Pierre Fima; Hanna Oppelmayer; Leyan Tao

Given a discrete countable group $Γ$, we introduce the concept of random subalgebras of the reduced group $C^*$-algebra $C_r^*(Γ)$. This extends the existing theory of invariant random subgroups and the one of invariant random subalgebras of the group von Neumann algebra ${\rm L}(Γ)$. As applications, we provide a characterisation of $C^*$-simplicity, a condition for amenability of the group and show the existence and uniqueness of a maximal nuclear $Γ$-invariant unital $C^*$-subalgebra of $C^*_r(Γ)$. Moreover, we give a topological characterisation of exactness of any separable unital $C^*$-algebra. Finally, we study exotic random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$ and super-exotic random subalgebras of ${\rm L}(Γ)$, that is, random subalgebras which do not arise purely from random subgroups of $Γ$ and not from random subalgebras of $C^*_r(Γ)$, respectively.
Local Work, Global Progress: A Convergence Theory of AI Agent Collaboration

Teams of large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly applied to complex tasks, but their collaboration protocols are mostly designed empirically, without convergence guarantees. We formalize collaborative problem solving as block optimization: each agent improves one part of a shared solution, guided by its local objective plus a correction for how its changes affect the other parts. A coordinator checks every proposal against the global objective and merges proposals that do not interfere with each other. We prove linear convergence up to an error floor that vanishes when the corrections are exact. Interfering proposals can also be merged once their combination has been checked; the rate then depends on how well the proposals actually combine, not on worst-case interactions. With GPT-OSS-120B agents on robot routing, a three-agent team finds collision-free plans in every run, better than those of a single agent that controls all robots. On a larger routing task, a six-agent team completes its search about twice as fast as the single agent (in median). Merging the best checked combination of proposals, rather than only proposals that do not interfere, cuts the team's search time by about 30%. With constants measured on the runs, our convergence bound holds in every round and follows the observed progress. We also test the theory on query planning in SQLite and on a synthetic task.
Gaussian Integral Operator between Fock Spaces

We study Gaussian integral operators \[(Tf)(z)=\frac1π\int_{\mathbb C} e^{αz^2+β\overline w^{\,2}+γz\overline w+ηz+δ\overline w} f(w)e^{-|w|^2}\,dA(w)\] acting between Fock spaces $\mathcal F^p$ and $\mathcal F^q$, where $0<p,q\leq\infty$. We give complete characterizations of their boundedness and compactness in terms of explicit conditions on the parameters of the Gaussian kernel. The proofs are based on a unified approach combining reproducing-kernel estimates, atomic decompositions, and sampling sequences, together with a reduction to diagonal operators on sequence spaces. We also study Schatten-class membership on $\mathcal F^2$ and compute the Hilbert--Schmidt norm explicitly.
Closed maximal eventually different families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ and weakly Farah ideals
Jialiang He; Jiaheng Zhuang; Yi Zhou

Motivated by the existence of closed maximal $\mathcal{I}$-eventually different ($\mathcal{I}$-MED) families, we study uniform combinatorial properties of ideals. For a fixed ideal, a property is uniform if its witnesses can be chosen by a single Borel map. We prove that every $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideal is uniformly weakly $P^+$. We also prove that the classes of Farah and weakly Farah ideals coincide, answering a question of Hrušák and Meza-Alcántara. We then show that every weakly Farah ideal is uniformly weakly Ramsey. As an application, we obtain closed $\mathcal{I}$-MED families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideals and weakly Farah ideals.
Global $L^2$ Approximation in the Bergman Spaces with Values in Holomorphic Vector Bundles

In this paper, we get global $L^2$ approximation theorems in Bergman spaces with values in singular holomorphic vector bundles over Stein manifolds generalizing results of Li and Zhou. The main results combine strong openness property of multiplier submodule sheaf and twisted $L^2$ estimates of $\bar\partial$-equations.
A Complete Dichotomy for $L_\infty$ Permutation Removal
Viet Hung Le; Ruilin Shi; Fan Wei

We study the removal problem for permutation patterns under the normalized $L_\infty$ earth mover's distance. We prove a complete dichotomy. Let \[ \mathcal E =\{(12),(21),(132),(213),(231),(312)\}. \] If $σ\in\mathcal E$, then every permutation of length $n$ that is $\varepsilon$-far from being $σ$-free contains at least $\varepsilon(n-1)$ copies of $σ$; for $0<\varepsilon\le 1/16$, this is sharp up to a constant factor for all sufficiently large $n$. If $σ\in S_k\setminus\mathcal E$, then for every sufficiently large $n$ there is a permutation of length $n$ that is $1/(8k)$-far from being $σ$-free and contains exactly one copy of $σ$. Thus the usual positive-density removal conclusion fails for every nontrivial permutation pattern, but the sparse behavior is completely characterized: the minimum number of copies is linear for exactly six patterns and is one for all others. Consequently, no canonical one-sided tester that rejects only after finding a forbidden copy can have query complexity independent of the permutation length.
There can be equitable social welfare orders but no fair voting system

In the context of intergenerational equity it is natural to ask that social welfare orders have th properties of finite anonymity and strong Pareto efficiency. Such social welfare orders can be constructed from nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers, and the existence of ultrafilters of this kind is known to be equivalent to the existence of a fair voting system for a countably infinite population in the sense of Arrow's theorem. Unfortunately, the existence of this variety of social welfare order, which we call anonymous Pareto, implies the existence of nonmeasurable sets of real numbers. For some, such as Litak, this entails that such social welfare orders are inadmissible for use in theoretical economics because they are non-constructive in nature. The authors seek to give nuance to this view, proving that anonymous Pareto and other social welfare orders can exist in the absence of nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers.
Nonlocal geometric rigidity inequalities and the justification of linearized peridynamics

We prove geometric rigidity inequalities for vector fields using double-integral Gagliardo-type quantities. We show that the nonlocal-norm distance of the difference quotient of a vector field from the difference quotient of a single rigid motion is controlled by the same nonlocal norm of a difference characterizing the distance to the manifold of all rigid motions. The inequality is then used to show the variational convergence of a sequence of rescaled nonlocal fully nonconvex integral functionals to a linearized energy functional. Related functionals arise in peridynamic formulations of continuum mechanics via the total strain energy; this variational convergence provides a rigorous justification of linearized peridynamics with volume constraint via the convergence of rescaled displacements. We additionally establish analogous rigidity inequalities in the linearized setting, which can be thought of as nonlocal analogues of Korn's inequality for displacements.
Foliations and Laminar Currents for $C^2$ Maximal Plurisubharmonic Functions

Let $u\in C^2(Ω)\cap\mathrm{PSH}(Ω)$ satisfy $(dd^c u)^2=0$ on a domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{C}^2$. We prove that the positive-rank locus of its Levi form carries a foliation by holomorphic curves tangent to the Levi-null directions, along which $u$ is harmonic. The flow boxes are locally bi-Lipschitz; in particular, the Levi-null slope is locally Lipschitz in the transverse variable. The Levi current is uniformly laminar on the positive-rank locus, with an explicit transverse measure, and laminar on $Ω$. A smooth example also shows that the Levi current can be laminar without being uniformly laminar on the whole domain. The analytic construction combines a local partial Legendre transform with a Hardy-space boundary equation.
Small Viscosity Limit of Navier-Stokes Equations in A Quarter Plane with Navier Slip Conditions

We study the vanishing-viscosity limit of Leray solutions to the two-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a quarter plane with Navier slip boundary conditions on both edges for a class of compatible well-prepared initial data. By multi-scale analysis, we deduce that a boundary layer of order $O(\sqrtε)$ arises near each edge of the corner and is described by a linearized Prandtl equation, and near the corner, their overlap and nonlinear interaction are captured by a two-dimensional corner profile. Although this profile occurs at order $O(\sqrtε)$, it is governed, in the fast variables, by a nonlinear initial-boundary value problem of Navier--Stokes type. The well-posedness and Sobolev regularity of the outer flow problems, together with the well-posedness and weighted estimates of the boundary-layer and corner-layer problems are obtained on a common time interval $[0,T]$ independent of $ε$. To ensure the required regularity of the outer Euler flow in the critical right-angle domain, it is assumed that the initial vorticity of the outer leading order flow vanishes in a neighborhood of the corner. We then rigorously justify the resulting composite expansion in the small viscosity limit. More precisely, after retaining the leading outer flow, the two weak boundary layers, the nonlinear corner layer, and the order-$ε$ outer correction, the error between the exact solution and this truncated expansion is $O(ε^{5/4})$ in $L^\infty(0,T;L^2(\Q))$ and $O(ε^{3/4})$ in $L^2(0,T;H^1(\Q))$.
Proliferation Transitions for Quantum Doubles of Groups

Proliferation transitions are phase transitions between a 2+1d topological order $\mathcal{T}$ and another $\mathcal{T}/\mathcal{A}$, obtained by condensing anyons in an algebra $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{T}$. We consider such transitions in quantum doubles of groups, $\mathcal{T}=D(G, ω)$, for finite groups $G$ possibly with three-cocycle $ω$, for which condensable algebras are fully classified. Given a condensable algebra $\mathcal{A}$, we represent $\mathcal{T}$ in terms of a Symmetry Topological Field Theory (SymTFT), that is tailored to the $\mathcal{A}$ proliferation transition. The SymTFT bulk is constructed from the Müger center of the subcategory generated by the algebra, i.e. the category of transparent lines, which can be bosons or fermions. Properties of the transition can then be inferred directly from the algebra classification data. For gauged Landau-Ginzburg (LG*) type transitions, we show that they do not only depend on the anyons in $\mathcal{A}$ through their field content, but the cubic interactions are fixed in terms of the multiplication structure of $\mathcal{A}$. Applied to twin algebras, which have the same anyon content but different multiplication structures, we show that twins result in distinct proliferation transitions.
Oscillator representations of quantum affine orthosymplectic superalgebras II
Jae-Hoon Kwon; Sin-Myung Lee; Masato Okado

As a continuation of our study on quantum affine spin-oscillator correspondence, we introduce a category of $q$-oscillator representations of quantum affine superalgebras of type $XB$ ($X=B,D$) and construct irreducible objects in a uniform way. Under the truncation functor inspired by the theory of super duality, they are related to finite-dimensional irreducible representations of $U_q(D^{(2)}_{n+1})$ ($X=B$) or $U_q(B^{(1)}_{n})$ ($X=D$). We also considerably streamline our previous arguments, which clarifies how our construction can be understood as a quantum affinization of classical super duality.

We produce the first known strictly convex ergodic billiards: sufficiently asymmetric lemon billiards. These billiard tables are the intersection of two circles of which one contains the centers of both. We previously proved that they have \emph{uniformly} hyperbolic returns to a suitable section, and we here control singularity curves, with an approach that seems new. This implies ergodicity and indeed the Bernoulli property.
Timing and Reliability Limits of Position-Assisted UWB Multicast Audio

One-to-many ultra-wideband (UWB) transport can disseminate shared audio blocks without replicating a downlink stream for every receiver. Yet common reception does not ensure aligned electrical playback, coincident acoustic arrival, or delivery to an entire receiver group. This paper develops a unified feasibility analysis of position-assisted UWB multicast audio that separates clock and actuation error, age-dependent acoustic propagation compensation, correlated block erasures, and reserved communication resources. We derive a conditional bound on one-listener arrival spread, a stationary expression for all-receiver block delivery under common and receiver-local losses, and complementary bounds for reliability-constrained admission. Reproducible Monte Carlo experiments examine 4,590 policy--run records across clock, localization, channel, and slot configurations. For eight receivers, affine clock correction produces a mean run-level 95th-percentile electronic span of $21.19\us$, while position assistance reduces the corresponding one-listener acoustic arrival span from $21.95\ms$ to $419.43\us$. Under the stated $30\us$ timing criterion, 98.86\% of compensated events still exceed the threshold. For 64 receivers, three block copies attain an all-receiver delivery probability of approximately 0.97478 under the modeled correlated channel. The analysis exposes the distinct failure mechanisms of position age, shared fades, retransmission limits, and schedule saturation, and establishes joint criteria for interpreting synchronous multicast audio performance.
Density Evolution for Stochastic Dynamical Systems Driven by α-Stable Processes: An Equation-Free Numerical Approach

While well-established approaches exist for computing probability densities of stochastic differential equations driven by Brownian motion, computing probability densities for general stochastic differential equations driven by α-stable processes remains challenging, and few general-purpose methods are available. A major difficulty is that the corresponding Fokker--Planck equations governing the density are generally unavailable in explicit form. In this paper, we develop an efficient approach to compute probability densities for stochastic differential equations driven by α-stable processes without relying on Fokker--Planck equations or any other governing equations. The proposed approach is easy to implement and computationally efficient. Numerical examples demonstrate its effectiveness and indicate an approximately first-order convergence rate with respect to the time step.
Kähler-Ricci Shrinkers with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature

We prove that every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature is holomorphically isometric to $\mathbb{C}^k\times N^{n-k}$ for some $0\le k\le n$, where $\mathbb{C}^k$ is the Gaussian shrinker and $N$ is a compact Kähler--Ricci shrinker with nonnegative Ricci curvature. As a corollary, every complete Kähler--Ricci shrinker with quasi-positive Ricci curvature is compact.
A necessary condition for a Romanoff type theorem

Let $\{a_k\}_{k\ge1}$ be an infinite strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with $a_k\mid a_{k+1}$ for every integer $k\ge1$. Dai and Pan proved that the set of integers of the form $p^2+q^2+a_k+a_l$, where $p,q$ are primes and $k,l\ge1$, has positive lower asymptotic density if $\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log a_k}{k}<\infty$ and $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d<\infty$. They also asked whether the latter condition is necessary. In this paper, we show that this condition is necessary by proving that if $\sup_{k\ge1}\sum_{d\mid a_k}\frac1d=\infty$, then this set has asymptotic density zero.
From the Optimal $L^2$-Estimates \((p,n)\) and \((n,p)\)-Forms to Uniform Griffiths \(p\)-Positivity via Convolution and Restriction

We prove that the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is preserved under standard convolution regularization. As an application, we show that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((p,n)\)-forms is uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive. By establishing the restriction property, we prove that a singular Hermitian metric satisfying the optimal \(L^2\)-estimate property for \((n,p)\)-forms is also uniform Griffiths \(p\)-positive.
Likelihood-Based Confidence Curves for Bounded Parameters
Hedvig Borgen Reiersrud; Clara Bertinelli Salucci; Riccardo De Bin; Alessandra Rosalba Brazzale

When a parameter is bounded, the likelihood ratio statistic does not generally follow the chi-square limit distribution of Wilks' theorem. In fact, its asymptotic null distribution depends on the distance from the null value to the boundary, interpolating between the chi-bar-square law on the boundary and the chi-square law in the deep interior of the parameter space. We derive this distribution and use it to construct confidence curves, which are nested collections of two-sided confidence intervals or regions, for bounded parameters. We extend the existing result for the scalar parameter to a two-dimensional parameter with one or both components bounded. As the bivariate distributions are integrals of normal distributions, which are not reducible to standard statistical functions, we also give a simpler approximated distribution obtained by moment-matching. We illustrate the methods on a canonical analysis from high-energy physics, namely the Poisson signal-plus-background experiment.
A twisted Marchenko lemma and applications
Jun-Yang Zhang; Shi-Hao Li; Shou-Feng Shen

We develop a twisted Marchenko lemma with applications into non-commutative two-component integrable systems. Starting from a twisted differential equation, we introduce the corresponding two-component Wronski matrix $W_{n,m}(\boldsymbolϕ,\boldsymbolψ)$. Under the Marchenko lemma conditions, the logarithmic derivative $(\partial W_{n,m})W_{n,m}^{-1}$ satisfies nonlinear equations, whose two-component projections yield a non-commutative two-component KP equation, while a single-component reduction recovers the non-commutative Burgers equation, KP equation and DS equation. A direct approach based on two-component quasi-Wronskians is developed, from which a higher-order non-commutative two-component KP equation is generated with matrix-valued solutions. Reductions of the seed functions of the non-commutative two-component KP hierarchy yield the one-component counterpart, while a stepwise reduction of those for the two-component KP equation gives the non-commutative DS and NLS equations.
Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass

We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8π$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates do not rule out growth as time tends to infinity, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.
Hausdorff dimension of the singular set in optimal transport
Shibing Chen; Qi-Rui Li; Yuanyuan Li; Jiakun Liu; Xiaotian Wu
