On a single central processing unit (CPU) core, and even without its GPU or parallel paths, it is the fastest of the packages we compared across languages, matching the closest packages only for plug-in discrete entropy and substantially faster for mutual information, the conditional and transfer measures, and the kernel, ordinal, and generalised-entropy estimators. The optional GPU and multi-threaded paths accelerate selected continuous estimators further. The library is open source and, to our knowledge, the most complete information-theory package for Rust.
Kurzweil's impulsive inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian
Stanislav Antontsev; Pardeep Kumar; Ivan Kuznetsov

In the present paper, we proceed with the research initiated in (S. Antontsev \emph{et al.}, Inverse Problems, 2021). We study the inverse problem for the Kelvin--Voigt equations with $p$-Laplacian and with a right-hand side in the integral over-determination condition, which approximates a discontinuous function at $t=0$. We rescale the problem in a neighbourhood $[0,1/n]$ and pass to the limit as $n$ approaches infinity. This leads to the inverse problem on an infinitesimal initial layer, which transforms the initial velocity into a new one.
Mass Deformations and Sheets in Logahoric Higgs Moduli

We use the framework of the logahoric Hitchin integrable system introduced in our earlier work and the sheets of the Lie algebra in order to describe the tame defects in a six dimensional $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ superconformal theory under mass deformations. We show that varying leaves of fixed dimension in the Hitchin system amounts to varying residue orbits of fixed dimension. Moreover, we verify the period and dimension conditions in mass-like deformations, as proposed by Balasubramanian--Distler, thus realizing the sheets of the Lie algebra on the Poisson moduli space of logahoric Higgs torsors.
Thompson's group $F$ is not weakly amenable

Let $F$ be Thompson's group, and let $D$ be the set of dyadic rationals in $[0,1]$. We give an embedding of $\mathbb Z^{(D)}\rtimes F$ into $F$, where the semidirect product is defined by the natural action of $F$ on $D$. Using this embedding, we deduce from the nonamenability of $F$ that $F$ is not weakly amenable.
Supercuspidal blocks and the local Langlands correspondence

Let $G$ be a connected reductive group defined over a non-archimedean local field $F$, and let $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ be a supercuspidal Bernstein block. In this paper, we define a cohomology class $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ represented by a 2-cocycle that encodes the equivalence class of $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$. We then formulate a conjecture describing $[μ_{\mathfrak{s}}]$ in terms of the enhanced $L$-parameter $(φ, ρ)$ attached to an irreducible representation in $\mathrm{Rep}^{\mathfrak{s}}(G(F))$ via the conjectural local Langlands correspondence. Finally, we verify this conjecture for the local Langlands correspondence for non-singular supercuspidal representations constructed by Kaletha.
Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
Wouter Castryck; Bogdan Adrian Dina; Péter Kutas; Gioella Lorenzon

We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.
Schrödinger estimates with arbitrarily small periodic regularity on $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{T}$

Let $M=\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{T}$ carry its product metric. We prove that the Schrödinger evolution maps $L^2(\mathbb{H}^2;H^s(\mathbb{T}))$ into $L^2([0,1];L^6(M))$ for every $s>0$, without any regularity assumption in the hyperbolic variable. The proof separates hyperbolic and periodic frequencies. A localized hyperbolic kernel estimate restricts the effective interaction time at hyperbolic frequency $L$ to order $L^{-1}$. Quadratic exponential sums then give a logarithmic bound when the periodic bandwidth is comparable to $L$. A mixed-norm decoupling argument, including an $L^6$-valued extension and a periodic transference step, reduces wider periodic bands to this case. The infimum of the admissible periodic regularities is therefore zero. The estimate at zero regularity is not established here.
Johannes Anschütz; Arthur-César Le Bras; Juan Esteban Rodríguez Camargo; Peter Scholze

We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory
On the Fluctuations of Associated Primes and Depths of Powers of Monomial Ideals
Mircea Cimpoeas; Mehrdad Nasernejad; Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

In this paper, we investigate the fluctuation phenomenon in the sets of associated primes and depths of powers of monomial ideals. We provide affirmative answers to two open questions posed in [8] concerning the existence of monomial ideals in K[x,y,z] whose associated primes exhibit prescribed patterns of appearance, disappearance, and reappearance of the maximal ideal across specified ranges of powers. For each construction, we also derive the corresponding fluctuation in depths. Furthermore, we construct a square-free monomial ideal that is nearly normally torsion-free but fails to satisfy the persistence property, thereby answering a question posed in [20] in the negative. This example arises as the edge ideal of the ideal minimally non-packing clutter Q_10, revealing an intriguing connection between combinatorial optimization and the algebraic properties of monomial ideals.
U-Examples: A Unified Family of Worst-Case Instances for Optimization Algorithms

Worst-case instances show where optimization algorithms fail: the Klee-Minty cube for the simplex method, ill-conditioned and rippled bowls for gradient descent, degenerate minima for Newton's method, redundant Klee-Minty cubes for interior-point methods, unprunable trees for branch-and-bound, deceptive landscapes for metaheuristics, and degenerate cycling for active-set methods. These constructions were developed over seventy years in separate literatures, each with its own tools. This survey reviews them together. We trace the history of rule-specific worst cases across seven representative algorithm classes and organize them with one reading: in each, the optimum lies near the start, yet the algorithm's own update rule is misdirected onto a long trajectory or, at the boundary, into a non-terminating loop. We call such an instance a U-Example; the letter U stands both for the unification and for the U-shaped bowls around which descent methods are made to crawl. A common framework treats every algorithm as a rule on a state space with a progress potential, so that one definition of misdirection, and of the resulting blow-up in cost, covers pivoting, descent, interior-point, tree-search, and population methods. Each member is drawn in a common visual grammar and quantified in general dimension $n$. The blow-up is independent of the dimension for the two descent members and exponential in it for four search members, with degenerate cycling as a breakdown. We connect the constructions to neighbouring theories (oracle complexity, performance estimation, smoothed analysis, and the complexity of local search), each of which asks a different question of the same instances. We then map each worst case to the remedy that defeats it, examine how robust the instances are, and close with open challenges, in particular whether a worst case can be predicted from the update rule alone.
DeHNSSo-v2: A compressible, curvilinear, and efficient extension of the Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver
Pietro Carlo Boldini; Yifu Chen; Marios Kotsonis

We present DeHNSSo-v2, a major update of DeHNSSo-v1 (Westerbeek et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 302, 2024), the open-source Delft Harmonic Navier-Stokes Solver for nonlinear stability analysis of shear flows. The new release adds a compressible formulation on general two-dimensional body-fitted geometries, automatic grid generation, linear-cost sparse assembly, reusable per-mode factorizations, and Newton pseudo-arclength continuation for high-amplitude nonlinear solutions. The curvilinear formulation preserves the fourth-order accuracy of the discretization on strongly distorted grids, and the compressible solver is confirmed to reproduce DeHNSSo-v1 in the incompressible limit. Validation spans published benchmarks for linear instability of compressible flat-plate boundary layers from $\mathrm{Ma}=0.5$ to $\mathrm{Ma}=4.5$, nonlinear oblique-mode breakdown at $\mathrm{Ma}=1.6$, nonlinear swept-wing crossflow compared with direct numerical simulations, and linear Tollmien-Schlichting wave interaction with a modeled surface-embedded Helmholtz resonator compared with experimentally validated linearized Navier-Stokes simulations. On the nonlinear test cases of DeHNSSo-v1, the computational developments result in a speed-up of approximately one order of magnitude. The $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry

We settle a central conjecture in this field: we show that the $m=2$ amplituhedron is a positive geometry. Our main new tool is a Hodge-theoretic criterion for being a positive geometry, connecting the work of Brown--Dupont with the original setup of Arkani-Hamed--Bai--Lam.

Together with the standard compact containment and boundary conditions, these estimates are both necessary and sufficient for $M_1$ tightness. As a consequence, we derive tractable and general sufficient conditions for additive functionals of strong Markov processes. The Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture for the Fisher-KPP equation
Hongjun Guo; Kelei Wang; Maolin Zhou

We resolve the Hamel-Nadirashvili conjecture, which concerns the classification of all [0,1]-valued entire solutions of Fisher-KPP equations with concave C^2 reaction terms in arbitrary space dimension. We prove that every such solution is a C_{loc}^{1,2} limit of solutions generated by finitely many planar traveling fronts, possibly together with a spatially homogeneous solution. We prove Lyapunov instability wherever the field $B$ does not vanish (under $C^1$ regularity), and at every isolated zero of $B$ provided it is real-analytic. For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.
Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems

Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, I: radiation conditions and a Rellich-type theorem

The boundary then carries a bound transverse mode, and at each energy $E > 0$ the system propagates two channels with the distinct wavenumbers $\sqrt{E}$ and $\sqrt{E+α^2}$: bulk waves decaying like $|x|^{-(n-1)/2}$ and surface waves decaying like $|x'|^{-(n-2)/2}$. This Part I treats the flat boundary, and its purpose is to develop, at that endpoint, the scattering theory of the two channels in full. We prove a limiting absorption principle $\mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{B}^*$, construct the generalized Fourier transform, derive an expansion of the resolvent at infinity in which the two channels appear in a single relation, characterize the solutions of $\mathcal{B}^*$ growth, and compute the scattering matrix. The radiation condition is imposed on the solution itself, with no decomposition into channels, and is shown to be equivalent to the vanishing of the incoming data. The main result is a Rellich-type theorem whose hypotheses are imposed only near infinity and which forces both channels to vanish simultaneously. The surface channel turns out to be rigid: its block of the scattering matrix is the identity and carries no information about $α$, so that on the band $-α^2 < E < 0$ the scattering matrix is trivial. Computing excited states of dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates by constrained gentlest ascent dynamics

Dipolar Bose--Einstein condensates (BECs), i.e., BECs with long-range dipole-dipole interactions (DDI), exhibit extraordinarily rich physics and serve as a versatile experimental platform for exploring exotic quantum states of matter. Within the mean-field framework, a dipolar BEC can be described by the Gross--Pitaevskii (GP) model with a DDI term. Its stationary states consist of the ground state, which minimizes the GP energy functional under the normalization constraint, and excited states, which are higher-energy critical points that typically correspond to constrained saddle points. Excited states encode collective excitation modes and play a key role in the dynamical stability and quantum phase transitions of cold-atom systems. However, in contrast to the extensively studied ground state, they remain far less explored numerically, especially in dipolar systems. Specifically, a semi-implicit sine-pseudospectral discretization with an orthonormalization correction step is adopted, and the nonlocal DDI terms are evaluated efficiently and accurately via the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT). The resulting scheme is applied to one-, two-, and three-dimensional dipolar BECs, enabling a detailed numerical investigation of their excited states. Remarkably, our simulations reveal that excited states can persist even in regimes where the ground state of the condensate becomes mean-field unstable. Classification of positive solutions to the critical Lane-Emden system

Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints

For the third method, we introduce a novel differentiable flow-matching surrogate that reduces the cost of a single forward map evaluation at the price of a distribution shift depending on the training distribution used for the surrogate. We apply the framework to the generation of virtual patient cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops along aortic geometries affected by coarctation, and we validate and compare the three methods on synthetic data.

We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.

Our main contribution addresses the second one. Since all solutions are translates of one profile, the initial condition can be replaced by an equivalent interior condition. For an unknown $u=φ(y)$, imposing it where the speed $|φ'f_q|$ of $u$ along the orbit is maximal bounds the propagator of the linearized equation by one; for $u=\ln y$ this is $y(x^\ast)=(q-1)/q$. For the first obstacle we use the sinh map of Tee and Trefethen: the time function is explicit, the complex singularities of the profile lie exactly at $\pm(2k+1)πi$, and the map parameters follow in closed form, so that $O(\ln(1/μ))$ nodes suffice. Instead, we linearize the functional directly in the target distribution, obtaining an influence-function expansion with a remainder controlled by the transport-map error. The influence function is characterized by a linear elliptic partial differential equation. Under regularity conditions, we use this expansion to prove central limit theorems in low dimensions and establish validity of the empirical bootstrap. We also derive semiparametric efficiency bounds and show that the plug-in estimators attain them under the same conditions.
Plasticity of the unit sphere of the space $c_0$
In this paper, we prove that the unit sphere of the space $c_{0}$ is plastic, i.e., every non-expansive bijection from this sphere onto itself is an isometry.

We obtain explicit free-field realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (0 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 1)$, $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$, and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$. In particular, the realizations of $\mathcal{SW} B (1 , 2)$ and $\mathcal{SW} B (2 , 2)$ are new. Using these realizations, we compute central charges, conformal weights, and eigenvalues of the generating currents on free-field highest-weight states, and construct the local integrals of motion $I_1$, $I_3$, and $I_5$.

This class contains the fundamental family of infinitely divisible distributions and its new extension, the set of rational-(quasi-)infinitely divisible laws. We prove that this class is dense in the family of all probability laws with respect to the total variation distance. We show that characteristic functions corresponding to this class admit Lévy-Khinchine type representations. In these formulas, the generalized spectral functions (the regularized Lévy measures) are special continuous linear functionals on the union of well known Bernstein spaces of entire functions of exponential type which are additionally bounded on the real line. We apply this spectral functions in criteria of weak convergence of distributions within the class under study. All necessary analytical constructions are proposed.
Finite groups with large sum of element orders compared to cyclic groups

The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.
Beta-expansions induced by general Parry polynomials and sharp iteration asymptotics of their transfer operators

Payoff Polarization and Garbage Concentration in a Stochastic Garbage Disposal Game

We investigate the long-term behavior of both payoffs and garbage distributions. We prove that payoff dispersion grows at least linearly in time almost surely, leading to payoff polarization, with the maximum and minimum payoffs diverging to positive and negative infinity, respectively. When disposal is complete and the underlying graph is connected, we further prove that all garbage becomes concentrated on a single agent after a finite random time, although the agent holding the garbage may change over time. These results characterize the emergence of payoff inequality and garbage concentration in stochastic competitive interactions on networks.
A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
Likun Qiu; Jianguo Huang; Xuejun Xu

The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.
Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations

In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation

In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

Thus, in this approximation phonons have a well-defined velocity, which we compute.

In this paper, the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres are defined. Then, a new family of non-null ruled surfaces associated with hyper-dual Lorentzian curves is defined via the E.Study hyper-map in Minkowski space and the definitions of the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres. Within this framework, the resulting non-null ruled surfaces are classified. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.
Absolute winning properties of exceptional sets for rational maps

We study Schmidt's game on the Julia set $J(f)$ of weak hyperbolic rational maps $f:\CC\to\CC$. For each $y\in J(f)$, let $E(f,y)$ be the set of points in $J(f)$ whose forward orbits stay a positive distance from $y$. We prove that $E(f,y)$ is absolute winning on $J(f)$ for each $y \in J(f)$. To do this, we first prove the absolute winning property for the exceptional set associated to the critical points by a potential game argument, and then use uniform expansion to obtain the result for each target point $y$.
Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families

We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.
Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions

For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $ω(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leqω(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.
Size and spectral radius conditions for the existence of $k$-factor in graphs with given minimum degree
Zengzhao Xu; Bo Deng; Ligong Wang

In recent years, characterizing the conditions for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in graphs has received significant academic attention. For integers $b\ge a\ge 1$, an $[a, b]$-factor of a graph $G$ is defined as a spanning subgraph $H$ such that $a\le d_{H}(v)\le b$ for every $v\in V(G)$. If $a=b=k$, a $[k, k]$-factor is called a $k$-factor of $G$. Let $δ(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. Hao and Li [Electron. J. Combin. (2024)] posed the problem of characterizing the size or spectral radius conditions for a graph to contain an $[a,b]$-factor with $δ(G)\ge a$. Fan, Lin and Zhu [Discrete Math. (2026)] solved the size version of this problem for the case $a < b.$ In this paper, for $a=b=k$, we characterize the size condition for a graph to have a $k$-factor with $δ(G)\ge k$. Using this result, we also characterize the spectral radius and distance spectral radius conditions for a graph to have a $k$-factor, respectively.
Orbital stability of standing waves for defocusing fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equations with a delta potential
Ramón G. Plaza; Miguel A. Sánchez-Alcántara

In this paper, a fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a delta potential and a repulsive nonlinearity in one space dimension is considered. First, it is proved that the Cauchy problem in Sobolev spaces on the real line is globally well-posed, independently of the sign of the delta potential. Moreover, in the case of an attractive delta potential, the existence, the minimization properties and the orbital stability of standing waves under the flow of the equation are established. The stability proof is based on concentration-compactness methods for the energy/charge functional. For that purpose, no explicit calculation of the standing waves is required and the results are based on the variational properties of the solutions alone.
A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
Minoru Hirose; Hideki Murahara; Shingo Saito

We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.
Control variates for dry friction under colored noise: variance rates for non-smooth observables

A control variate method was introduced by Garnier and Mertz (2022) for multivalued stochastic differential equations driven by colored noise. For smooth observables, the asymptotic variance is $O(\varepsilon^{2})$, where $\varepsilon^{2}$ is the correlation time of the noise. However, for non-smooth reliability observables, such as threshold indicators and overshoot severities, rate estimates have not been established in general. In this paper, rate estimates are derived for the inertial dry-friction inclusion driven by colored noise in the three regimes whose white-noise propagators are known. The asymptotic variance of the resulting control variate estimators is $O(\varepsilon^{2α})$ for $α$-Hölder observables with $α\in(0,1]$, $O(\varepsilon)$ for observables of bounded variation satisfying a one-sided continuity condition, $O(\varepsilon^{1+α})$ for observables that are both $α$-Hölder and of bounded variation, and $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{2,1+2α\}})$ for observables with finitely many $α$-cusps, where $α\in (0, 1]$ is the cusp exponent. The last three bounds hold up to logarithmic factors. Bounds on the bias of the white-noise approximation and non-asymptotic sample-size estimates are also derived, and the comparison principle is shown to be preserved under coupled time discretization. Numerical experiments in the three regimes support the predicted rates.
Bulk limits of the truncated circular beta ensembles
Yun Li; Mingchang Liu; Joseph Najnudel

We study the bulk limits of the rank-one truncation of the circular beta ensembles obtained by deleting the first row and column. We prove that the normalized Blaschke products of the truncated circular beta ensembles converge in law to a constant multiple (depending on $β$) of the i.i.d.~Gaussian analytic function (GAF) uniformly on compacts of the unit disk. As a consequence, we identify the bulk point process limit with the zero set of GAF, which was proved in the seminal work of Peres and Virág to form a determinantal point process with the Bergman kernel. Our method also applies to the rank-one multiplicative perturbations of the circular beta ensembles in the mesoscopic regime.
Spectral analysis of multi-bubble solutions to the Brezis-Nirenberg problem

We investigate weighted spectral limits for separated multi-bubble configurations and refined spectral asymptotics for the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[ -Δu=u^p+\varepsilon u^q, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }Ω, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb R^N$ with $N\geq3$, $p=(N+2)/(N-2)$, $1\leq q<p$ and $\varepsilon$ is a positive parameter. We first determine the limits of the ordered weighted eigenvalues associated with families of positive functions admitting an $m$-bubble decomposition at distinct interior points with a remainder vanishing in $H_0^1(Ω)$. The limiting eigenvalues are those of the single-bubble problem, with all multiplicities multiplied by $m$. We then refine this analysis for positive multi-bubble solutions of this problem with comparable concentration scales, deriving precise expansions of the first $(N+2)m$ eigenvalues and characterizing their eigenfunctions when $1<q<3$ if $N=4$ or $1\leq q<p$ if $N\geq5$. The leading corrections are determined by explicit symmetric matrices involving $q$, the concentration parameters, and the Green and Robin functions. In particular, we prove that the dilation matrix is positive definite. Together, these spectral results yield Morse index bounds for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, with an exact formula when the matrix governing the translation modes is invertible.
5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
Hitoshi Ikemori; Shinsaku Kitakado; Yoshimitsu Matsui; Toshiyuki Okubo; Toshiro Sato

We derive the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem from the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator through symplectic reduction. By rewriting the moment maps of the harmonic oscillator in terms of five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we identify the moment map expected to yield the Runge-Lenz vector. We then perform the reduction with respect to the SU(2) symmetry, derive the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian, and show explicitly that the identified moment map reduces to the Runge-Lenz vector.
Constant Step Sizes for Muon-Type Spectral Optimizers on Strongly Convex Quadratics
Pratik Jawanpuria; Bhabatosh Garai; Bamdev Mishra

Muon and related optimizers update a weight matrix with a spectrally transformed gradient. In this work, we study such spectral optimizers with a constant step size on strongly convex matrix quadratics, which isolate the effect of the update from the confounds of nonconvexity, noise, and step size schedules. We analyze an update using two quantities: the gain, which is the factor by which it amplifies the gradient along each singular direction, and the length, which is the norm of the update. These two quantities place the popular spectral updates in three regimes with different behavior: (i) with a bounded gain, the iterates behave like preconditioned gradient descent and converge for step sizes set by the largest curvature; (ii) with an unbounded gain but a vanishing length, they still converge, with the admissible step sizes set by the total curvature instead; and (iii) with a non-vanishing length, they do not converge for almost every initialization. Interestingly, the practical variants of Muon fall in all three regimes, depending only on how the update is normalized and scaled and not on the polynomial that approximates the polar factor. Experiments validate these findings.
Efficient Perturbation-Based SC Decoding for Long Polar Codes
Zhongjun Yang; Zhichen Liu; Li Chen; Xianbin Wang; Huazi Zhang

Soft information perturbations can significantly improve the successive cancellation (SC) decoding performance of polar codes. This is an effective method for realizing low-latency yet high performance for long polar codes, since each perturbation-based SC (PSC) decoding can be performed in parallel. However, little theoretical insight has been revealed so far regarding its work rationale. This paper provides the theoretical analysis of the soft information perturbation. It reveals that PSC decoding improves the SC decoding performance through correcting the erroneous bit estimations, especially the first erroneous bit (FEB). It further validates that perturbing the soft information does not degrade the error-correction capability of SC decoding. Such revelations lead to the design of optimal perturbations that maximizes the FEB correction probability, resulting in an enhanced PSC decoding performance. Based on this, a novel hybrid PSC (HPSC) decoding is proposed. By introducing the random and biased perturbations, the HPSC decoding can better divert from the initial erroneous estimation and converge to the intended one. Our simulation results demonstrate that with the optimal perturbation, the HPSC decoding can achieve a similar performance as the cyclic redundancy check (CRC) aided SC list (CA-SCL) decoding, while avoiding path sorting and expansion.
Information, Estimation, and Prediction for Discrete Memoryless Channels via Poissonization

We develop information--estimation relations for an arbitrary discrete memoryless channel with finite input and output alphabets by varying the expected number of observations while keeping the channel fixed. A single hidden input is observed through a \textit{Poisson} number of conditionally independent channel uses, whose mean specifies the observation budget. The derivative of mutual information with respect to this budget equals the minimum expected relative-entropy loss for estimating the input's output distribution. The posterior average of the channel's output distributions achieves this minimum and is the Bayesian predictor for the next observation. When the input distribution, the channel, or both are misspecified, the relative entropy between the true and assumed observation laws is the integral of the excess prediction loss over the budget. We also extend these relations to finite-state processes taking values in the input alphabet and observed through the channel at independent Poisson sampling times. Both in the matched setting and under model mismatch, the expected prediction loss accumulated over time using past observations equals the corresponding loss using the full observation record (noncausal estimation), averaged over lower sampling rates. We also characterize how redundancy between two outputs selects among input distributions that achieve one-use capacity. For the coupon-collector channel, where each observation is sampled uniformly from an unknown subset, we derive the exact capacity loss of any input distribution. In particular, balanced subset families can substantially reduce the input alphabet while preserving the leading capacity terms.
Eliminating the Higgs field and perturbing Yang-Mills connections in cone Yang-Mills theory

We study the configurations of the cone Yang-Mills functional over a closed connected manifold. We show that the Euler-Lagrange equation from variations in the Higgs field is always uniquely solvable for $ζ\neq 0$, allowing us to eliminate one of the two equations from the theory. By eliminating the equation, we obtain a family of ``effective cone Yang-Mills functionals'' on the space of connection 1-forms indexed by $ζ$, which reduce to Yang-Mills theory when $ζ= 0$. This suggests a way to nontrivially deform the Yang-Mills moduli space. We take the first step towards this deformation by showing that, near certain critical points of the Yang-Mills functional, there is a family of smooth connections $A_t$ which satisfy the $tζ$-cone Yang-Mills equations.
Sharp boundedness criteria for nonnegative kernels on regular curves in the Heisenberg group

In this paper we study singular integrals associated with the nonnegative kernels \[ K_α(x,y,z)=\frac{|z|^{α/2}}{\|(x,y,z)\|^{α+1}}, \qquad α>0, \] in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb H$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Korányi norm. This family was introduced by Chousionis and Li. We first show that there exists a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve $E\subset\mathbb H$ such that the singular integrals associated with $K_α$ are unbounded on $L^2(E)$ for every $0<α<4$. This extends the counterexamples of Chousionis, Li and Zhang from $0<α<2$ to the full range $0<α<4$. Combined with the boundedness theorem of Fässler and Orponen for $α\ge4$, our result determines the exact range of exponents for boundedness on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve. We also consider the more general kernels \[ K_Φ(p)=\frac{1}{\|p\|} Φ\!\left(\frac{|z|^{1/2}}{\|p\|}\right), \qquad p=(x,y,z)\neq0, \] where $Φ:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $Φ(0)=0$. We show that the associated singular integral is $L^2$-bounded on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve if and only if $Φ(u)=O(u^4)$ as $u\to0$. When this condition fails, we construct a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve on which the operator is unbounded. The curves in both constructions can be chosen as horizontal lifts of planar $C^1$ graphs with arbitrarily small slope.
Forest Characterization of When SDP-RLT Strengthens RLT for Bilinear Terms
Hayato Watanabe; Takami Sato; Kazuhide Nakata; Ken Kobayashi

We study two relaxations for bilinear terms in box-constrained variables: the reformulation-linearization technique (RLT) relaxation and the SDP-RLT relaxation, which combines RLT with semidefinite programming (SDP). We represent the pattern of bilinear terms by an undirected graph, with one vertex for each variable and one edge for each bilinear term. A point feasible for the RLT relaxation fixes only part of the lifted matrix of the SDP-RLT relaxation, leaving the remaining entries to be chosen subject to the diagonal RLT inequalities, and the two relaxations differ exactly when these entries cannot always be chosen so that the matrix becomes positive semidefinite. Formulating this as a positive semidefinite matrix completion problem, we show that the feasible regions of the two relaxations coincide if and only if the graph is a forest. We also measure how large the difference can be when the graph contains a complete bipartite subgraph: a bilinear objective given by a Hadamard matrix yields optimal values whose ratio grows with the size of that subgraph.
Anytime-Valid Runtime Monitoring of Learned Barrier Certificates
Zhipeng Cao; Taoran Wu; Weiru Cui; Luke Ong; Bai Xue

Learned barrier certificates provide a principled mechanism for establishing safety of stochastic systems, but their validity may deteriorate during deployment when the underlying dynamics differ from those used for training. We propose an anytime-valid runtime monitor that audits a learned barrier certificate using observed closed-loop trajectories. The monitor is intended to detect loss of statistical support for the deployed barrier condition; it does not by itself guarantee detection before unsafe entry or safety of a subsequent intervention. Specifically, the conditional barrier-drift condition is formulated as an episode-wise sequential hypothesis test, and observed barrier increments are transformed into a nonnegative test supermartingale, yielding finite-sample false-alarm control under arbitrary stopping times. Inspired by finite-horizon safety verification, we further introduce a deterministic temporal shaping of the monitoring boundary, making the monitor more conservative early in a prescribed deployment horizon while preserving anytime-validity. The monitor is designed to detect statistical evidence that the safety certificate is no longer consistent with the observed dynamics, rather than to predict unsafe entry. To assess the monitor empirically, we evaluate empirical alarm behavior under valid and invalid certificates. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/runtime-barrier-monitor.

We study prescribed holomorphic lattices for regular-singular connections and residual factors of quantum $F$-bundles. For an arbitrary ordered monodromy spectrum, we classify the fully framed local groupoid: each residue fibre is a discrete affine space of dimension $r(r-1)$, with a unique normal form and trivial stabilisers. We then analyse elementary changes of lattice. A strictly positive integral residue difference obstructs the oriented wall; otherwise, in arbitrary rank, the extending normal-form arcs form an affine torsor of relative dimension $r(r-1)$, and specialisation to the shifted residue slice is polynomial and triangular by root height. Adjacent walls exhibit the composite-root correction dictated by the type-$A$ root-subgroup relations, while an example over the dual numbers detects a nilpotent saturation defect. For one-branch $F$-bundles, the scalar branch is recovered from the residual trace, and scalar residualisation yields a symmetric monoidal equivalence with zero-branch $F$-bundles. This construction yields residual atoms, functorial Jordan strata, and a residual chemical formula compatible with blow-ups and projective bundles. In the $A$-model, residualisation removes the unit direction; the rationally marked large-radius residual germ recovers the divisor cubic and distinguishes the marked residual germs of the Pfaffian and Grassmannian Calabi--Yau threefolds.
Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups

We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of the generalized cactus group associated with a finite standard parabolic subgroup of the underlying Coxeter group. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types B, D, E, F, and H, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine the associated generalized cactus group directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When the Coxeter diagram has finitely many vertices, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups. In type A, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group on $n$ strands if and only if it embeds into a Sylow 2-subgroup of the symmetric group on $n$ letters. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types A and B and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.
The law of large numbers for non-additive capacities without continuity

We consider a capacity on a general measurable space associated with a sequence of identically distributed random variables. With a weak assumption concerned with the independence and very few restrictions on the capacity, we show that, on a set with full lower-capacity, any cluster point of empirical averages lies in the mean interval with the lower and upper Choquet integrals of the random variables being its bounds, and, under a Fubini-independent product capacity introduced by Ghirardato (1997), cluster points fill the whole mean interval with full upper-capacity. The results give answers to two open questions of Terán (2014).
Maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems

We determine the maximum ranks of free abelian subgroups of generalized cactus groups associated with finite Coxeter systems. To obtain the upper bounds, we use the cubical flat torus theorem of Wise and Woodhouse. We then verify the sharpness of these upper bounds by constructing free abelian subgroups of the corresponding ranks. Our result shows that the maximal ranks of free abelian subgroups of ordinary cactus groups can be larger than conjectured by Genevois. As an application, we show that these groups are not quasi-isometric to any right-angled Artin group unless they are virtually free abelian.
Multi-time-stepping splitting scheme with mass lumping for the multiscale wave equation
Yating Wang; Wing Tat Leung; Zhengya Yang; Shufan Li

Efficient simulation of wave propagation in high-contrast media is challenging because standard explicit schemes are subject to severe time-step restrictions induced by fine spatial scales and fast multiscale modes, whereas fully implicit schemes require costly globally coupled solves. In this work, we develop a mass-lumped multi-time-stepping partially explicit splitting method for multiscale wave equations. Based on a nonlocal multicontinuum (NLMC) decomposition of the approximation space, the solution is separated into contrast-dependent fast components and contrast-independent slow components, which are advanced implicitly and explicitly, respectively. A mass-lumping approximation diagonalizes the coarse-scale mass operator and removes the coupling between two subproblems, thus enabling multirate time integration for the two parts. To further improve efficiency, we introduce a residual-based adaptive strategy that dynamically adjusts the time step of the explicitly treated subsystem according to its temporal error indicator. The proposed scheme is shown to be energy stable under suitable assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed mass-lumped multi-time-stepping scheme substantially reduces computational cost while maintaining accuracy comparable to that of standard fully implicit methods.

The inclusive eigenvalue counting function lies strictly below the leading Weyl term at every positive energy; consequently, each eigenvalue strictly exceeds its Weyl prediction, with multiplicities included. We also prove the same strict inequality for the Aharonov--Bohm operator on planar annuli at arbitrary flux. In dimension two, the nonmagnetic result gives a fully analytic proof of the planar annulus theorem of Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sher (J. Lond. Math. Soc., 2026). The common ingredient is a lattice-point bound for the shell action, uniform in the starting point of a tail and in the lattice translation. Quadrature for the inverse action controls the change of convexity caused by the inner boundary. The tail estimate supplies the hypothesis of the known dimension-reduction argument for balls, while lattice translations represent the magnetic flux. Laptev's product argument yields corresponding strict bounds on products of shells and nonempty bounded open sets.
On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality

Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Csáji, Csikvári, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on surfaces of nonpositive curvature
Federico Rodriguez Hertz; Jana Rodriguez Hertz; Weisheng Wu

We give a full proof that the geodesic flow of a closed surface of genus at least two with a \(C^{3+\mathrm{Lip}}\) metric of nonpositive curvature is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. In a forthcoming paper, we will present the corresponding result for smooth rank-one manifolds in every dimension.
Local Maxima of Discrete Gaussian Processes: Exact Distributions and Infill Limits

The height limits established here are unified by a continuous family indexed by the magnitude of the conditional height-curvature correlation parameter $η\in[0,1]$, with a Gaussian endpoint at $η=0$, and smooth peak laws for $0<η\le 1$ with a Rayleigh endpoint at $η=1$. Explicit finite-grid bounds control density and tail errors and yield uniform approximations across sites. For each fixed nonconstant, mean-square continuous stationary process, the fourth spectral moment gives a complete classification: finiteness yields a smooth family member, whereas an infinite moment yields the Gaussian endpoint and divergent expected peak counts on every interval of positive length. Nonstationary examples, Matérn covariance models, and numerical comparisons illustrate the results, including logarithmic boundary behavior and the distinction between distributional convergence and relative tail accuracy.

We begin a systematic study of $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-instantons on complete non-compact cohomogeneity one $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-manifolds with Aloff--Wallach spaces $N_{k,l}=\mathrm{SU}(3)/\mathrm{U}(1)_{k,l}$ as principal orbits. Let $M = S^{2n+1}/Γ$ be a manifold diffeomorphic to a compact space form, endowed with a bumpy Finsler metric $F$. In this paper, we prove that there exist at least $n+3$ contractible minimal closed geodesics on $M$, assuming that all contractible minimal closed geodesics have non-zero Morse indices. Here, a contractible closed geodesic is called minimal if it is not an iteration of any other contractible closed geodesic. In particular, this confirms the generalized Anosov-Katok conjecture for the bumpy quotient manifold $(S^3/Γ, F)$ under the non-zero Morse index assumption.
Adaptive Normalized Gradient Method for $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth Problems: Estimating Problem Parameters as a Region

We propose a parameter-free and efficient gradient descent algorithm for $(L_0,L_1)$-smooth optimization. This notion of smoothness, introduced by Zhang et al. (2020), allows the smoothness bound to grow with the gradient norm. Similar to cutting-plane localization, our method uses a sequence of observations to maintain a region of plausible values for $(L_0,L_1)$ and uses this region to select step sizes. In the convex setting, our method attains the standard iteration complexity bound $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\left(L_0/ε+ L_1^2\right)\|x^0-x^*\|^2\right)$ for finding an $ε$-optimal solution, while in the nonconvex setting it finds an $ε$-stationary point within $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\left(L_0/ε^2 + L_1/ε\right)(f(x^0)-f^*)\right)$ iterations. Experiments on logistic regression and real phase retrieval demonstrate that our method can exploit $(L_0,L_1)$-smoothness and perform efficiently on nonconvex problems.
Minorization and exponential ergodicity for degenerate diffusions with countable switching

We establish a local-minorization criterion for diffusions with countably many state-dependent switching regimes, even when every frozen transition law is singular. One regular controlled path yields a common absolutely continuous component for nearby initial states, with rate positivity required only at the switching locations. The proof controls a family of Brownian perturbations and its derivatives while retaining a path restriction for the switching likelihood. Controlled entrance and a joint Lyapunov inequality then give weighted exponential ergodicity. A concrete coefficient and rank criterion and degenerate network examples illustrate the result.
Cramer-Rao Type Bounds for Generalized Exponential Families

It is well known that the sufficient statistics of an exponential family attain the usual Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) for their expected value. In this paper, we extend this result to a broader family of distributions that includes exponential families and power-law families, with Student t-distributions as special case. To derive the generalized Cramer-Rao inequality, we first apply Eguchi's theory to Bregman divergence to obtain a Riemannian metric and then follow the approach of Amari and Nagaoka. Since this approach applies only to models with finite support, we use Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to extend it to models with countably infinite or continuous support. The resulting generalized CRLB provides a finite-sample lower bound related to the asymptotic covariance matrix of the Minimum Bregman Divergence Estimator (MBDE). In this paper, we study the enhanced nonlinear stability of stably stratified Couette flow in the three-dimensional Boussinesq system driven by a common affine Stratonovich transport noise. Lemma 3.13 was found by Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic).

We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. We study topological vector group topologies on the real line generated by Hamel coefficient functions and circle-valued characters. We determine their continuous characters, completions, and isomorphisms, and construct a sequence separating modular convergence from convergence of real-valued observations. We also classify precompact topologies and prove that no greatest nondiscrete topology exists. For the separate problem of a greatest compatible locally quasi-convex topology, we establish transfer and dilation criteria and rule out a family of dyadic counterexample constructions. The existence of a greatest compatible topology remains unresolved.

The Terracini locus of a projective variety tells us the sets of points at which Terracini's lemma will fail to recover the dimension of the corresponding secant variety. We study the Terracini loci of tangential varieties of Veronese varieties, classifying several cases, including a complete classification of the Terracini loci of tangential varieties to rational normal curves. At CRYPTO 2007, Damgård and Nielsen introduced a preprocessing approach to multi-party computation (MPC) to achieve linear communication complexity. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.

We prove that the average order of connected induced subgraphs of a connected simple graph of order $n$ and minimum degree at least $3$ is strictly greater than $n/2$, which settles a conjecture of Vince~[\emph{J. Graph Theory} 97 (2021), 82--103]. A key technical contribution is to establish existence and uniqueness of the relevant solutions to the coupled nonlinear free-boundary equations arising from value-matching and smooth-fit conditions. A verification argument then establishes the optimality of the resulting policies over all admissible switching strategies.

Guangjun Zhu; Jiaxin Li; Yulin Hu
In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.

We show that if $G$ has exactly one regular orbit on $V$, then the characteristic $q$ of $V$ is a Fermat prime, $V$ is irreducible over ${\Bbb F}_q$, ${\rm dim}_{{\Bbb F}_q}V$ is a power of $2$, and the centraliser of $G$ in ${\rm GL}(V)$ embeds into $G$. We construct local families of solutions of the $q$-difference second Painlevé equation that vanish at infinity with a common algebraic expansion, parameterised by the amplitude of an exponentially small correction. Considering an appropriate boundary region, a formal expansion that retains two independently excited exponential perturbations is developed, and subsequent transseries summation predicts the location of simple poles. Adopting a $q$-theta function realisation of the exponential factors, we prove an asymptotic pole-location formula for a one-parameter family of true solutions. We then use these two ingredients as a substitute for weak containment in the coarse bimodule and deduce several rigidity theorems in the framework of Popa's deformation/rigidity theory. As a main consequence, we prove that every $q$-Araki--Woods factor is stably strongly solid. We also prove a normalizer rigidity theorem for inclusions arising from direct sum representations. Finally, we compute Connes' $τ$-invariant, and construct a continuum of pairwise non-isomorphic type $\mathrm{III}_1$ $q$-Araki--Woods factors with the same $τ$-invariant.
Hodge Theory of Novikov Type Landau--Ginzburg Models

We establish a strong Hodge decomposition theorem for Novikov type Landau--Ginzburg models, that is, triples $(M,g,θ)$ consisting of a non-compact complete Kähler manifold $(M,g)$ and a non-trivial closed holomorphic one-form $θ$ on $M$.Under the well-tameness condition and under the assumption that $M$ is Stein, we prove that the space of $L^{2}$-forms on $M$ admits an orthogonal decomposition into the space of harmonic forms of the twisted Laplacian $Δ_θ$ and the images of the twisted Dolbeault operators $\bar\partial+θ\wedge$ and $\bar\partial^{\dagger}+ι_{\barθ^{\sharp}}$; moreover, the harmonic space is concentrated in degree $n=\dim_{\C}M$ and is isomorphic to the Milnor rings of $θ$. As applications, we endow the complement of a hyperplane arrangement with a complete cylindrical Kähler metric, and we show that the differential of a master function with nonresonant weights is well-tamed with respect to this metric. After passing to a log resolution in the non-normal-crossing case; we then apply the results to the Yang--Yang functional of the Gaudin model, whose critical points are the Bethe roots: the top-degree harmonic space is described by the corresponding Milnor rings, and the number of Bethe roots is given by the Varchenko--Orlik--Terao lattice formula.
The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs

The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $χ_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ χ_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $Γ$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.
Rotations, Shears, and Two-Generation on Spheres

For every round sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, we exhibit two explicit divergence-free vector fields whose flows generate a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. One generator is an elementary planar rotation, \[ A=R_{12}, \] while the other combines a linearly modulated planar rotation with a chain of adjacent planar rotations: \[ B=x_3R_{12}+\sum_{k=2}^n R_{k,k+1}. \] Thus two one-parameter groups suffice, and two is the smallest possible number. The proof separates naturally into two steps. We first show that the $n$ adjacent rotations \[ R_{12},R_{23},\ldots,R_{n,n+1} \] together with the shear $x_3R_{12}$ generate, through their flows, a $C^\infty$-dense subgroup of $\SDiff_0(S^n)$. The infinitesimal argument is organized by transverse vector spherical harmonics. For $n\ge4$ the relevant harmonic spaces are irreducible $SO(n+1)$-modules; on $S^2$ the argument reduces to the Hamiltonian/Poisson formalism; and on $S^3$ the transverse harmonic spaces split into two curl eigenspaces. We then show that all $n+1$ of these vector fields lie in the Lie algebra generated by $A$ and $B$. A Casimir operator separates the quadratic shear from the linear rotational terms, after which the remaining rotations can be recovered successively. Finally, standard approximation formulas for flows convert the Lie-algebraic generation result into $C^\infty$ density in $\SDiff_0(S^n)$.
On the Accuracy of Approximate Leave-One-Out with Blockwise Nonsmooth Regularization in High-dimensions
Honghao Lin; Songbin Liu; Arian Maleki; Vahab Mirrokni; Chen Shang; David P. Woodruff; Hanbo Yang; Wenjin Zhang

Approximate leave-one-out (ALO) refers to methods that provide computationally efficient and statistically accurate approximations to leave-one-out risk estimation. These methods have recently attracted increased attention because of their connections to other important problems, including machine unlearning and data valuation. For empirical risk minimization, ALO methods often rely on a few Newton steps and therefore require smooth loss functions and regularizers. In high-dimensional problems, however, regularizers are frequently non-smooth. This has motivated the development of heuristic ALO methods for non-smooth regularization, whose empirical accuracy is often strong but whose theoretical justification remains limited. In this paper, we study the accuracy of a heuristic ALO method for a broad class of non-differentiable penalties that promote block sparsity in the proportional high-dimensional regime. Assuming uniformly bounded block sizes, we prove that the expected average absolute discrepancy between the exact leave-one-out loss and its ALO approximation is $O(\log^{3/2}(en)/\sqrt{n})$. Our proof technique differs substantially from existing approaches and relies on obtaining sharp bounds on the number of active groups whose status changes between the full-data and leave-one-out estimators. In addition to yielding stronger guarantees under weaker assumptions than prior work, our analysis provides new insight into the stability of sparse estimators under perturbations of the training data.
Pointwise decay of steady Navier--Stokes flows with Navier-slip boundary condition in two-dimensional channels

We establish a pointwise decay estimate for steady incompressible Navier--Stokes flows in two-dimensional channels with positive Navier friction coefficient. Specifically, for the arbitrary-flux solutions constructed by Sha, Wang, and Xie \cite{SWX22f}, under suitable outlet conditions and weighted geometric bounds on the channel walls, we show \[ |\Bu(x_1,x_2)|\le \frac{C}{f(x_1)}, \] where $f$ is the channel width. Our decay rate is optimal in the cross-sectional supremum norm when the prescribed flux is nonzero. The main difficulty is that rescaling by the local width changes the Navier friction coefficient into a potentially large parameter. The key technique is to establish a local Stokes boundary estimate uniform in this parameter.
Soliton Profiles in 1D: Enhanced Neural-Network Solvers and Constrained Deep Ritz Methods
Chandler Haight; Alex D Rodriguez; Svetlana Roudenko

We develop and compare enhanced neural-network solvers for one-dimensional ground-state profiles, which are solutions of $$ Q^{\prime\prime}=bQ-γQ^{p},\quad Q>0,\quad p>1, \quad b, γ>0, $$ the stationary profile equation for the nonlinear Schrödinger, generalized Korteweg-de Vries, and nonlinear Klein-Gordon equations. Its explicit sech-type solutions serve as exact reference for error computation and benchmark hyperparameter selection. We improve on the standard Adam-trained physics-informed neural network (PINN) baseline by introducing higher-order optimization via Gauss-Newton/Levenberg-Marquardt and L-BFGS refinements, as well as Fourier-feature PINNs, and constrained Deep Ritz (DR) formulations. In DR approaches we introduce two new neural-network formulations, which implement two classical variational characterizations: a Nehari-constrained Deep Ritz method, in which the height is learned by projecting onto the Nehari/Pokhozhaev manifold, and a Weinstein Deep Ritz method, in which a normalized profile minimizes the Weinstein quotient. The Deep Ritz formulations perform best overall, in particular, the Weinstein variant gives the best error-runtime balance. The neural-network based solvers remain less accurate and efficient than classical Petviashvili iteration in 1D, however, the current study provides a proof of concept: the mesh-free formulation, non-reliance on exact profiles or the related features make them promising in higher dimensions and for more complicated nonlinearities and dispersive operators.
On Entries of Spectral Decompositions and Applications

The entries of the spectral idempotents of a graph are its local and crossed local multiplicities. This paper uses these classical quantities in three applications. First, in a graph on $n$ vertices without isolated vertices, every local multiplicity is at most $\frac{n-1}{n}$, and every diagonal entry of the Cesaro average mixing matrix is at most $1-\frac{2}{n}+\frac{2}{n^2}$. In both bounds equality holds only for the complete graph. This proves the connected form of the complete graph trace conjecture of Godsil, Guo and Sobchuk together with its equality case, and component and degree refinements follow. The two upper bounds and their attainment by complete graphs also occur in a recent machine checked proof, without a formal characterization of when equality holds. Second, for the line graph of a connected graph $Γ$, the average return probability at a bridge with a bipartite component on one side is at least the reciprocal of the rank of the unsigned incidence matrix. Equality holds exactly for $P_2$ and $P_3$. The proof combines local moments with known inverse-incidence formulas. Finally, the paper gives a short proof of Godsil's entry criterion, which says that vertices $u$ and $v$ are strongly cospectral exactly when $\left|(E_θ)_{uv}\right|=(E_θ)_{uu}$ for every eigenvalue $θ$. The criterion recovers the known classification in connected noncomplete strongly regular graphs, where the strongly cospectral pairs are precisely the two-vertex parts of cocktail party graphs.
On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation

We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.
Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Magnetohydrodynamic Equations

We establish Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary fractional magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system with different orders of dissipation. Our first result shows that every smooth solution satisfying the natural homogeneous Sobolev energy conditions is trivial whenever $1\leqα\leq 5/3$ and $3\leqα+2β\leq5$, without any additional integrability assumptions on the velocity or magnetic fields. This extends previous results to new parameter regimes, including cases with $β<1$. Beyond this region, we prove a complementary Liouville theorem under suitable integrability conditions only on the radial components of the velocity and magnetic fields. The proofs rely on the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and localized energy estimates.
Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions

In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.
Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories
Iván Angiono; Agustina Czenky; Pavel Etingof; Victor Ostrik; Julia Plavnik; Guillermo Sanmarco

We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.
The Spectrum of the Discrete Mathieu Operator with Nonreal Coupling

We study the discrete Mathieu operator with nonreal coupling in the large-period limit, using complex WKB methods for analytic finite-difference equations. We obtain quantization formulas in different regions of the complex energy plane. Away from the corners of the image of the classical symbol, these formulas involve cosines of classical action integrals with small analytic corrections to the actions. Near each corner, we derive a uniform quantization formula involving the reciprocal Gamma function. The quantization formulas constrain spectral accumulation to curves determined by the competing exponential terms. Numerical computations illustrate the resulting spectral geometry.
Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields

$\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.
A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
Chuang Zhong; Masaki Kashima; Yaping Mao

The induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)$ is defined as the minimum order of a graph $F$ such that any 2-coloring of its edges with red and blue leads to either a red induced copy of $G$ or a blue induced copy of $H$. In 1998, Kohayakawa, Prömel, and Rödl conjectured that for any fixed graph $G$, there exists a constant $f=f(G)$ such that the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G, H)$ is bounded by $|V(H)|^f$ for every graph $H$. In this paper, we completely solve the Kohayakawa--Prömel--Rödl conjecture, which states that for any graphs $G$ and $H$ with $|V(G)|=k\ge2$ and $|V(H)|=t\ge2$, $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)\le t^{60k^2+3}$. This verifies the conjecture with $f(G)=60|V(G)|^2+3$.
We prove that a Borel strict partial order is an increasing union of wellfounded Borel partial orders if and only if it admits an (injective) Borel homomorphism to the eventual domination order.
Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds

We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of Álvarez López and Calaza.
The Finite Basis Problem for Multiplicatively Idempotent Semirings

The variety of semirings satisfying $x^2\approx x$ is hereditarily finitely based in the signature consisting of addition and multiplication, without designated constants. Multiplication may be noncommutative, and the semirings need not be finite. A subdirect decomposition reduces the proof to the subvarieties defined by $3x\approx x$ and $3x\approx2x$. In the latter case, we express each polynomial identity using a common doubled part and isolated word occurrences. Four fixed identities align the first- and last-occurrence words of these occurrences. Induction on their content extracts protected identities. The associated word identities define a band variety, to which the finite basis theorem for bands applies.
Generic distinction of induced representations: the case of symmetric spaces

Let H be the fixed-point subgroup of an involution of a reductive group G over a local field F of characteristic zero. We give a necessary condition for a parabolically induced representation of G(F) to admit a non-zero family of H(F)-equivariant linear forms depending holomorphically on the induction parameter. By works of Blanc-Delorme and Brylinski-Delorme, this condition is essentially sufficient. As a global consequence, we obtain vanishing results for regularized periods of Eisenstein series. We illustrate this on symplectic periods, where we extend Offen's computation of truncated periods of certain cuspidal Eisenstein series to inner forms of GL(2n).
A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs

We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erdős--Rényi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.
Quantum Variance for Hecke--Maass Cusp Forms on the Vertical Geodesic

Let $X=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H$, and let $\{u_j\}$ be an orthonormal basis of even Hecke--Maass cusp forms on $X$ with Laplace eigenvalues $1/4+t_j^2$. For a real-valued $ψ\in C_c^\infty(0,\infty)$, define \[ μ_j(ψ)=\int_0^\inftyψ(y)|u_j(iy)|^2\,\frac{dy}{y}, \qquad M(ψ)=\frac6π\int_0^\inftyψ(y)\,\frac{dy}{y}. \] For $T\ge2$, $1\le U\le T$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove \[ \sum_{\substack{u_j\ {\rm even}\\T<t_j\le T+U}} L(1,\mathrm{sym}^2u_j)|μ_j(ψ)-M(ψ)|^2 \ll_{ψ,\varepsilon}T^{1+\varepsilon}. \] As a consequence, for fixed $0<θ\le1$, $0<η<θ/2$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, if $T^θ\le U\le T$, then all but \[ O_{ψ,θ,η,\varepsilon} \!\left(T^{1+2η+\varepsilon}\right) \] of the even forms with $T<t_j\le T+U$ satisfy $μ_j(ψ)=M(ψ)+O(T^{-η})$. In particular, the exceptional proportion tends to zero in this short spectral interval.
Theoretical Foundations of Sequential Dynamic Programming

Many economic problems have several controls per period, whose joint choice is subject to the curse of dimensionality. Solving them in stages is computationally cheaper, but no general result says when staging is exact. I develop a separability theory, discrete choices and non-concave objectives included: staging is exact if utility, transitions, and constraints depend on earlier decisions only through a state passed forward. For each ordering the smallest such state exists and is unique up to relabeling. Any state that keeps staging exact for all preferences over later decisions and the future must carry everything the smallest one carries for the transition. For affine primitives, the smallest state consists of the linear combinations, such as cash-on-hand, on which later outcomes depend. Its dimensions pick the order whose largest stage is smallest. In a six-choice household model, each stage chooses one variable on a three-dimensional state, the joint problem all six.
Geometry-informed importance sampling for rare events
Qinyi Wang; Anya Katsevich; Shanyin Tong

We propose GeoIS, a new importance sampling method for estimating rare event probabilities for an underlying Gaussian distribution that exploits asymptotic theory and local event geometry. The proposal distribution is a mixture of two components. The first component draws a Gaussian along the boundary near the instanton and adds to it an exponentially distributed shift into the rare event. This component is derived from the known asymptotic approximation to the optimal zero-variance proposal distribution. The second mixture component is designed to cover missing event mass due to boundary-approximation mismatch, thereby preserving unbiasedness. We rigorously analyze this sampling strategy's performance as a function of event geometry, dimension, rarity level, and number $N$ of importance samples.
