Property RD and boundary representations]{Property RD for $\widetilde A_2$ groups\\and boundary representations

We develop a boundary representation approach to Rapid Decay property for groups acting on buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$. The central estimate combines a multiplicity argument on the product of Furstenberg boundary with the Riesz--Thorin theorem. For simply transitive actions on vertices, we also establish the polynomial bound conjectured by Ramagge, Robertson and Steger in the vector-radial case. The cubic degree of this bound is optimal. The method also uses multiplicity argument with the Riesz--Thorin theorem but on the single Furstenberg boundary.
On the Linear Convergence of SISTA for Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport
Giorgia Bifronte; Armand Ley; Maxime Sylvestre

We prove a linear convergence rate of a Sinkhorn-type algorithm for entropic martingale optimal transport in arbitrary dimension. The algorithm follows a block-coordinate ascent scheme, alternating exact Sinkhorn updates for the marginal potentials with an explicit gradient step for the potential associated with the martingale constraint. Under irreducibility and non-degeneracy assumptions on the compactly supported marginals, we establish linear convergence of the dual objective values and iterates. Our analysis relies on a pointwise coercivity estimate involving the gradient of the dual functional with respect to the potential for the martingale constraint. This property allows us to establish uniform $L^{\infty}$ bounds on the iterates. Combining these bounds with smoothness and strong convexity modulo affine invariances yields a uniform Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality along the iterations and, consequently, a linear convergence rate. We complement our theoretical results with numerical experiments illustrating the convergence behavior of the algorithm.
Well--posedness and homogenization of a waste--protein clearance model in cortical tissue
Miroslav Bulíček; Ansgar Jüngel; Marie E. Rognes; Lucie Wintrová

We formulate and analyze a mathematical model for the clearance of waste proteins from cortical tissue. The model tracks three species of waste proteins, distinguished by their size, and incorporates constant production at neuronal surfaces, reaction-diffusion in the bulk of interstitial fluid, and nonlinear dynamics on capillary surfaces. We establish the existence, boundedness, and uniqueness of a solution to the microscopic model. Using two-scale convergence, we derive a homogenized model and prove that the microscopic solutions converge to the corresponding macroscopic limit. The resulting model reveals how the microscopic arrangement and relative volume fractions of neurons and capillaries affect waste-protein transport and clearance at the tissue scale. Numerical simulations illustrate these effects and demonstrate how variations in cortical microstructure translate into differences in the macroscopic clearance dynamics.
Pasten's arithmetic derivatives and the decomposition into gains

Pasten attached to each coprime triple $a+b=c$ a lattice of arithmetic derivations that obey the Leibniz rule and are additive on this one equation. An arithmetic Wronskian then gives an $abc$-type inequality governed by the norm $\|ψ\|$ of the derivation, and Pasten showed that sufficiently small derivations exist under the $abc$ conjecture and give an $abc$ inequality with a fixed exponent. We determine exactly which values this Wronskian takes, and we show that its estimate with exact prime weights has the best possible coefficient. The quality $X=\log c/\log\operatorname{rad}(abc)$ factors into an approximation gain and a power gain for each chosen presentation of the triple, and the resulting inequality bounds $X$ and both gains. For coprime polynomials the same argument gives $G_a < 1$ and $G_p < 3$. We also show that the largest absolute value of the derivation on $a$, $b$ and $c$ exceeds $c/\operatorname{rad}(abc)$ whenever the derivation is additive on the triple with non-zero Wronskian, so that it gives no bound on the quality by itself, and we determine its minimum when $a=1$. For Fermat triples the presentation by bases has approximation gain greater than $n/3$, which recovers Pasten's conditional asymptotic Fermat theorem. Finally, for five triples we certify the minimal norms and find the inequality within $0.08$ of the quality, with equality for the triples $1+80=81$ and $1+2400=2401$.
Optimal Oracle Complexity of Dual Halpern Iteration in Normed Spaces

In this work, we study the convergence and error bounds of dual Halpern iteration for nonexpansive operators in normed spaces. First, we show that dual Halpern iteration exhibits the same optimal residual rate as Halpern iteration in the deterministic setting through a direct convergence analysis. With inexact operator evaluations, we also conduct a convergence analysis in normed spaces and derive the robust error bound of inexact dual Halpern iteration. Based on this robustness result, we study the oracle complexity of stochastic dual Halpern iteration in $(\mathcal{R}^d,\|\cdot\|_p)$ for $p\in(1,\infty]$, using an unbiased stochastic oracle with bounded variance $σ^2$. Notably, for $p\in[2,\infty]$, our method achieves an oracle complexity of $O\left(ε^{-1}+σ^2ε^{-3}\right)$ in its dependence on $ε$ and $σ$, which matches the lower bound for the case $p=\infty$ without a logarithmic gap in the dependence on $ε$.
Majorization for superpositions of nonorthogonal states and the existence of golden states

In the resource theory of superposition relative to linearly independent, nonorthogonal reference states, golden states are known for two reference states and for special overlap matrices, and all of them are maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. We clarify what decides their existence and their Löwdin structure. The robustness and the geometric measure of superposition are maximized by the same states, which overlap equally with every reference state; their maximal values are set by the ground-state energy of a classical $XY$ model on the overlaps of the dual basis. For every overlap matrix, these states, and only these, are golden under the maximal superposition-free operations, but they need not be maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis. For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove a necessary and sufficient criterion, Gram majorization, for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients; it reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that golden states of these operations must be maximally coherent in the Löwdin basis, but that this does not ensure their existence: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit a golden state if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $Φ$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(π+|Φ|)/3]$. Equal-overlap states also yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the Löwdin basis, which show that white noise on the span of the reference states is a resource unless these states are orthonormal.

We give the classification of C-spaces (i.e., compact homogeneous spaces admitting an invariant complex structure), up to finite cover and equivariant diffeomorphism, of dimension 6, 8 and 10. The conditions for the existence of a balanced, pluriclosed, CYT and LCK Hermitian metric are established for dimensions 6 and 8.
A direct obstacle proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ bound for the Gaussian Riesz transforms

We give a detailed, direct proof of a dimension-free weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the first-order Gaussian vector Riesz transform, using the fractional obstacle method of Ouyang, Spector, and Stockdale. For $dγ_n=π^{-n/2}e^{-|x|^2}\,dx$, let $L=-\tfrac12Δ+x\cdot\nabla$, $D=2^{-1/2}\nabla$, and $R_γ=DL^{-1/2}Π_0$, where $Π_0$ removes the mean. We prove that $R_γ$ has weak-type constant at most $2$ on real-valued inputs, independently of $n$. The main construction is the unique unshifted decomposition $F=g+L^{1/2}u$, for nonnegative $F\in L^2(γ_n)$ and $a>\int F\,dγ_n$, with $u\geq0$, $\min\{F,a\}\leq g\leq a$, preservation of mass, and $g=a$ on $\{u>0\}$. We retain the details of coercivity, the Lewy--Stampacchia estimate, the upgrade from the form domain to the operator domain, and locality. We also identify the $L^1$ extension with the principal-value transform and obtain the constant $8/π$ for complex-valued inputs.
Rigidity of Euclidean Convex Fillings for Ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim Mass

We prove rigidity for compact integral current fillings with respect to ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim mass. Let $C\subset\R^n$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, $n\ge1$, and let $T\in\I_n(X)$, where $X=\spt T$ is compact. Suppose $ι:\partial C\to X$ is an isometric embedding for the Euclidean chord metric and \[ \partial T=ι_\#\cur{\partial C},\qquad \M(T)=\Leb^n(C). \] Then $ι$ extends to a surjective isometry $I:C\to X$ satisfying $I_\#\cur C=T$. No map from the filling to the convex body is assumed.
A Simple and Unified Method for Gradient-Variation Regret

Gradient-variation online learning has attracted increasing attention for its connections to game theory and optimization. It has been studied in both non-stationary online learning, which aims to minimize dynamic regret against time-varying comparator sequences, and universal online learning, which seeks to adapt to unknown loss curvature. Prior work obtained gradient-variation bounds using different techniques tailored to each setting. We propose a simple and unified method based on surrogate losses with a quadratic penalty on decision movement, yielding gradient-variation bounds in both settings. For non-stationary online learning, the method induces an optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction, enabling a broad class of algorithms to match the rate established by Zhao et al. (2024). For universal online learning, it yields a simple algorithm that matches the optimal universal regret bounds of Yan et al. (2024) while relaxing the extended smoothness assumption. Finally, we apply our method to online games and improve on existing guarantees.
Wiener's criterion and resolutivity for the $p$-parabolic equation

We characterize boundary regularity for $u_t=Δ_p u$ in arbitrary bounded open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ for $n\ge2$ and $p\in(2n/(n+1),2)\cup (2,\infty)$. We prove equivalent Wiener criteria in terms of capacitary potentials on prescribed cylinders and in terms of intrinsic capacities. Both require divergence at every positive obstacle height. Independently, we prove Perron resolutivity for continuous data on the full topological boundary of every nonempty bounded open set for all $n\geq 1$ and $p>1$. As an application of the Wiener criterion, we prove a Petrovski\uı-type criterion in the singular range, which gives regularity of the origin for $|x|<C(-t)^{1/p}$ for every $C>0$. For $2<p<n$, examples show that divergence at every sufficiently large height does not imply regularity.
Limits of Besov Norms on Quantum Euclidean Spaces
Qingquan Deng; Guixiang Hong; Ping Li; Yanzhen Long

We extend the Bourgain--Brézis--Mironescu (BBM) and Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova (MS) limit formulae to higher-order Besov norms on quantum Euclidean spaces $\R^d_θ$, a fundamental class of noncompact noncommutative manifolds obtained by deformation quantization of $\R^d$. A central ingredient is a Banach realization of the homogeneous Sobolev endpoint that forms a compatible couple with \(L_p(\R_θ^d)\), together with the equivalence \[ K\bigl(\x,\varepsilon^k; L_p(\R_θ^d),\dot W_{p,0}^k(\R_θ^d)\bigr) \approx ω_p^k(\x,\varepsilon). \] This framework yields a unified proof of both endpoint formulae through the endpoint continuity of real interpolation scales. The principal new ingredient at the MS endpoint is the sharp large-translation asymptotic \[ \lim_{|h|\to\infty}\|T_h\x-\x\|_p = 2^{1/p}\|\x\|_p, \qquad \x\in L_p(\R_θ^d),\quad 1\leq p<\infty, \] whose proof combines oscillatory decay of the non-pure terms in the tracial expansion with weighted spectral-measure arguments adapted to the semifinite trace.
Sign bias in hyperbolic double cosets

We study sign bias between hyperbolic double cosets with $ad>0$ and $ad<0$ in appropriate cocompact Fuchsian groups. We prove that an eventual bias can only favour $ad<0$, and show that such a bias occurs within every cocompact Fuchsian commensurability class. When the normal-derivative periods of all nonconstant eigenfunctions with eigenvalue at most $1/4$ vanish, we prove an $Ω_\pm(X^{1/2})$ result and show that the counting difference takes both signs in every sufficiently large interval $[X,CX]$, for some fixed $C>1$.
Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions
Somnath Giri; Muslim Malik; Rishikesh Yadav

Solutions of second-order elliptic PDE problems on nonconvex or cracked domains with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions typically lie outside $H^2(Ω)$. Near re-entrant corners, crack tips and points where the boundary condition changes type, the gradient grows like $r^{λ-1}$ with $λ<1$. We study residual-based adaptive refinement in hybrid variational-collocation PINNs. A multiscale Fourier-feature network is trained on a composite loss. The loss combines a variational residual tested against Legendre bubble functions, a strong-form collocation term and penalties for the Dirichlet and Neumann data. The variational term needs only first derivatives of the network, whereas the collocation term requires second derivatives and provides a residual that can be evaluated at any point. After each training stage, candidate points selected by this residual are added to the collocation set. The method is tested on five two dimensional benchmarks, namely a Mode~III crack, a cross-shaped domain with four re-entrant corners with unequal amplitude, a reaction-diffusion problem with four localized peaks, a monotone semilinear problem with a boundary layer and the Motz problem. Compared with uniform point insertion under the same collocation and iteration budget, residual-based refinement reduced the relative $L^2$ error by up to a factor of $32$, the relative $L^\infty$ error by up to a factor of $38$ and the relative $H^1$ semi-norm error by up to a factor of $15$.
On True Minimum Distances of Goppa Codes
Yaqi Chen; Hao Chen; Chao Liu; Huimin Lao

Binary Goppa codes are important in coding theory and cryptography. It is well-known that the minimum distance of a binary Goppa code defined by a squarefree polynomial of degree $r$ is at least $2r+1$. Though from the classical results of C. J. Moreno, O. Moreno, F. Levy-dit-Vehel and S. Litsyn that the true minimum distances of binary Goppa codes are $2r+1$, when the extension field degree $m$ is larger than $(r-1)^{4r}$. There have only very few families of binary Goppa codes with determined true minimum distances. In this paper, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for binary Goppa codes such that their minimum distances are $2r+1$ and $2r+2$. Infinitely many infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance $2r+1$ are given. In particular, we construct such codes for every Goppa degree $r$ in the range $2^{h-1}<r<2^h$ over $\mathbb F_{2^{2h}}$. For every $2\le r\le\lfloor2^m/3\rfloor$, we also obtain at least $2^m-3r+1$ distinct monic squarefree Goppa polynomials of degree $r$ over $\mathbb F_{2^m}$, such that their related binary Goppa codes have minimum distance $2r+1$. We extend a criterion for $q$-ary Goppa codes to split auxiliary polynomials and obtain some infinite families of $q$-ary Goppa codes attaining their designed distances $r+1$. We also construct infinite families of binary Goppa codes with minimum distance exactly $2r+2$.

Can a strictly convex billiard be ergodic? For the billiard in a suitable intersection of two circles, we establish \emph{uniform} expansion of vectors in an invariant cone family under the return to a well-chosen section. This is the first and most onerous step towards a forthcoming proof of ergodicity (the Chen--Mohr--Zhang--Zhang conjecture) and statistical properties. Together, this appears to be the first time that a strictly convex billiard is shown to be ergodic.
Simultaneous Sharp-Interface Limits for a Diffuse-Interface Landau--de Gennes Droplet Model
Sisi Guan; Wei Wang; Lei Zhang

Nematic droplet models based on diffuse interfaces involve competing microscopic transition layers whose interaction is lost if the small parameters are sent to zero successively. We study this interaction for the diffuse-interface Landau--de Gennes model of Shi et al., with phase-field thickness $\varepsilon$ and exterior $Q$-tensor relaxation length $κ_\varepsilon$, and show that their relative scale selects the effective sharp-interface theory. Within a regular-interface class, we establish the corresponding sharp-interface limit for every limiting ratio $r=\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}κ/\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty]$. Three qualitatively different regimes emerge. When $r=+\infty$, the two transition layers separate asymptotically and the interfacial costs decouple, recovering the previously obtained iterated limit. When $r\in(0,+\infty)$, the layers overlap and produce a genuinely coupled, $r$-dependent anisotropic surface density. When $r=0$, finite energy forces the interior trace of $Q$ to vanish on the limiting interface. The comparable-scale regime requires a genuinely coupled interfacial analysis. Thus the exterior relaxation length is not merely a regularization parameter: together with the phase-field thickness, it determines the macroscopic surface energy and anchoring law of the sharp-interface limit.
From Chaplygin Sleigh to Torpedo: An~example of a~Cartan-Geometric View of Left-Invariant Nonholonomic Systems

We discuss two models of a 3D torpedo in which the centre of mass $x$ moves only longitudinally, while the body may rotate about $x$. Although these are simple examples of left-invariant distributions on the Lie group $SE(3)$, they possess rich geometric structures. For the simplest model, we arrive at an abelian extension of a flat (3,5) path geometry, while adding tiny coupling, we obtain a non-trivial hyperbolic type codimension two CR geometry whose symmetry algebra is just $\mathfrak{se}(3)$.
Inconsistency between Frequentist and Bayesian inference, approximation of improper priors and permissible priors
Pierre Druilhet; Erwan Saint Loubert Bié

Improper priors are widely used in objective Bayesian inference, although posterior propriety does not by itself guarantee coherence between Bayesian and frequentist assessments. We investigate this issue by approximating improper priors with proper priors and examining the convergence of the resulting posterior distributions. We introduce monotone $q$-vague convergence, which ensures pointwise Kullback-Leibler (KL) convergence of the posteriors, and study expected KL (EKL) convergence together with its total variation counterpart (ETV). Through continuous and discrete examples, we show that EKL convergence can depend on the sequence of compact sets used for approximation. In particular, convergence along one compact exhaustion need not extend to others. Our main result connects posterior approximation to inconsistency: strong inconsistency prevents both ETV and EKL convergence for any proper-prior approximation. Consequently, KL-permissible and TV permissible priors cannot be strongly inconsistent. We also introduce weak inconsistency and show that it may persist despite EKL convergence. Finally, a unified discrete framework covering the Flatland and Fraser-Monette-Ng paradoxes illustrates the distinction between these notions. In particular, ETV convergence need not imply EKL convergence, while the absence of weak inconsistency does not guarantee an EKL convergent compact approximation.
A Deep Backward Scheme for Reflected BSDEs via Penalization : Approximation and Convergence Analysis
E. H. Essaky; M. A. Jalal; Y. Ouknine

We propose and analyze a deep backward numerical scheme for Markovian reflected backward stochastic differential equations with a generator independent of the control variable, based on the penalization method. The reflection constraint is replaced by penalized BSDEs, which are approximated backward in time by neural networks, with particular attention to the dependence of the errors on the penalization parameter \(λ\). We derive quantitative error estimates for both the value process \(Y\) and the control process \(Z\). A key ingredient is an \(L^2\)-regularity estimate for the control component with explicit dependence on \(λ\). Exploiting the monotonicity of the penalization term, we obtain stability estimates uniform in \(λ\) and prove uniform spatial Lipschitz bounds for both the penalized value functions and the discrete backward targets. Consequently, the GroupSort Lipschitz constraints and the associated neural-network approximation error can be controlled uniformly in \(λ\). The global analysis separates penalization, time-discretization, forward, and neural-network approximation errors. Balancing the dominant terms yields a mean-square error of order \(O(|π|^{1/3})\) for the value component, together with a corresponding estimate for a post-training reconstruction of \(Z\). Numerical experiments with an explicit reflected BSDE and American option problems illustrate the scheme on one-dimensional and structured high-dimensional benchmarks.
A connection inequality for the random-cluster model
Jianping Jiang; Sike Lang; Yuxuan Sun

For a finite graph $G=(V,E)$, let $ϕ$ be the random-cluster measure with edge parameters $(p_e)_{e\in E}$, cluster weight $q\geq 1$ and free boundary condition. For each $x\in V$ and all nonempty $A,B\subseteq V$, we prove $ϕ(x\leftrightarrow B)\geq ϕ(x\leftrightarrow A)\min_{a\in A}ϕ(a\leftrightarrow B)$. For $q=1$, this is the (slightly generalized) Kozma-Nitzan inequality. Our extension to $q>1$ is based on a recent proof of this inequality by Blanc-Renaudie. As an application, we give a simple proof of sharp upper bounds for one-arm and point-to-plane connection probabilities in the subcritical regime.
Local data augmentation for imbalanced binary classification
Harold Gu{é}neau; Alain Celisse; Pascal Delange

Facing imbalanced binary classification, we aim at maximizing the recall while limiting the proportion of false detections in the minority class. For doing that, the present work studies the effect of several rebalancing strategies, from the uniform subsampling of the observations from the minority class, to a more involved local data augmentation scheme. To be more specific, we establish that only rebalancing class proportions cannot modify the classification performance, whereas local data augmentation is proved to have an impact on the final results. The local augmentation scheme is introduced by means of a two-step procedure. The first step randomly subsamples anchor points among the training observations. These anchor points are used in the second step, for drawing new augmentation data following an ''augmentation kernel'' to be specified. This enables us to decouple the impact of the anchor points subsampling from the one of drawing augmentation data accounting (or not) for the local geometry of the support. The experiments on synthetic data illustrate the practical performance of several strategies for subsampling anchor points combined with either a Gaussian or a diffusion-based augmentation kernel. Compared to SMOTE-like data augmentation procedures, a better performance is achieved when subsampling in the close neighborhood to the classification boundary combined with a Gaussian augmentation kernel. Furthermore in specific settings where the geometric structure of the support matters, the experimental results show that using a diffusion-based augmentation kernel outperforms the Gaussian one.
Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness are algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication

We continue our investigations on pointwise multipliers for spaces of dominating mixed smoothness. In this paper we prove that under a certain conditions Triebel - Lizorkin spaces of dominating mixed smoothness form algebras with respect to pointwise multiplication.

In 1996, Michaux and Villemaire showed that any nontrivial expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +)$ defines new unary sets. We conjecture that the same holds over the structure $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$, and we prove a partial result in this direction. To do so, we first show that every nonempty sparse $k$-automatic set is a Presburger-definable image of some Cartesian power of $k^\mathbb{N}$. Using this characterization, we prove that if an expansion of $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$ defines the same unary sets, then every set of sublinear growth definable in the expansion is already definable in $(\mathbb{N}, +, k^\mathbb{N})$.
From Inverse Vandermonde Matrices to the Shift Structure of the Dirichlet Eta and Beta Functions

We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the inverse of Vandermonde matrices with nodes drawn from the quadratic sequences u n = n 2 and u n = (n -1 2 ) 2 . We derive new limiting formulas for the entries of the inverses, expressed through the even and odd central factorial numbers. These formulas are then used to study the asymptotic behavior of a ratio of determinants involving a modified Vandermonde matrix. For each node sequence, the corresponding determinant ratio converges uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane to an explicit expression involving the Dirichlet eta or beta function. We then study a family of related functions and, using an inversion theorem, exhibit their shift structure: the shifted values of the eta and beta functions are recovered as finite linear combinations of the family, which yields an integral form of these values as integrals of polynomials related to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials against generalized (half-)Clausen functions. A unified form of the shift representation, valid for an arbitrary base point z with Re(z) > 0, brings the eta and beta families under a single theorem. On the critical line the representation is unitary and the values on the two sides are complex conjugates.
One-Dimensional Symmetry Reductions of the Monge-Ampère Equation on Some Semi-Homogeneous Convex Cones in $\mathbb{R}^4$
Amir Valiakhmetov; Ewsey Obzherin; Alexey Chernov; Roland Hildebrand

Motivated by non-symmetric conic optimization, we construct six explicit families of semi-homogeneous proper convex cones $K$ in $\mathbb R^4$. For each family, a specified three-dimensional subgroup of linear automorphisms of $K$ has generic orbits of codimension one. This yields an orbit invariant $t$ and reduces the Monge-Ampère equation $\det F''=e^{2F}$, defining the canonical barrier on $K$, to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) with independent variable $t$. The families include asymmetric power, rotational-power, exponential, and nonabelian-type cones. For the power and exponential cases we derive first integrals and parametric solutions of the ODE. The reductions open the way for computing the canonical barrier on these cones numerically.
Power-of-two cycles in projective cubic graphs of large edge-width

Heckman and Krakovski proved that every 3-connected cubic planar graph contains a cycle of length 2^m for some 2 $\le$ m $\le$ 7. We extend this to 3-connected cubic graphs embedded in the real projective plane with face-width at least three and edge-width at least 48; the cycle may moreover be taken contractible. The argument passes to the spherical double cover, where the planar theorem provides the cycle inside a subgraph of diameter at most 47, and the condition on the edge-width guarantees that this subgraph projects injectively.
Topological mapping class groups of non-simply connected 4-manifolds

We construct topological isotopy invariants of homeomorphisms of non-simply connected 4-manifolds using the topological Dax invariant of disks and the Freedman-Quinn invariant of spheres. Our invariants are effective for various non-smoothable 4-manifolds without assuming that the fundamental groups are good. They detect infinite-rank free abelian direct factors of the pseudoisotopy-trivial and homotopy-trivial mapping class groups, and give lower bounds on the Prüfer rank of the Torelli groups modulo homotopy-trivial mapping classes, including examples of infinite Prüfer rank. Our method is also useful for smooth 4-manifolds. We construct stably smoothable homeomorphisms of the Enriques surface and many Dolgachev surfaces that act trivially on homology but are not homotopic to the identity.
On Special Arithmetic Gamma Values and Thakur's Gauss Sums: From $\infty$-adic to $v$-adic

In this paper, we establish an explicit algebra isomorphism between the normalized $\infty$-adic arithmetic gamma values and their $v$-adic counterparts. The construction relies on Thakur's arithmetic Gauss sums, which arise naturally from the Gross-Koblitz-Thakur relations. Our result demonstrates the phenomenon that Gauss sums, commonly regarded as "finite" analogs of gamma functions, serve as a bridge connecting the $\infty$-adic and $v$-adic gamma values.
The Exhaustive Peres Transform: Extraction and Universal Coding

Peres's iteration of von Neumann's procedure, run to exhaustion and keeping everything it does not extract, is a bijection of {0,1}^N that splits every string into fair bits and a residual. The residual is self-delimiting and determines the number of ones, so the fair bits are exactly uniform given the residual under every exchangeable law. Each residual one accounts for a power of two of the weight of the input; consequently, on every input of length N, the residual has fewer than sqrt(3) N^0.793 ones. This deterministic sparsity gives a short proof, with an explicit remainder, that the number of fair bits per symbol tends almost surely to the entropy, for Bernoulli sources and, by binarisation, on every finite alphabet. For coding, the Bernoulli likelihood factorises along the recursion, and code B, which stores the fair bits and codes the residual at plug-in biases, has the length of the two-part code. Alternatively, code G stores the fair bits and writes the Elias gamma codes of the gaps of the residual: it needs no parameter, no estimate and no arithmetic coder. On every string its length is at most the logarithm of the type class plus O(N^0.793 log N); a concatenation of J pieces costs, without transmitting the cuts, its piecewise empirical entropy plus a term that is sublinear when J = o(N). After a Burrows-Wheeler transform of the reversed string, code G competes on every individual sequence with the empirical conditional entropy of every order at once, which gives universality for stationary ergodic sources.
Decomposing the Action of Macdonald Operators for Classical Types

We study Macdonald operators associated to classical root systems of types $B_N$, $C_N$, and $D_N$. We provide explicit formulas for decomposing the cumulative action of these operators as the sum of the actions of lower-rank operators and auxiliary operators. We also discuss the same idea in the elliptic case, also known as Ruijsenaars operators, and show that under the trigonometric limit, the identity reduces to type-$A_N$ decomposition.
Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
Zhuowen Guo; Rongzhong Xiao; Shuhao Zhang

Let $(X,\mathcal B,μ)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(μ)$ and $G\in L^q(μ)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$. Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.
Basis Selection For Analog Coded Computing Under Differential Privacy Constraints
Aaditya Sharma; Rimpi Borah; J. Harshan

In analog coded computing, encoding basis functions are typically chosen to guarantee exact reconstruction and improve numerical stability. However, the same basis functions also determine the statistical geometry of the observations available to colluding workers, and hence directly influence the privacy of the underlying data. This suggests that basis selection should not be viewed solely as a reconstruction or numerical conditioning problem, but rather as a joint privacy and accuracy co-design problem. Motivated by this observation, we revisit Analog Lagrange Coded Computing (ALCC) and show that the full orthogonality constraints imposed by the conventional Lagrange basis are stronger than what is required for exact recovery. We retain only the interpolation constraints necessary for the data bearing basis functions and require the noise bearing basis functions merely to vanish at the data recovery points. This yields a parameterized family of generalized polynomial encoding bases that preserves exact reconstruction while introducing additional design degrees of freedom. We then derive a basis-dependent characterization of differential privacy for colluding workers and formulate a privacy-calibrated numerical optimization problem that jointly selects the data and noise basis functions to reduce reconstruction error while satisfying a prescribed \((ε,δ)\)-DP requirement. The resulting framework therefore treats the encoding basis itself as a privacy-design variable, rather than selecting a fixed closed-form basis a priori. The same design philosophy is also compatible with alternative privacy metrics such as mutual-information leakage. Numerical results show that, at the same privacy level, optimized basis functions substantially reduce floating-point reconstruction error relative to conventional ALCC.
Semiclassical measures for quantized elliptic and parabolic symplectic linear maps of the multidimensional torus

We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, $ξ$) = Q($ξ$)/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. We prove that the set of semiclassical measures associated to a periodic matrix A coincides with the set of invariant probability measures of A. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.
Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
Louis Carillo; Lo{ï}s Delande; Boris Nectoux

Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.
Biconservative hypersurfaces in space forms with harmonic curvature
Ram Shankar Gupta; Andreas Arvanitoyeorgos; Marina Statha

A biconservative hypersurface $M$ in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ is a hypersurface whose normal part of the vector $Δ\vec{H}$ vanishes. We study such hypersurfaces with harmonic curvature or parallel Ricci curvature, and prove that have constant mean curvature. Also, by combining our results with previous results of H.B. Lawson Jr. and M. Umehara we obtain that if $M$ is a biconservative hypersurface in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ with parallel Ricci tensor or harmonic curvature, then the shape operator $\bold{A}$ of $M$ is covariant constant, i.e. $\nabla\bold{A}=0$.
Homotopy distributions for Vietoris-Rips complexes of random circle samples

We determine the distribution of the homotopy type of the Vietoris-Rips complex of a fixed number of independent uniform points on a circle. An exact identity expresses each binomial moment of a periodic-orbit count as one probability for circular gaps, multiplied by a constant avoidance factor. We evaluate these probabilities by finite lattice-point counts and interpolation, obtaining explicit formulas for every sample size and every real scale. On an explicit rational partition, the probabilities are continuous piecewise polynomials of degree at most one less than the sample size. We also determine the homotopy distribution in the first transition window above each positive critical fraction $c_t=t/(2t+1)$. In this window the number of critical periodic orbits converges to a Poisson law with explicit intensity, yielding the limiting probabilities of the preceding odd sphere, the contractible type, and every wedge multiplicity of the critical even sphere.
A Sarkisov Involution from a Rational Cubic Curve on a Quartic Double Solid

Building on an earlier classification of smooth weak Fano threefolds of Picard number two with small anticanonical morphism, we prove that Case~28 of the table of E1-E1 links from that classification is geometrically realizable. We construct the link by blowing up a smooth rational cubic curve on a degree-two del Pezzo threefold $V_2$, realized as a quartic double solid. A lattice calculation on an anticanonical K3 surface shows that the anticanonical morphism of the blow-up is small, and the covering involution of the anticanonical double cover realizes the flop. The resulting Sarkisov link is a birational involution with the numerical invariants of E1-E1 Case~28.
Second-Order Cover Time of Random Regular Graphs

Let $G_N$ be a uniform random $d$-regular graph on $N$ vertices, with $d\ge3$ fixed. Cooper and Frieze showed that the cover time of simple random walk on $G_N$ is asymptotically $θ_dN\log N$, where $θ_d=(d-1)/(d-2)$. We prove that, in probability over the graph and uniformly in the starting point, $(T_{\rm cov}-θ_dN\log N)/(θ_dN)$ converges in distribution to a standard Gumbel law, confirming a prediction of Tishby, Biham, and Katzav [40]. The proof reduces late points to avoidance probabilities of finite sets via factorial moments, estimates these by Green-matrix capacities, and compares the latter with capacities on the infinite $d$-regular tree. We also obtain Gumbel limits for lazy, continuous-time and finitely many independent walks. For the unvisited set, we prove weighted laws of large numbers, spatial Poisson limits in the cover-time window, and joint Poisson limits for fixed tree-component shapes in their disappearance windows.
Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
Zekai Li; Mauricio Barahona; Philipp Thomas

Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.
Waveguide Deployment Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems
Yanqing Xu; Zhiguo Ding; Xiu Yin Zhang; Tsung-Hui Chang

Most existing studies on pinching-antenna systems optimize the antenna positions or activation states under a prescribed waveguide deployment, where mutually parallel waveguides are commonly adopted. However, it remains unclear whether, and under what conditions, such a deployment is optimal from a communication-performance perspective. To fill this gap, this paper investigates long-term waveguide deployment optimization for pinching-antenna systems over a rectangular service region. We first consider the fundamental two-waveguide case and derive a closed-form sufficient condition, jointly determined by the waveguide height and the service-region aspect ratio, under which a deployment parallel to the longer side of the service region is globally optimal. We then consider the general multi-waveguide case, where the orientation and offset of each waveguide are jointly optimized without prescribing any deployment pattern, and develop an adaptive exchange algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. We further show that, within the parallel class, the waveguides should be aligned with the longer side of the service region, while in the large-height regime, the globally optimal unrestricted deployment asymptotically concentrates all waveguides on the centerline along the longer side. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithm and reveal how the preferred deployment geometry depends on the waveguide height and service-region shape. In particular, nonparallel deployments can provide noticeable gains in intermediate-height regimes, whereas parallel or center-concentrated deployments become favorable in other regimes.
Fate of Arnold tongues and canards in Mobius systems with noise

We consider a class of noisy dynamical systems on the two-dimensional torus whose phase evolution is governed by Mobius transformations. In the deterministic limit, these systems favor phase-locking that is described by the band-gap structure of an associated Schrodinger equation with a periodic potential. We use the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin method to characterize this structure in the slow-fast limit. Then we show that large-deviation theory describes fluctuations of the finite-time rotation number, whereas weak-noise escape actions determine the exponential scale of rare phase slips. These estimates provide quantitative criteria for metastable phase-locking and melting of Arnold tongues over a prescribed observation time. We derive sufficient conditions for stochastic trajectories to follow prescribed canard segments. With controlled entrance errors, exponential amplification of fluctuations along repelling branches leads to an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence in the slow-forcing limit.
Semigroup of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables
Fr{é}d{é}ric Bayart; Maofa Wang; Xingxing Yao

This paper considers discrete and continuous semigroups of composition operators on the Fock space of several complex variables. For discrete semigroups generated by a single operator, the asymptotic behaviour is analysed. Strongly continuous semigroups are studied, and in particular it is shown that the classical Berkson-Porta theorem fails in this context. As an application, we show that any bounded composition operator is strongly reducible on the Fock space and that it is mean-ergodic.

We introduce the notion of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings and begin the development of their theory over an arbitrary base scheme $S$, in analogy to that of higher coverings in an $\infty$-topos. We show that for $n=0$, our notion recovers Morel's $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings between simplicial sheaves. Under suitable assumptions, we then provide a Galois-theoretic classification of $\mathbb{A}^1$-$n$-coverings. Finally, we answer a question of Morel concerning a geometric criterion for $\mathbb{A}^1$-coverings in the negative.
A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category

We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(σ_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $σ_2$ is the Galois automorphism $ζ_{117}\mapstoζ_{117}^2$.
Gabriele Buriola; Giacomo Cozzi; Antonia Dammrau; Anton Freund

We establish a general result on the proof-theoretic strength of well-ordering principles in reverse mathematics. The novelty is that our result gives information over base theories as weak as $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, while previous results of Arai, Pakhomov-Walsh and Buriola-Weiermann required the stronger base theory $\mathsf{ACA}_0$. On the way, we strengthen a result of Carlucci-Mainardi-Rathjen about the ordinal analysis of theories of the form $\mathsf{RCA}_0+\text{``$α$ is a well-order"}$.
On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces

We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.
Energy Equality, Vectorial $L^1$ Contraction, and Mixed-Norm Stability for Parabolic Systems with Rough Skew-Symmetric Potentials

We consider Dirichlet parabolic systems with measurable, real skew-symmetric zero-order potentials on bounded Lipschitz domains in three dimensions. Although skew-symmetry formally removes the potential from the energy balance, singular coefficients may leave the product $CU$ merely integrable, so testing the equation with the solution is not justified. We overcome this obstruction through bounded-gradient entropy identities and stable approximation. For $C\in L^r(0,T;L^q(Ω;\mathbb R^{m\times m}))$ with $1\le r\le\infty$, $6/5\le q\le\infty$, and $2/r+3/q\le7/2$, we establish existence and uniqueness in the full energy--distributional class, exact energy equality at every pair of times, Euclidean-vector $L^1$ contraction, and strong convergence of both solutions and coefficient--solution products under strong coefficient approximation. We compare a vectorial entropy proof with a derivation by scalar entropies and spherical averaging, and explain the narrower roles of temporal regularization, convex invariance, and adjoint transposition. An application to diffusion--precession gives quantitative stability under $L^1$ perturbations of prescribed magnetic fields for bounded initial data, including singular fields outside the main mixed-norm range.

For each $n\geq 4$, we show that the infimal Willmore energy of a non-orientable surface of odd genus immersed in $\mathbb{S}^n$ is attained by an index $(n+1)$ minimal surface in this class. For $n=4$, we obtain in addition the analogous conclusion for surfaces with non-zero Euler number. The proof uses the fact that such surfaces represent a non-trivial cobordism class together with an observation of M. Gromov relating the conformal area in $\mathbb{S}^n$ to minimal fillings in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$.
Two-Dimensional Euclidean Free Fermi Fields from Grassmannian Stochastic Analysis
Claudio Dappiaggi; Francesco Carlo De Vecchi; Pietro Tullio Falzoni; Paolo Rinaldi

Motivated by Nelson's Euclidean Markov-field construction, we develop a counterpart for the massive two-dimensional free Dirac field. Starting from a Gaussian white noise with values in a Grassmann algebra on a non-commutative probability space, we construct the associated Brownian motion and a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck field. The resulting Euclidean Fermi field is realized as a tempered distribution on spacetime test functions, with values in the underlying algebra. Its mixed two-point functions reproduce the Euclidean Dirac fundamental solution. Time-zero fields are obtained by conditional expectation onto the past filtration generated by the noise, while their covariance is the reflected Euclidean Dirac kernel. We show that conditional expectation is compatible with Wick ordering and maps Euclidean Wick polynomials to the corresponding time-zero Wick polynomials. The Euclidean time-translation semigroup is then constructed on time-zero fields and Wick sectors, with generators given by the one-particle Hamiltonian and by its second quantization.
Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision

We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.
Invertible non-cyclic functions in the little Bloch space

This paper presents a method for exhibiting functions $F$ in the little Bloch space $\B_0$ which are invertible, in the sense that $1/F$ also belongs to $\B_0$, and yet fail to be cyclic for the forward shift. The functions obtained in this way give rise to shift-invariant subspaces in $\B_0$ of index two, of a special type. The approach rests on a harmonic-measure criterion for non-cyclicity. This criterion gives a new manifestation of a principle of Borichev and Hedenmalm, and applies in a broad class of spaces of analytic functions.
Well-posedness threshold of the 2D Euler equations in Hölder spaces on infinite sectors

We study existence and uniqueness for the 2D incompressible Euler equations on infinite sectors of acute angle $β$, focusing on vorticity in Hölder-type spaces. In the inifinite sectors, for every $β$, H"older regularity cannot be expected without decay at infinity. Moreover, the corner causes Schauder-type estimates to fail at sufficiently high regularity. To address these difficulties, we introduce weighted H"older spaces and establish well-posedness for every acute angle, without any decay assumption at infinity. These spaces include scale-invariant functions, allowing us to study their regularity and dynamics. We then apply this theory to standard $C^{k,α}$ spaces and show that $k+α=π/β-1$ is the well-posedness threshold. Above this threshold, we construct initial data that exhibit instantaneous loss of regularity. At the threshold, the problem is well-posed if and only if $π/β$ is not an integer. For well-posedness in $C^{k,α}$, we assume that the initial vorticity belongs to a weighted H"older space rather than imposing decay at infinity. This class includes compactly supported initial vorticities.

We prove that the partition division operator $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k$ preserves e-positivity, resolving a conjecture of Alexandersson and Dai. For $μ\vdash kn$ and $ν\vdash n$, we express the coefficient of $e_ν$ in $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k(e_μ)$ as a normalized sum of positive rational weights over closed walks on a finite directed graph of $k$-restricted partitions. The proof combines the Pieri rule and a root of unity factorization for Macdonald polynomials. As a corollary, we recover the h-positivity of the symmetric functions $A_{n,k}$ of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.

Orlov has shown that additive invariants such as K-theory and Hochschild homology of smooth finite-dimensional DG-algebras behave similarly to those of finite-dimensional algebras. The similarities only go so far: there are examples of finite-dimensional DG-algebras with vanishing and uncountable Grothendieck groups. We show that for DG-quivers with relations, the Grothendieck groups are free of the expected rank and that, in the smooth case, all additive invariants are determined by the base field. We use our results to rule out certain finite-dimensional DG-algebras from being phantoms.
The rank of the random $k$-XORSAT matrix beyond satisfiability

The random $k$-XORSAT matrix is an $m\times n$ random matrix $\mathbf A$ over $\mathbb F_2$ that represents a random instance of the $k$-XORSAT problem. Each row of $\mathbf A$ contains precisely $k\geq3$ non-zero entries in random positions. The rows are drawn independently. The matrix $\mathbf A$ is known to have full row rank for $m/n$ below the random $k$-XORSAT satisfiability threshold, which is known explicitly [Dubois, Mandler~2002; Pittel, Sorkin~2016]. Motivated by a problem from quantum game theory and refining a result of Cooper, Frieze and Pegden (2019), we determine the limiting distribution of the rank of $\mathbf A$ beyond the satisfiability threshold.
Flip classes and elementary expansions of vertical-strip LLT polynomials

After the substitution $q\mapsto q+1$, vertical-strip LLT polynomials are weighted sums of strict $P$-partition generating functions indexed by orientations of decorated unit-interval graphs, with weight $q^{\mathrm{asc}(θ)}$. A flip moves an ascending edge across a triangle while keeping its long edge. We show that the sum over every flip class is elementary-positive: it equals the sum of the elementary symmetric functions given by the highest reachable vertices of its orientations. This answers Hwang's question on the Schur positivity of LLT flip-class sums, and it holds for circular unit-interval graphs as well. Summing over classes gives a new proof of the elementary expansion of Alexandersson and Sulzgruber, and its circular analog, which was open. We also obtain a flip-class refinement of the elementary expansion of LLT cumulants.
Young Parabolic PDEs and the Martingale Problem for Young SDEs
Fabio Bugini; Michele Coghi; Khoa Lê; Chengcheng Ling

Under mild regularity assumptions, we prove that the martingale problem associated with the hybrid Young--Lyons--Itô differential equation admits a unique solution in the natural class of solutions satisfying Krylov-type estimates, thereby establishing probabilistic weak well-posedness. Our proof relies on an analysis of the associated Kolmogorov equations, which are Young-type parabolic PDEs with irregular coefficients. The resulting theory for such Young-type parabolic PDEs is also of independent interest.
The Wandering Must Continue: Pure Mathematicians as Rangers of the North

Pure mathematics is an honest barometer of a civilization's scientific capacity, maintaining an unwritten culture of rigor, intellectual honesty, and precision whose primary service is not merely theorems, but human judgment. In an era of automated theorem generation and formal verification, this essay argues that establishing a result and understanding why it holds remain distinct achievements that require deliberate institutional protection.
Adelic Asphericity and One-Relator Pro-\(p\) Groups

We give a direct Fox-calculus proof of the known rational asphericity theorem for every finite presentation complex with one nontrivial relator, including proper powers. The proof uses completed Fox derivatives and the absence of zero divisors in the completed algebra of a prounipotent group. Exact scalar extension to the finite adeles then yields adelic asphericity and a product decomposition of the higher homotopy groups of integral Bousfield--Kan completion. We also prove rational and pro-\(p\) analogues of Mannan's formula for finite two-complexes, with their natural topologies and fundamental group actions. The rational cohomological Whitehead criterion is proved directly. For a discrete one-relator group with relator not a proper power, we show that the tower \(L_2ν_n(G)\) is Mittag--Leffler. Consequently \(\limone_nL_2ν_n(G)=0\), and \(π_2(\Z_\infty BG)\) is naturally the inverse limit of the nilpotent Baer invariants. We identify this Baer limit canonically and topologically with the kernel of the integral augmentation-completed Fox operator and with the product of its local pro-\(p\) kernels. The comparison yields a torsion-free profinite homotopy module, vanishing inverse limits of the finite-stage transgression kernels, and explicit lifting obstructions. These results provide a homotopy-theoretic framework for the question of Serre in Gildenhuys's corrected formulation.
Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
Adam Ghalem; Lou Salaün; Davide Rinaldi; Fragkiskos D. Malliaros

Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.
Efimov effect in an internal spectral gap of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian

We prove the existence of an Efimov sequence in an internal gap of the essential spectrum of a three-particle lattice Hamiltonian. The system consists of two identical spinless fermions and one distinguishable particle on \(\Z^3\), with repulsive pair interactions. For each fixed fermion-to-third-particle mass ratio \(γ>γ_*\approx13.6069657\) and total quasi-momentum near \(π\mathbf1\), the mixed zero-range coupling is tuned to a simultaneous upper-threshold resonance. Sufficiently strong nearest-neighbour repulsion between the fermions separates the upper fermion-pair two-cluster spectrum from the free three-particle band. Infinitely many discrete eigenvalues accumulate at the lower endpoint of the resulting gap, which coincides with the free upper edge. We establish logarithmic eigenvalue-counting asymptotics with the same positive coefficient as at zero fermion--fermion coupling. This coefficient also governs accumulation above the essential spectrum throughout the closed weak-coupling interval, including its critical endpoint. We classify the channel spectrum near the free upper edge for all nonnegative fermion couplings.
Singular Stability Estimates for Passive Gamma Emission Tomography of Spent Nuclear Fuel
Tommi Heikkilä; Tapio Helin; Sean Holman; Shubham R. Jathar; Jesse Railo

We study the joint recovery of attenuation and source coefficients from the attenuated X-ray transform, motivated by passive gamma emission tomography of spent nuclear fuel. Both coefficients are constant on known, disjoint disks of equal radius representing fuel rods. The surrounding moderator has known attenuation and zero source. We use tangential singularities of the data to give a sufficient condition on the geometry and coefficients for unique joint reconstruction from full data. For rods arranged on parallel rows separated by more than one rod diameter, with source coefficients uniformly bounded away from zero, we derive explicit reconstruction formulas and stability estimates for both coefficients. The estimates use a singular seminorm determined by two functionals per rod, computed from angular data near selected tangencies. Numerical experiments examine the approximation of these functionals from discretized data.
Sphere Theorems for $\frac{10}{3}$-Positive Curvature Operator of the Second Kind

In this paper, we prove that every connected closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq4$ with $\frac{10}{3}$-positive curvature operator of the second kind is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We also obtain a classification of connected closed Riemannian manifolds with $\frac{10}{3}$-nonnegative curvature operator of the second kind. The key step is to show that $\frac{10}{3}$-positivity implies the PIC1 condition. Finally, we give an example showing that $\frac{10}{3}$ is optimal for deducing PIC1 from $α$-positivity.
Hadamard well-posedness and nonuniform dependence for the incompressible free-boundary ideal MHD equations

We prove local Hadamard well-posedness for the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary ideal magnetohydrodynamic equations without surface tension under the Taylor sign condition. For every $5/2<s<4$, the result holds on bounded fluid domains whose closures are diffeomorphic to the closed ball, with the velocity, magnetic field, and boundary in the standard $H^s$ spaces. No additional regularity in the magnetic direction is required. The proof rests on a fourth order geometric energy inequality whose coefficients are controlled by these $H^s$ norms, the fixed geometric bounds, and the Taylor lower bound. A harmonic extension of the boundary normal provides the coefficient control needed at this regularity. We also prove that, near every admissible initial state and at each positive time in a common local existence interval, the Eulerian solution map is not uniformly continuous on any nonempty open subset of a sufficiently small data neighborhood. The construction combines localized magnetic oscillations prescribed at the observation time with time reversal and Galilean translations.
Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz-based convergence analysis with approximate weakly convex subdifferentials: bundle, quadratic penalty, and moving balls approximation methods

The Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) property has been widely used for establishing global sequential convergence and analyzing local convergence rate of optimization algorithms. Most existing analysis frameworks rely on the construction of a suitable KL potential function such that along the sequence generated, it admits sufficient descents and its exact subdifferentials are suitably controlled by successive changes of the iterates. It allows approximate sufficient descents, the use of diminishing stepsizes, and controls on enlarged subdifferentials of $ψ$ known as the $\varrho$-weakly-convex-$\varepsilon$-subdifferentials. We illustrate the usefulness of our framework by establishing the global sequential convergence and analyzing the local convergence rate of some recent variants of bundle method, quadratic penalty method and moving balls approximation method. Specifically, we show that these methods fall under our framework by presenting explicit and natural choices of $ψ$, and derive suitable choices of model parameters, penalty parameters and constraint shrinkage parameters, respectively, for establishing their global sequential convergence and local convergence rate based on the KL property and exponent of $ψ$.
Structural aspects of $1$-limited domination in cubic graphs

A set $D\subseteq V(G)$ is a $1$-limited dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $D$ has a neighbor in $D$ and every vertex of $D$ has at most one neighbor outside $D$. The minimum cardinality among all $1$-limited dominating sets of $G$ is denoted by $γ_1^{\mathrm L}(G)$. For every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$, there exists a nonnegative integer $t$ such that $γ_1^{\mathrm L}(G)=\frac n2+t$. We establish structural properties of $1$-limited dominating sets in terms of $t$ and use them to study the induced cycles vertex number, that is, the maximum number of vertices inducing a $2$-regular subgraph. As applications, we determine the exact $1$-limited domination numbers of generalized Blanuša snarks and flower snarks.
Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations

We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.
Two pointwise estimates for singular integral operators over p-adic groups

We establish some new pointwise boundedness properties for rough singular integral operators defined over p-adic groups. The properties of these operator rely essentially on the behavior of their rough kernels and we will present two different cases that fall outside the setting of the classical Calder{ó}n-Zygmund setting.
Corrections to ``The Method of Gaps: Exact Expressions for the Generalization Error of Supervised Learning Algorithms''

In this paper, a counterexample to Lemma 5 of the paper referenced in the title is provided. Consequently, the formulation of the method of data-driven gaps presented in the referenced paper relies on an additional assumption, namely, that the conditional distribution of the training dataset given the learned model has identical data-point-specific marginals. To overcome this limitation, a generalized formulation of the method of data-driven gaps that does not rely on Lemma 5 and does not require the training samples to be independent or identically distributed is presented. Through this formulation, the applicability of the method of data-driven gaps is extended to a broader class of data distributions and randomized learning algorithms.
Families that intersect in an arithmetic progression

For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $μ_n$ be the uniform measure on $2^{[n]}$. A family $\mathcal F \subseteq2^{[n]}$ is called $k$-AP-intersecting if $F_1\cap F_2$ contains a nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression for every $F_1, F_2\in\mathcal F$. Writing $m_k$ for the supremum of $μ_n(\mathcal F)$ over all $n$ and all such families $\mathcal F$, we prove \[ 2^{-k}\le m_k\le32\cdot 2^{-k}\qquad(k\ge3). \] This greatly improves a recent result of Gillott, who proved that $m_k \leq k^{-1/3}$ for all sufficiently large $k$, and answers his question on $m_k$'s exponential decay. We also prove a similar bound for the corresponding cross-intersection problem.
The resource cost of cooperative invasion

A contact network can favor cooperation by sheltering a lineage until its descendants compete with defectors as a group. We determine the contact strengths, invasion times and measurement effort needed to realize this advantage at fixed population size. Individuals reproduce according to averaged cooperation payoffs, and offspring replace neighbors through contacts of equal weight in both directions. Contact contrast is the ratio of strongest to weakest contact. Under weak selection on a six-site path, the least contrast needed to favor a single cooperator over the reverse invasion by a defector grows as $656ε^{-2}$ for uniformly placed mutants and $4050ε^{-3}$ for mutations in newborn offspring, as the benefit-cost ratio $b/c=1+ε$ approaches one. The extra power arises because rare replacement protects a site while suppressing mutation arrival there. Global bounds force two weakly coupled groups and exact mirror symmetry of the least-contrast contacts for sufficiently small $ε$.
